commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix CohereASR FP16 attention bias dtype
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve CohereASR runtime FP16 relative-position bias buffers when loading FP32 checkpoint tensors. Fixes #54377; refreshed against main `c5f8adc0` after #55190.

## Claims

- Remove the loading-time buffer dtype override; keep the normal weight loader and shared attention-buffer references.
- Move the existing regression into `tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py`, as requested by @ekagra-ranjan, retaining upstream fusion and audio-token tests.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py -v` — **6 passed**.
- The migrated bias-loading regression fails against unmodified main production code (`float32` rather than `float16`) and passes with this fix.
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/cohere_asr.py tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py` — **passed**, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- No new Turing/H100 model or WER evaluation ran on this host: CUDA cannot initialize (driver 12.4; installed torch CUDA 13.0). Earlier H100 testing reported by the reviewer is prior-head evidence in this discussion, not a fresh result.

## Details

The custom `param.data.to(loaded_weight.dtype)` replaced the runtime FP16 buffer with an FP32 tensor before loading, overriding `--dtype` and leaving attention with mixed dtypes. The normal loader already casts checkpoint values into the existing destination dtype.

Duplicate check: re-read #54377 and searched open PRs by issue number and CohereASR/pos_bias; no competing open fix was found. #55190 is a merged attention optimization, whose tests are preserved. Current main still contains the offending conversion. This PR has been open since 2026-08-30.

AI assistance was used for this refresh and validation. Commits include Signed-off-by and OpenAI Codex attribution; human review of the updated diff and remaining hardware validation are still required.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Batch invariance: pin FlashInfer FP8 bmm and W4A16 NVFP4 kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, pins two GEMM paths so that a row's result does not depend on the batch:

- FlashInfer's FP8 `bmm` (`flashinfer_scaled_fp8_mm`) is pinned to the `cutlass` backend.
- W4A16 NVFP4 linears use the Humming kernel.

This was split from #62017 by @aoshen02. Without BI, behavior is unchanged.

## Changes

- `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`: `flashinfer_scaled_fp8_mm` passes `backend="cutlass"` to `bmm_fp8` under BI and `"auto"` otherwise. With FlashInfer autotune (on by default at `-O1` and above), `"auto"` tunes over cutlass, cuBLAS and cuDNN per M bucket, so different batch sizes can run different backends.
- `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`: under BI, a W4A16 NVFP4 linear selects `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel`, which already reads `use_batch_invariant` from `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`. Before this change, the BI branch forced the W4A4-only `CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel`, and kernel init raised `ValueError: CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel does not support W4A16`. With `--linear-backend` set to something other than Humming, a warning is logged and the setting is overridden.
- Tests:
  - `test_flashinfer_fp8_mm_batch_invariant_after_autotune` in `tests/v1/determinism/test_cutlass_batch_invariance.py` (SM100+);
  - `test_batch_invariant_w4a16_selects_humming` in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_kernel_selection.py` (CPU).

The router FP32-logits branch (with the `out_dtype` argument of `mm_batch_invariant`) and the two sm100 tuned M buckets for Nemotron-H shapes were moved out of this PR. They stay in #62017 for the Nemotron-H wiring.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 (SM100), vLLM nightly image `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7`, FlashInfer 0.7.2. The touched files are identical between that image and this PR's base `fa75d3456d`, so "base" is the image as shipped and "PR" is the image with this PR's two files overlaid.

**FP8 `bmm`.** Static per-tensor FP8 inputs. Each M slice `x[:M]` was compared bitwise against the first M rows of the M=2048 output, for M in {1, 2, 7, 16, 64, 128, 512, 2048}, on four (N, K) shapes. The table counts rows that differ.

| Backend | Autotune | 4096x4096 | 2688x4096 | 4608x2688 | 14336x4096 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` (base) | off | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `auto` (base) | on | M=128: 14, M=512: 50 | M=512: 21 | 0 | M=7: 2, M=64: 15, M=128: 30 |
| `cutlass` (PR) | off | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `cutlass` (PR) | on | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Max abs diff of the differing rows is 3e-5 to 6e-5. Without autotune, `"auto"` falls back to its first runner (cutlass), so it is invariant; the variance only appears after tuning. As a diagnostic, cuBLAS alone and cuDNN alone were each invariant after autotune on these shapes: the variance comes from switching backends between buckets. The new test failed in 1 of 2 runs at base (the tuner's pick is timing dependent) and passed in 2 of 2 runs with the PR.

**W4A16 NVFP4.** A synthetic `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4(use_a16=True)` layer, with the same M sweep, on shapes 4096x4096, 2688x4096 and 4608x2688.

| Code | BI | Kernel | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 1 | — | `ValueError: CutlassNvFp4LinearKernel does not support W4A16` at init |
| PR | 1 | `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel` | 0 rows differ at every M, outputs finite |
| base/PR | 0 | `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel` (unchanged) | 0 rows differ in this sweep (without autotune) |

So the W4A16 change fixes a crash at init under BI rather than a numerical difference.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_kernel_selection.py
# 4 passed; the new test fails at base with the ValueError above
pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_cutlass_batch_invariance.py -k test_flashinfer_fp8_mm_batch_invariant_after_autotune
# GB200: PR 2/2 passed; base 1/2 failed
```

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) passes on the changed files.

Not tested: end-to-end serving of an FP8 or W4A16 NVFP4 model under BI, and throughput. Humming and pinned `cutlass` are chosen for invariance, not speed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Flashinfer attention warmup deadlock under PP>1
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix a deadlock during Flashinfer attention warmup under PP>1.

## Claims

Fix a deadlock that occurs when one PP rank contains only Flashinfer attention groups while another PP rank contains a mix of Flashinfer and non-Flashinfer attention groups.

Most commonly affects models with dflash / dspark drafters on Blackwell, where Flashsinfer is often the default attention backend for the target model.

## Validation

Ran on B200:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16","num_speculative_tokens":2,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

On this PR, we get
```
INFO:     Started server process [771742]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

On main, we get stuck after
```
EngineCore pid=813035) INFO 10-28 17:46:40 [shm_broadcast.py:878] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work (e.g. compilation, weight/kv cache quantization).
(EngineCore pid=813035) INFO 10-28 17:47:40 [shm_broadcast.py:878] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work (e.g. compilation, weight/kv cache quantization).
```

`--enforce-eager` doesn't resolve this because Flashinfer attention warmup is run regardless of enforce eager and compilation mode.

`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` doesn't resolve this because it controls Flashinfer autotuning, not Flashinfer attention warmup.

```
pytest -v -s \
  tests/model_executor/test_attention_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py

99 passed, 2 warnings
```

## Details

During `kernel_warmup`, we may call `mixed_batch_attention_warmup` to run "a mixed prefill+decode batch to warm up both attention paths".

This is currently gated under "all attention groups use the Flashinfer backend" because hybrid attention backends may not support the dummy run.

With spec decode, the drafter may choose a different attention backend than the target model. Since the drafter is present on the last PP rank only, different ranks will disagree on whether they should participate in the Flashinfer warmup, causing deadlock.

The current fix synchronizes across PP ranks and only runs the Flashinfer attention warmup if all ranks agree. In effect, warmup behavior is consistent between PP=1 and PP>1.

Related:
- #60791 tracks issues with MiniMax-M3. Item 8 lists "PP where stages differ in running the M3 attention warmup". M3 warmup also uses `mixed_batch_attention_warmup` but it's separate from Flashinfer warmup.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][glm5next] Add SM121 TP=2 skinny-GEMM plans for GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash decode TPOT **-15% at concurrency 1 on 2x DGX Spark (SM121, TP=2)** by running the BF16 decode GEMMs on the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM instead of cuBLAS. On `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` the attention projections (KDA and MLA), shared experts and LM head stay BF16 and take roughly 46 of a 68 ms decode step on cuBLAS gemv. `glm5next` has no low-latency GEMM module yet, so this adds one modelled on `qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py` (#59753, #59632, #61437) with measured SM121 skinny-GEMM plans for the TP=2 local shapes, installed from `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextMTP`. Supersedes #62949.

## Claims

- 7 local `(N, K)` shapes at M = 1/2/4 (20 entries), routed only on capability `(12, 1)`; other GPUs, dtypes, token counts and shapes keep the standard linear path (cuBLAS).
- Kernel: skinny GEMM is 1.35x to 1.73x faster than cuBLAS gemv at M=1 (238-283 GB/s vs 162-176 GB/s), 1.04x to 1.36x at M=2/4.
- End to end, no speculation, concurrency 1: TPOT 64.0 -> 54.1 ms (-15%), 15.3 -> 18.0 tok/s. With MTP k=3 the decode step is one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1: ITL -3.6%, TPOT -2.7%, 26.7 -> 27.8 tok/s.
- GSM8K (n=100): 93 with cuBLAS, 94 with skinny GEMM.

## Validation

Kernel, cuBLAS (`F.linear`) vs skinny GEMM through the module path on GB10 (CUDA graph replay, weight rotated out of L2, nightly 8e2beaa3bf), cosine 1.000000 between the two outputs for every entry:

| shape (N, K) | layer | M | cuBLAS (us) | skinny GEMM (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (12576, 4096) | KDA in_proj | 1 | 608 | 429 | 1.42x |
|  |  | 2 | 453 | 425 | 1.07x |
|  |  | 4 | 450 | 429 | 1.05x |
| (4096, 4096) | KDA o_proj | 1 | 203 | 137 | 1.48x |
|  |  | 2 | 147 | 136 | 1.08x |
|  |  | 4 | 148 | 140 | 1.06x |
| (2048, 4096) | shared gate_up, MLA qkv_a | 1 | 103 | 64 | 1.61x |
|  |  | 2 | 78 | 64 | 1.22x |
|  |  | 4 | 79 | 63 | 1.24x |
| (4096, 1024) | shared down | 1 | 51 | 30 | 1.73x |
|  |  | 2 | 39 | 29 | 1.34x |
|  |  | 4 | 39 | 29 | 1.36x |
| (8192, 1536) | MLA q_b | 1 | 147 | 102 | 1.44x |
|  |  | 2 | 115 | 102 | 1.13x |
|  |  | 4 | 122 | 101 | 1.20x |
| (4096, 8192) | MLA o_proj | 1 | 291 | - | not included |
|  |  | 2 | 289 | 278 | 1.04x |
|  |  | 4 | 300 | 280 | 1.07x |
| (77440, 4096) | lm_head | 1 | 3606 | 2663 | 1.35x |
|  |  | 2 | 2789 | 2655 | 1.05x |
|  |  | 4 | 2741 | 2581 | 1.06x |

These are cold-L2 numbers, which is the serving case: decode reads each weight once per step and 45 layers do not fit the 24 MB L2. Weighted by how often each shape runs in a decode step, the entries save about 13 ms per step at M=1 and 3 ms at M=2 or M=4 in the probe; the server gains 10 ms at M=1 because the GEMMs interleave with MoE and attention. MLA o_proj at M=1 is not included: cuBLAS already streams this shape at 231 GB/s (162-176 GB/s on the other shapes), so the best skinny config from the sweep gained only 3% in the module path, under the 5% bar. M=8/16 are within 2% of cuBLAS and are not listed.

End to end, cuBLAS (current main) vs skinny GEMM (this PR): `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` TP=2 on two Sparks, FP8 KV, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, 8 requests at concurrency 1, greedy (`--temperature 0`), two interleaved runs per arm (each cell lists run 1 / run 2), nightly 8e2beaa3bf:

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | GSM8K (n=100) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 64.17 / 63.83 | 63.94 / 63.68 | 15.27 / 15.33 | 93 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 54.14 / 54.10 | 54.03 / 53.96 | 18.02 / 18.03 | 94 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | **-15.4%** | -15.4% | +17.8% | +1 |

With MTP k=3 (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8`, same nightly and sampling):

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 36.05 / 36.11 | 102.72 / 103.27 | 26.79 / 26.66 | 2.87 / 2.87 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 35.08 / 35.16 | 99.18 / 99.41 | 27.51 / 28.02 | 2.85 / 2.90 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | -2.7% | **-3.6%** | +3.9% | +0.2% |

With MTP the ITL is the decode step (one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1); TPOT and tok/s divide it by the tokens accepted per step. Under greedy decoding the acceptance length stays within 2.85-2.90 across the four runs, so the step gain carries over: TPOT -2.7%, tok/s +3.9%. An earlier 4-request run at model-default sampling gave -12% without speculation (the number in the commit message); with MTP its acceptance length swung 3% between repeats, which hid the step gain.

An nsys census of the skinny GEMM arm shows every listed shape on `CuteSkinnyGemm` in the server (45% of GPU time without speculation, 39.5% with MTP); what is left on cuBLAS is KDA `f_b`/`g_b` (4096, 128) (#57617), the fp32-output router gate (288, 4096) and MLA o_proj at M=1.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next`, 26 passed on GB10 (table validity, capability routing, hook installation, 20 selected shapes with cosine > 0.999 against `F.linear`). The selected-shape test skips off capability (12, 1), which CI does not have.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# on each DGX Spark, --node-rank 0 / 1
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \
  --master-addr 192.168.100.1 --master-port 29500 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.84 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --reasoning-parser glm45 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
# MTP k=3 arm: add --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
#   and use --gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8
# SPEED_BENCH_DIR holds throughput_2k.jsonl, built from nvidia/SPEED-Bench with NeMo-Skills prepare.py
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path $SPEED_BENCH_DIR --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_2k \
  --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 2 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 0
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next
```

</details>

## Details

- Plans come from a CUDA-graph sweep over block_size, outputs_per_block, k_unroll, vector_width and static_k with the weight rotated out of L2, keeping entries that beat cuBLAS by more than 5%. `(2048, 4096)` serves both the shared-expert gate/up and the MLA fused q_a/kv_a projection.
- The replacement method follows the quant method the layer carries: a quant config that excludes `lm_head` gives `ParallelLMHead` an `UnquantizedLinearMethod` rather than an `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, and the head stayed on cuBLAS until this was handled.
- Not covered: TP=1 (the model does not fit one Spark), KDA `f_b`/`g_b` `(4096, 128)` (#57617), MTP `eh_proj` (a plain `nn.Linear`), and M=3, which uses cuBLAS.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the sweep scripts, the module and the tests; all code and measurements were reviewed and run by the author.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] draft_lm_head_quantization for DSpark drafters
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This lets the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DSpark drafters use `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#59973), which so far was limited to EAGLE and MTP. A drafter that shares the target `lm_head` then computes its base logits through a private FP8 or NVFP4 copy of that head, while the target keeps verifying with its own BF16 head. It is the vLLM counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#39622.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --speculative-config \
  '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"}'
```

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, AgentX, `"fp8"`: ITL P50 is 4.0% lower at TP2 c1 and 2.4% lower at TP4 c1. A trace shows the draft-head GEMM going from 348 µs to 60 µs per step. From c8 up the result is neutral within noise.
- Acceptance length and GSM8K are unchanged within run-to-run noise, because the target still verifies with its own head.
- No new mechanism: the sharing logic EAGLE and DSpark had in common is now one helper, `share_target_lm_head`, and DSpark opts in through `DSparkSpeculatorConfig.supported_options`. Off by default.

## Validation

All runs: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03` (the same vLLM commit as this PR's base) with the changed files mounted, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, InferenceX recipe `dsv41flash/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml` (DSpark k=5, probabilistic drafting, `--monokernel`). The only difference between arms is `"draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"`.

**AgentX** (InferenceX `infx.bench agentic`, golden synthetic AL 3.51, 900 s, fresh server per point, one run per point). ITL P50 in ms, BF16 head -> FP8 head:

| | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 | 1.89 -> 1.81 (**-4.0%**) | 1.90 -> 1.81 (-4.9%) | 1.95 -> 1.86 (-4.5%) | 2.26 -> 2.24 (-0.7%) | 3.13 -> 3.11 (-0.5%) | 4.67 -> 4.69 (+0.4%) | 9.42 -> 9.35 (-0.8%) |
| TP4 | 1.56 -> 1.52 (**-2.4%**) | 1.57 -> 1.52 (-2.9%) | | | | | |

The c1 numbers match the trace below. At c2 and c4 the trace accounts for only about 0.5% (44 µs per step at c4), so most of the improvement measured at those points is run-to-run variance.

**Draft-head kernel per decode step** (torch profiler, TP2, rank 0, 60 steps). The draft-head GEMM is swapped one for one, and the target verify head (`Cijk_..._BBS`, about 104 µs) is untouched:

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| c1 (M=5) | `wvSplitK_hf_sml` 347.8 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 54.6 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |
| c4 (M=20) | `Cijk_..._BBS` 104.5 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 55.8 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |

**Acceptance and accuracy** (TP2, `rejection_sample_method: block`):

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| AL, AgentX traces at c8 (from `vllm:spec_decode_*` counter deltas, about 112k drafts each) | 3.416 | 3.400 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319, greedy, 2 runs | 0.909 / 0.913 | 0.904 / 0.914 |

**Tests** (MI355X, rebased branch): `pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py`: 54 passed, 4 skipped (the NVFP4 cases, which are CUDA-only). `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization`, which exercises the refactored EAGLE/MTP path with `"fp8"`: passed. `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main`, including mypy: passed.

<details>
<summary>Full AgentX table, draft-head microbenchmark, run notes</summary>

| TP | conc | ITL mean/P50/P90 (ms) | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | 1.99/1.89/2.27 -> 1.92/1.81/2.26 | 78.6 -> 80.4 | 247 -> 242 |
| 2 | 2 | 2.02/1.90/2.30 -> 1.93/1.81/2.27 | 109.7 -> 109.2 | 249 -> 252 |
| 2 | 4 | 2.28/1.95/2.97 -> 2.11/1.86/2.41 | 137.6 -> 143.8 | 152 -> 140 |
| 2 | 8 | 2.50/2.26/3.64 -> 2.49/2.24/3.47 | 215.6 -> 212.9 | 140 -> 148 |
| 2 | 16 | 3.12/3.13/3.78 -> 3.17/3.11/3.78 | 336.3 -> 336.6 | 2030 -> 1999 |
| 2 | 32 | 5.03/4.67/6.02 -> 5.25/4.69/5.89 | 659.8 -> 661.8 | 6485 -> 6527 |
| 2 | 64 | 10.25/9.42/14.29 -> 10.05/9.35/14.19 | 1120.4 -> 1134.2 | 315 -> 321 |
| 4 | 1 | 1.61/1.56/1.80 -> 1.58/1.52/1.80 | 44.7 -> 44.9 | 189 -> 193 |
| 4 | 2 | 1.62/1.57/1.80 -> 1.60/1.52/1.81 | 56.6 -> 59.3 | 191 -> 207 |

At each TP2 point both arms ran at the same time on GPU pairs {2,3} and {4,5}, swapping pairs every point. The TP4 points ran one arm at a time on the same four GPUs. AgentX replays paced traces, so at low concurrency the arms serve different request mixes and token throughput follows that mix. ITL is the speed metric.

Draft-head GEMM alone (`ParallelLMHead` against `quantized_lm_head_copy`, CUDA-graph replay), in µs:

```
TP2 64640 x 5120   M=5    M=10   M=20   M=40   M=80   M=160  M=320
BF16               352.4  96.7   99.4   101.4  107.0  124.2  185.0
FP8                57.0   56.7   57.2   59.0   63.3   71.4   171.6
TP4 32320 x 5120
BF16               183.9  60.5   55.5   59.9   71.7   73.8   136.9
FP8                33.7   33.7   32.3   38.3   38.2   49.2   63.2
```

</details>

## Details

- **Changes**:
  - `share_target_lm_head` in `eagle/utils.py`, next to `_should_share`, installs the target head or its quantized copy, raises if quantization was requested but the drafter keeps its own head, and returns the installed head. `load_eagle_model` uses the returned head for the MTP `shared_head` fixup. `load_dspark_model` passes its vocab-size check as `can_share`. `load_dflash_model` can adopt it with `quantization=None` in a follow-up.
  - `DSparkSpeculatorConfig` accepts `draft_lm_head_quantization` only for `DSparkDraftModel` and `DSparkV41DraftModel`. Other DSpark drafters may read `lm_head.weight` directly: Muse Spark casts its activations to the head's dtype, which would be FP8 for a quantized copy. They are rejected during config validation, before the target loads. EAGLE's `head_dtype` check is shared through `check_draft_lm_head_quantization`.
  - Weight reload and weight transfer already refresh the copy, because `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` and `share_source_lm_heads` run on any `DraftModelSpeculator`.
- **Not a duplicate of #47584**: that PR adds a separate env var (`VLLM_DSPARK_FP8_DRAFT_HEAD`) and a new rowwise FP8 module, for the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4 DSpark path only. This PR reuses the existing `draft_lm_head_quantization` config and kernel selection, so it works on any platform with an FP8 linear kernel.
- **Kernel on ROCm**: `"fp8"` resolves to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` (hipBLASLt FP8 `_scaled_mm`).
- **Why c1 benefits most**: at M=5 (one request, five drafts) the BF16 dispatch picks `wvSplitK`, which is about 3.5x slower than at M=10. `deepseek_v41/amd/ops/draft_lm_head.py` already pads around that, but only on gfx942. A lossless fix to that dispatch is a separate follow-up.
- **Memory**: one extra FP8 copy of the per-rank head shard, about 0.33 GB at TP2 and 0.17 GB at TP4 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. It is created during model loading, so KV sizing accounts for it.
- **CI coverage**: the quantized copy and its refresh are covered by the existing `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py`. The shared EAGLE/MTP path is covered by the MTP e2e test above. The DSpark path is validated end to end above. CI has no DSpark checkpoint test for it. `"nvfp4"` takes the same path but was not measured here.

commits.pr_title: [MORI] Add MORI EP V2 support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `--all2all-backend mori`, an expert-parallel all2all backend that runs MoRI EPv2 (`mori.ops.dispatch_combine_v2`) where it is supported and MoRI EPv1 otherwise. EPv2 dispatches and combines tokens through a MoRI CCO symmetric-memory window, so all EP ranks must sit in one load/store-accessible (LSA) team, e.g. one node.

`VLLM_MORI_EP_V2` selects the version. When it is unset, `mori` prefers EPv2 and falls back to EPv1 with a warning in any of these cases:

- the EP size exceeds 8 (except on gfx1250, whose UALink team can span hosts);
- `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1` is set (except on gfx1250);
- `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` is used;
- the model is not BF16.

Setting it to `1` forces EPv2, and `0` selects EPv1. The choice is made once in the ROCm platform's config hook. On EPv1 across nodes, `mori` uses InterNodeV1LL when the per-rank token budget is at most `VLLM_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256), and InterNodeV1 otherwise.

The existing MoRI backends (`mori_high_throughput`, `mori_low_latency`) are unchanged and always run EPv1. `docs/serving/expert_parallel_deployment.md` explains how to choose among them.

The MoRI EPv1 flag `use_mori_kernels` is renamed to `use_mori_epv1_kernels`, next to `use_mori_epv2_kernels`. This touches its existing users in `rocm_aiter_moe.py`, `deepseek_v32` and the MiniMax-M3 test.

No other open PR adds a MoRI EPv2 backend.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4-Pro with DP8+EP8 on 8× MI355X, `mori` on EPv2 matches TP8 and the existing MoRI EP backend on GSM8K.
- Under the InferenceX MI355X serving recipe (8k/1k), `mori` on EPv2 gives about 13% more output throughput and about 11% lower TPOT than `mori_high_throughput`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 8× MI355X, `--moe-backend aiter`, CUDA graphs, MoRI main.

**Accuracy**

| Backend | Parallelism | GSM8K (lm-eval, 1319 q, 5-shot, strict) |
|---|---|---|
| default | TP8 | 0.950 |
| `mori_high_throughput` | DP8+EP8 | 0.958 |
| `mori` (EPv2) | DP8+EP8 | 0.955 |

GSM8K ran with 4096 max new tokens, so about 33 answers per backend were cut off before the final answer. The absolute scores are lower than with a longer budget, but the backends can be compared with each other.

**Throughput.** InferenceX vLLM MI355X recipe: DP8+EP8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, prefix caching, DSpark speculative decoding (6 tokens), and model runner V2. The load is random input/output of 8k/1k, with 640 requests at concurrency 64 and 1280 requests at concurrency 128. Both runs used the same image, on an earlier revision of this branch where the backend was still named `mori_epv2`.

| Backend | c64 output tok/s (TPOT ms) | c128 output tok/s (TPOT ms) | GSM8K (200 q) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mori_high_throughput` | 1835 (30.3) | 2339 (47.0) | 0.965 |
| `mori` (EPv2) | 2073 (26.9) | 2644 (41.8) | 0.960 |

The eager mode (`--enforce-eager`) start-up also passed. Unit tests: `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_epv2_prepare_finalize.py`.

## Follow-ups

- Make mori the single MoRI backend: fold mori_high_throughput and mori_low_latency into it (deprecate first, then remove). VLLM_MORI_EP_V2 stays as the EPv2/EPv1 override.
- Add EPv2 across nodes (RDMA), so multi-node EP no longer falls back to EPv1.
- Use quantized (FP8/FP4) dispatch on EPv2. MoRI supports it, but this backend does not use it yet.

AI assistance (Claude, Codex) was used to write and review this change. The submitter reviewed the changes and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct weight reload: write checkpoint tensors into the live model
[Model] Add NVIDIA Canary (nvidia/canary-1b-v2) speech-to-text support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `CanaryForConditionalGeneration` for [`nvidia/canary-1b-v2`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/canary-1b-v2) (FastConformer encoder + Transformer decoder; 25 European languages, ASR + X↔En speech translation). It targets the native Transformers checkpoint layout (`model_type: canary`, available since Transformers 5.16, which vLLM already pins), so no `.nemo` conversion or `trust_remote_code` is needed.

A user asked on the vLLM Slack whether `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` could work. No existing issue or PR: `gh pr list --search canary` / `gh issue list --search canary` only return unrelated NIXL "import canary" CI items.

The decoder is built from vLLM layers; the FastConformer encoder reuses the Transformers module, as `parakeet.py` already does (see Details).

## Claims

- `nvidia/canary-1b-v2` loads and serves via `LLM` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` + `/v1/audio/translations` (source language from `language`, target from `to_language`, default `en` for translations).
- Greedy output is token-identical to Transformers `CanaryForConditionalGeneration.generate` on the clips below (fp32 and bf16, batched).
- WER on the existing `test_wer_correctness` earnings22 slice: 12.34 (vLLM, bf16, CPU) and 12.336 (vLLM, bf16, L40 GPU, unmodified test) vs 12.46 (Transformers, fp32); 12.34 is added as the expected value for `nvidia/canary-1b-v2`.

## Validation

The runs below are on an Apple M5 Pro (vLLM CPU backend, `--enforce-eager`, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=2`). GPU results are in the next section.

**Token parity vs Transformers** (3 prompts in one `llm.generate` batch, greedy, `max_tokens=128`):

| clip | task | fp32 | bf16 | output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en (6 s, TTS) | en→en | match | match | `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Speech recognition on VLLM is now working.` |
| de (5 s, TTS) | de→de | match | match | `Guten Morgen, heute ist das Wetter sehr schön und wir gehen in den Park.` |
| de (5 s, TTS) | de→en | match | match | `Good morning, today is the weather very nice and we go into the park.` |

**WER** (`D4nt3/esb-datasets-earnings22-validation-tiny-filtered`, 511 clips, Whisper `EnglishTextNormalizer`, same code path as `test_wer_correctness`):

| implementation | dtype | WER |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transformers `generate` (greedy) | fp32 | 12.46 |
| vLLM (this PR), `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | bf16 | 12.34 |

The vLLM number came from calling the test's `run_evaluation` with `max_concurrent_reqs=8`; the unmodified test sends all 511 requests at once, which times out on CPU. The expected value was measured with bf16 on CPU; the test allows up to 12.56. On GPU the unmodified test passes with 12.336 (see below).

**Server checks** (`vllm serve nvidia/canary-1b-v2`):
- 67 s clip → chunked by the STT chunker (40 s limit) and transcribed correctly.
- 8 concurrent requests → identical outputs.
- `language=ja` → HTTP 400 with the supported-language list (see Details).

**Tests**

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_canary.py                     # 6 passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k canary  # 3 passed
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k Canary                      # passed
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                              # passed
```

`tests/models/test_initialization.py -k Canary` segfaults on macOS in the forked child (Whisper and Cohere ASR fail the same way there); on Linux it passes (below).

**GPU (single NVIDIA L40, Linux)**

- `test_wer_correctness[...-model_config2]` unmodified, all 511 requests at once: WER **12.336**, passed.
- `test_canary.py` (6), Canary's `processing/test_common.py` cases (3), `test_registry_imports[CanaryForConditionalGeneration]` and `test_can_initialize_large_subset[CanaryForConditionalGeneration]` pass.
- End-to-end through `vllm serve`: with `--dtype float32` the output text is identical to Transformers greedy on all 14 en/de transcription and de→en/en→de translation cases (in bf16, 2 near-tie cases differ by a word; see the linked comment). Long audio (79 s / 135 s) is chunked correctly, German WER is 8.0% on 4 MLS clips, `ja` returns 400, streaming matches non-streaming, and 16 concurrent requests match sequential ones. Details: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64215#issuecomment-6472494788
- CUDA graphs work. Throughput vs `whisper-large-v3` with `vllm bench serve` on the earnings22 slice: 43.8 vs 17.3 req/s at concurrency 32 and 59.1 vs 17.1 at 128. Details: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64215#issuecomment-6472054652

## Details

- **Decoder** is native vLLM: reuses `CohereASRAttention` / `CohereASRCrossAttention` / `CohereASRMLP` from `cohere_asr.py` (Transformers' Canary is itself a subclass of its Cohere ASR model). Differences from Cohere ASR: `[sin | cos]` positional table (vs interleaved), no encoder→decoder projection, `proj_out` with bias. Weight renames are decoder-scoped regexes in `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- **Encoder** currently reuses Transformers' `ParakeetEncoder` as-is, the same way `parakeet.py` does for Nano Nemotron VL. Checkpoint names match 1:1, so correctness comes from the reference implementation. I'm keeping it this way in this PR: no ASR encoder in vLLM uses tensor-parallel layers yet (`cohere_asr.ConformerEncoder` also uses plain `nn.Linear`), so swapping in the Cohere ASR encoder would remove duplicated code without a TP or kernel benefit, and the model fits on one GPU. Sharing `cohere_asr.ConformerEncoder`, which needs a config adapter because it reads NeMo-style config dicts, could be a follow-up if reviewers prefer.
- **Processor**: `CanaryProcessor` renames `input_ids` → `decoder_input_ids`, so `_call_hf_processor` calls `ParakeetFeatureExtractor` and the tokenizer directly. Features are extracted per clip and passed with `feature_lengths`; the encoder mask is rebuilt after padding.
- **Prompt**: the same control-token sequence as the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja` (`<|startofcontext|><|startoftranscript|><|emo:undefined|><|src|><|tgt|><|pnc|><|noitn|><|notimestamp|><|nodiarize|>`).
- **Languages**: `validate_language` rejects languages outside the 25 trained ones instead of the base class's warn-and-continue, because the prompt needs a trained language token; with `ja` the model silently returned empty text.
- **Limitations / TODO**: `max_audio_clip_s=40` is my choice for vLLM's chunker (NeMo uses its own dynamic chunking for long-form); no timestamps/ITN/diarization control tokens exposed yet (always `noitn/notimestamp/nodiarize`, punctuation on); TP not tested.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Pair KV regions by layer for every transfer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

NIXL pairs a peer's KV regions with the local ones in several ways, depending on the transfer:

- **By index**, for PP=1 peers: region *i* there is region *i* here, and the region group lists must match. Otherwise only pure MLA models transfer, through region-mapped reads.
- **By a PP window**, for pull from a PP stage: a slice `[offset : offset + num_local_regions]` of the peer's regions (`_remote_region_offset`).
- **By layer name**, for push from a PP stage under HMA or packed caches: `_align_remote_regions_by_layer` rewrites the peer's metadata into one region per local layer. `_compute_desc_ids` then routes blocks through `_transfer_layer_group_ids`.
- **By packed-row splitting**, when only the peer packs its rows: `_split_remote_packed_rows`, which refuses multi-group rows.

`_compute_desc_ids` has a separate mode for each: flattening, group mapping (with its handling of shared `-1` regions) and layer routing.

This PR replaces all of them with one rule: **every transfer pairs regions through the layers both sides hold.**

- Every worker advertises the layers of each of its regions (`region_members`) and the cache group of each layer (`layer_group_ids`), not only push PP stages under HMA.
- On the handshake, `_pair_regions` looks each layer up on both sides and records one pair (peer region, local region, cache group) per layer, deduplicated. A layer registered as two regions (K and V apart) pairs them in order. A region shared by several groups pairs once per group it holds a layer of. So which layers share a region no longer has to match between P and D, nor between a PP stage and the decoder.
- Group numbers are compared per layer, so a mismatch is caught even inside a region shared by several groups (group `-1`), where a per-region check cannot see it. Group ids are deterministic for a given model and config (PP stages group the whole model), so this guards against P and D having different plans, e.g. when KV page sizes unify at one TP size but not the other and the sliding-window layers fall back to full attention.
- Mamba/SSM hybrids pair the same way: attention pages and SSM sub-regions (conv sub-projections, SSM state, CSA-linear PLE page) are read from the peer region their layer pairs with. A hybrid peer with a different cache-group plan is refused at the handshake. PP stages stay refused for hybrids (not validated).
- Descriptor lists stay one per region on both sides. A peer's list keeps only its regions that pair (`_select_remote_regions`). A transfer reads or writes each pair at its group's blocks, which is the only mode of `_compute_desc_ids` for attention: `pairs=(regions, keys)`.
- When only the peer packs its rows, `_expand_remote_packed_rows` first views each row as one region per layer. That also covers rows holding layers of several groups, which `_split_remote_packed_rows` refused.
- Each pairing is kept per engine (`_dst_pairs`), and every TP rank of one engine must pair the same way.
- Refused at the handshake:
  - a peer that advertises no layers;
  - a peer missing a local layer;
  - a PP=1 peer holding layers this worker does not;
  - a layer split into a different number of regions on the two sides;
  - region metadata of different lengths;
  - a Mamba/SSM hybrid peer with any layer in another cache group.
- A non-hybrid layer in different cache groups on P and D still falls back to region-mapped reads for pull (MLA only), and is refused otherwise.
- `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` 15 → 16. A peer without `region_members` fails the compatibility hash instead of pairing by index.

Removed: `_remote_region_offset`, `_align_remote_regions_by_layer`, `_split_remote_packed_rows`, `_requires_layer_name_routing`, `_tracks_region_layers`, the `_transfer_layer_*` tuples, `_uses_region_group_mapping`, `dst_uses_region_group_mapping` and `_check_mamba_pairs`.

The pull guard for PP + HMA stays. This PR changes how regions pair, not which topologies are allowed.

### Related PRs

None of these replaces how regions pair; this PR does not duplicate them.

- #53360 adds `region_members` to the pull path for PP producers, including hybrid Mamba. It pairs each stage region with one local region, by the region's first layer, and copies every member group's blocks between those two regions. With layers of several groups sharing a region, that copies one group's KV into another group's pages. Pairing by layer, as here, avoids that.
- #56187 extends push's layer-name routing to Mamba/SSM. This PR replaces that routing, so the two conflict; Mamba pairs through the same layer pairs here instead.
- #57662 changes how regions are deduplicated at registration (by base address and block length). That is orthogonal to pairing, but both PRs touch `register_kv_caches`.
- #60113 adds support for different cache-group plans on P and D; this PR only detects them.

## Test Plan

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Changed tests:

- **`test_nixl_push_connector.py`**:
  - The layer-alignment tests are now `_pair_regions` tests: pooled regions kept once, a PP stage keeping the decoder's regions of its layers, split layers, packed rows next to unpacked regions, and each refusal above.
  - The PP-window test now selects regions by layer.
  - The region-groups test now checks `groups_match`; a new test has the peer treat a sliding-window layer of a shared region as full attention.
- **`test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`**: packed rows advertise `region_members` and expand through `_expand_remote_packed_rows`. The asymmetric packed PP test computes descriptor ids from the stored pairs. New MLA + KDA hybrid test: a peer putting a KDA layer in another cache group is refused.
- **`test_nixl_connector_hma.py`**: the descriptor-id tests pass `pairs`.
- **`test_nixl_connector.py`**: the fake handshake advertises `region_members`.

## Test Result

- **Unit suites:** the failing set is identical to `main` on the same machine (CPU only), test for test:
  - 145 need a GPU;
  - 113 need NCCL;
  - one needs a gated HF repo, one Ray, one a newer `humming`.
- **`pre-commit`:** all hooks passed, including mypy.

### Real model KV layouts (simulation)

Each model's real per-layer KV plan, built with vLLM's own planner and allocator (model on the `meta` device, `load_format=dummy`, no weights). Real NIXL workers (P and D) register those caches; D handshakes with P and reads one request (pull), or P writes it (push); every recorded descriptor pair is executed as a memory copy, then every D page is compared byte for byte with tagged data written into P, and all of D's other bytes must stay zero.

TP and PP ranks are simulated in one process. Each P and D rank builds its own KV plan and caches at its TP/PP rank (a PP engine groups the layers of all its stages, as the engine core does), and D (pull) or each P rank/stage (push) handshakes with every peer rank. Attention split across TP ranks is compared per KV head, by global head index (heads replicated when TP > KV heads); MLA pages are compared whole; TP-split SSM state is compared row by row with the P rank and position holding it, each concatenated projection split on its own (Kimi-Linear conv `[q | k | v]`, Qwen3-Next conv `[q | k | v]` with key and value sizes, Nemotron conv `[x | B | C]`; recurrent and SSM state split by head). Pages are paired by token position when P and D have different logical block sizes (Kimi-Linear: 1920 vs 1024 tokens at TP1 vs TP2). Swapping two descriptors, or swapping D's q and k conv rows after the transfer, fails the check.

- **GPU**: one GB300, real GPU attention backends.
- **CPU**: CPU attention backend, block sizes 128, or 1152/1408 after Mamba alignment. FP8 checkpoints (MiMo-V2-Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Kimi-K2, MiniMax-M2, GLM-4.5-Air) are built without their quantization config, which has no CPU kernel and does not change the KV plan. Descriptor counts are from the first CPU run (TP1, same).

TP mismatch: P TP1 → D TP2 and P TP2 → D TP1. PP: P PP2 → D TP1 and D TP2. Numbers are descriptor counts.

| Model | KV plan (groups → regions) | Sim | pull: same | pull: TP mismatch | push: same | push: TP mismatch | push: PP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | 61 sparse MLA + 61 indexer, 1 group → 122 | GPU | ✅ 366 | ✅ 732 / ✅ 366 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 20 KDA + 7 MLA, 4 groups → 7 shared | GPU | ✅ 710 | ✅ 832 / ✅ 496 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | refused (Mamba PP) |
| gpt-oss-20b | 12 sliding window + 12 full, 2 groups → 12 shared | GPU, CPU | ✅ 72 (CPU: 48) | ✅ 144 / ✅ 144 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / refused (HMA push, D TP > P TP) |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | 27 MLA, 1 group | GPU | ✅ 81 | ✅ 162 / ✅ 81 | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | 36 GDN + 12 full, 4 groups → 12 shared | CPU | ✅ 168 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | refused (Mamba PP) |
| NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 | 27 Mamba2 + 4 full, 8 groups → 4 shared | CPU | ✅ 116 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | refused (Mamba PP) |
| Gemma 3 1B (1 KV head) | 22 sliding window + 4 full, 7 groups → 4 shared | CPU | ✅ 52 | ✅ / refused (replicated KV) | ✅ | ✅ / refused (replicated KV) | ✅ / refused (HMA push, D TP > P TP) |
| MiMo-V2-Flash | 39 sliding window + 9 full, 6 groups → 9 shared | CPU | ✅ 96 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / refused (HMA push, D TP > P TP) |
| DeepSeek-V3 / Kimi-K2 | 61 MLA, 1 group | CPU | ✅ 122 | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |
| Qwen3-8B / MiniMax-M2 / GLM-4.5-Air | 36 / 62 / 46 full, 1 group | CPU | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ | ✅ / ✅ | ✅ / ✅ |

Every refusal is a documented guard. "Replicated KV": with fewer KV heads than TP ranks, a non-MLA, non-Mamba transfer is refused when the side issuing it (D for pull, P for push) has the lower TP (`_validate_remote_agent_handshake`, unchanged by this PR). Kimi-Linear (as any Mamba hybrid over NIXL) needs `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`. MiniMax-M1 is not covered: `MiniMaxM1ForCausalLM` (and `MiniMaxText01ForCausalLM`) were removed from vLLM in v0.23.

DeepSeek-V3 also passes with block-major MLA on both sides (`BLNHC`, the whole block row is one region), and with P on `BLNHC` and D on `LBNHC`, where D expands P's packed row into one region per layer (`_expand_remote_packed_rows`).

Compared with older code on the same layouts:
- `main` (merge base 4541fcdd8), GPU rows plus Gemma 3 1B and MiMo-V2-Flash PP push (CPU): same results and identical descriptor counts. Main pairs PP stages by layer name in push (`_align_remote_regions_by_layer`), which this PR replaces with the one pairing rule.
- This branch before the Mamba pairing commits (`90ec0cb5c`), CPU rows: identical descriptor ids (same digests on Qwen3-Next, Nemotron, gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V3).
- `main` before this PR, DeepSeek-V3 with P on `BLNHC` and D on `LBNHC`: identical descriptor ids. The old `_split_remote_packed_rows` and the new expansion make the same reads.

Different cache-group plans on P and D are covered by the unit tests only.

### End-to-end P/D

gpt-oss-20b, pull, P TP1 → D TP2 on one GB300 node: GSM8K 5-shot (completions) flexible-extract 0.364 through the P/D proxy vs 0.362 on a single instance without P/D; 1320 requests, 2640 NIXL reads, no failed transfers or notifications.

Found along the way, independent of this PR (also before it): Qwen3-Next and Nemotron with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` read wrong bytes and write outside the request's blocks even with identical P and D. The likely cause is that Mamba registration in `register_kv_caches` uses `block_stride = physical_page_size`, which only holds for layer-major layouts. Auto layout picks `LBHNC` for these models, so it needs the layout forced. To be fixed or refused separately.

- **Not run yet:**
  - model evals for the other topologies above (the simulation checks the bytes of each block directly);
  - pull from PP stages, which is still refused under HMA.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. The submitter reviews every changed line before marking it ready.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][gRPC] Drain in-flight RPCs and engine work within --shutdown-timeout
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `vllm serve --grpc` ignores `--shutdown-timeout`. On SIGTERM it cancels in-flight RPCs after a hardcoded 5 s (`server.stop(grace=5.0)`). It then calls `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` without a timeout, so EngineCore gets the default 5 s join before SIGKILL. This PR spends the `--shutdown-timeout` budget instead: in-flight requests finish, then EngineCore drains work that outlives an RPC, such as NIXL prefill blocks that the decode side has not read yet, until the same deadline plus a 5 s teardown floor. Related: #61562 (drain order for the multi-API-server HTTP path), #41383 (NIXL KV cache lease), #55102 (previous fix to this launcher). ## Claims With `--shutdown-timeout N > 0`: - SIGTERM makes the gRPC server refuse new RPCs at once (`UNAVAILABLE`). In-flight RPCs run to completion for up to N s, and never less than the 5 s they get with the default `0`, so setting a timeout is never less graceful than not setting one. Today they are cancelled after 5 s with `UNAVAILABLE: Cancelling all calls`. - EngineCore keeps serving until no RPC that could still send it a request is in flight and AsyncLLM has no request left. RPCs are counted from the moment the server dispatches them, so a request that reached the server before SIGTERM is served even if it is still arriving, being preprocessed or queued in EngineCore. EngineCore then drains what outlives an RPC until N s plus a 5 s teardown floor. A prefill instance in a NIXL P/D deployment keeps the blocks it has handed off until the decode instance reads them. Today it is SIGKILLed about 5 s after SIGTERM, and the decode request fails under the default `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"`. - RPCs still running at the deadline (`max(N, 5 s)`) are cancelled, and their requests are aborted while EngineCore is still running. - An RPC that carries no request, such as a router's `SubscribeKvEvents` stream, does not hold shutdown: it is cancelled 5 s after EngineCore stops. - A second SIGTERM or SIGINT cancels all RPCs at once. - The process exits within `max(N, 5 s) + 5 s`, plus the time to kill what is left. - `--shutdown-timeout 0` (the default) keeps the current behavior. `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` now runs off the event loop there too. ## Validation **Setup** - Image: upstream nightly `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8e2beaa3bff595577a069d49d96bde9074294ec2` (vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev197+g8e2beaa3b`). Its `grpc_server.py` is byte-identical to this PR's base. - Extras: `smg-grpc-servicer==0.14.0` for the `grpc` extra. - Model and hardware: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, with prefill and decode on two B300 GPUs of one node. - KV transfer: `NixlConnector` (`kv_role=kv_both`). - Flags: `--enforce-eager --shutdown-timeout 60` unless a row says otherwise. - Columns: `main` is the image as is. "First revision" is this PR as first pushed (RPCs drain first, then EngineCore gets what is left of the budget). "Overlapped" is the variant suggested in review: EngineCore is signalled at SIGTERM, concurrently with the RPC drain. "This PR" is the current head. Each column mounts its `grpc_server.py` over the image's copy and starts fresh servers for each row. - The `SubscribeKvEvents` row starts both servers with `--kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:"}'`. The in-flight row starts the prefill server with `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072`. The preprocessing row runs a single `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` server (no KV transfer) with `SMG_VLLM_MM_PROCESSOR=inprocess`; the client serves the request's image from a local HTTP server that answers after 1.5 s. | Scenario | `main` | First revision | Overlapped | This PR | |---|---|---|---|---| | Control: prefill → decode handoff, no SIGTERM | 32/32 tokens, `length` | 32/32 | 32/32 | 32/32 | | NIXL handoff: SIGTERM prefill once its RPC returns, send the decode leg 8 s later | decode `finish_reason=error`, 0/32; prefill exits +6.9 s | 32/32; prefill exits +12.3 s | 32/32; +13.6 s | **32/32; prefill exits +11.9 s, after the read** | | 4000-token stream on the decode server, SIGTERM after the first tokens | cut at +5.0 s with `UNAVAILABLE: Cancelling all calls`, 419/4000; server exits +11.9 s | 4000/4000; +51.2 s | 4000/4000; +54.7 s | **4000/4000 (stream ends +48.0 s); server exits +52.0 s** | | A `SubscribeKvEvents` stream open on the SIGTERMed server, in the handoff case and in a 1000-token stream | | streams held to +60.0 s, then EngineCore SIGKILLed with 0 s left (`MPClient: start timeout=0.0s`); prefill exits +62.4 s, decode +62.3 s | subscription cancelled at +17.0 s / +21.5 s; prefill exits +18.3 s, decode +22.9 s | **subscription cancelled at +15.9 s / +20.9 s, 5 s after EngineCore stopped; prefill exits +17.1 s, decode +22.0 s** | | Prefills in flight at SIGTERM: 17 prompts of 7680 tokens fill one 131072-token step, 15 more follow 0.1 s later, SIGTERM at 0.15 s, decode legs 3 s after the prefills return | | 32/32 decoded | **15 prefills return `finish_reason=abort`, 17/32 decoded** | **32/32 decoded** | | Stream longer than the budget: `--shutdown-timeout 20`, 7000-token stream | | cancelled at +20.0 s, then EngineCore SIGKILLed with 0 s left; exits +22.2 s | cancelled at +20.0 s; EngineCore tears down; exits +24.6 s | **cancelled at +20.0 s; EngineCore gets the 5 s floor and tears down within it; exits +24.8 s** | | Second SIGTERM: on prefill 2 s after the first (decode leg at +8 s); on decode 5 s into a 7000-token stream | | | decode leg 32/32, prefill exits +12.4 s; stream cancelled at +5.0 s, exits +10.3 s | **decode leg 32/32, prefill exits +12.0 s; stream cancelled at +5.0 s, exits +8.8 s** | | `--shutdown-timeout 0` | ignored: same as the rows above | handoff `error`, prefill exits +6.9 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (426/4000), exits +8.7 s | handoff `error`, +7.2 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (396/4000), exits +10.3 s | **handoff `error`, prefill exits +7.0 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (428/4000), exits +10.2 s** | | `--shutdown-timeout 2`, below the 5 s default grace: NIXL handoff as above, 4000-token stream | | | | **decode leg 32/32, prefill exits +11.7 s; stream cut at +5.0 s (413/4000), as with `0`; exits +8.8 s** | | A request still being preprocessed at SIGTERM: its image fetch takes 1.5 s, and it was sent 50 ms before SIGTERM | | | | **32/32, done +2.1 s after SIGTERM; EngineCore is signalled once it finishes (`MPClient: start timeout=62.9s`); server exits +6.9 s** | | New RPC 0.5 s after SIGTERM | `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNAVAILABLE` | Each case ran once per column. The "This PR" column is the current head, e21408569e. With `--shutdown-timeout 2`, 8ba921b0b3 gave in-flight RPCs exactly 2 s, so the stream was cut at +2.0 s (170/4000). Its decode leg also failed: EngineCore's deadline was about 7 s, and the read came at +8 s. With a request still being preprocessed at SIGTERM, cbe28ee5e9 started EngineCore's shutdown 0.1 s after SIGTERM. `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` closes the renderer's executor first, so the request failed while its image was being processed: `INVALID_ARGUMENT: multimodal placeholder validation failed: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown`. **Why the overlapped variant aborts in-flight prefills.** When SIGTERM arrived, its prefill server logged `EngineCore: draining in-flight requests count=16`: the second wave had reached the server before SIGTERM but was still in EngineCore's input queue behind the first step. EngineCore rejects every request it reads once its shutdown has started (`_reject_add_in_shutdown`), so those 15 came back as aborts. With this PR the prefill server logged `MPClient: start timeout=64.6s`: EngineCore was signalled 0.4 s after SIGTERM, once all 32 prefills were done. **Unit test.** `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_grpc_shutdown.py` runs `_drain_and_stop` against a real `grpc.aio` server and a fake `AsyncLLM` whose `shutdown(timeout)` blocks like EngineCore's drain mode and rejects requests it reads after shutdown has started. Like `test_grpc_health.py`, it is skipped when the `grpc` extra is not installed. In the image above with `smg-grpc-servicer==0.14.0`: `8 passed`, including `test_inflight_count_follows_rpcs`, which checks that the count follows completed and cancelled RPCs and leaves subscriptions out. Against the overlapped variant, `test_requests_queued_at_sigterm_are_served` fails. Without the interceptor, `test_request_in_preprocessing_at_sigterm_is_served` fails; its fake only registers the request after a preprocessing delay. **Commands** ```bash pip install "vllm[grpc]" # smg-grpc-servicer + smg-grpc-proto CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --grpc --port 18000 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --shutdown-timeout 60 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' & P=$! CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5605 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --grpc --port 18050 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --shutdown-timeout 60 \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' & D=$! python grpc_shutdown_repro.py pd --prefill localhost:18000 --decode localhost:18050 python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff --prefill localhost:18000 --prefill-pid $P \ --decode localhost:18050 --delay 8 python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream --addr localhost:18050 --pid $D --max-tokens 4000 ``` The other rows add, on fresh servers: ```bash # SubscribeKvEvents open (both servers also get --kv-events-config, endpoints on distinct ports) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff ... --hold kv-events python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream ... --max-tokens 1000 --hold kv-events # prefills in flight (prefill server also gets --max-num-batched-tokens 131072) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff ... --concurrency 32 --prompt-len 7680 \ --wave2 15 --wave-gap 0.1 --sigterm-during-prefill --sigterm-delay 0.15 --delay 3 # stream longer than the budget (both servers with --shutdown-timeout 20) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream ... --max-tokens 7000 # second SIGTERM python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff ... --second-sigterm 2 python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream ... --max-tokens 7000 --second-sigterm 5 # request still being preprocessed: one server, no KV transfer SMG_VLLM_MM_PROCESSOR=inprocess vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct --grpc --port 18000 \ --enforce-eager --max-model-len 8192 --shutdown-timeout 60 & VL=$! python grpc_shutdown_repro.py mm --addr localhost:18000 --pid $VL \ --model-dir --media-delay 1.5 --sigterm-after 0.05 ``` On our cluster both servers were pinned to one NIC (`UCX_NET_DEVICES=mlx5_0:1 UCX_TLS=rc_x,rc,dc_x,dc,cuda_copy`). Otherwise UCX picks the NIC nearest each GPU, and the two land on rails that do not reach each other. This is a property of the cluster, not of this change, and the control row shows the handoff path works.
grpc_shutdown_repro.py ```python """Reproducer for `vllm serve --grpc` ignoring --shutdown-timeout. Needs `pip install "vllm[grpc]"` (grpcio + smg-grpc-proto). Start the servers yourself (commands in the PR description), then: # 1) in-flight stream on SIGTERM python grpc_shutdown_repro.py stream --addr localhost:50051 --pid # 2) control: plain prefill -> decode handoff, no SIGTERM (must succeed first) python grpc_shutdown_repro.py pd --prefill localhost:50051 --decode localhost:50052 # 3) NIXL handoff: SIGTERM the prefill after its RPC returns, read on decode python grpc_shutdown_repro.py handoff --prefill localhost:50051 \ --prefill-pid --decode localhost:50052 --delay 8 # 4) slow preprocessing at SIGTERM: a Qwen3-VL server (SMG_VLLM_MM_PROCESSOR=inprocess) # fetches the request's image from a local server that answers after # --media-delay s; SIGTERM lands --sigterm-after s after the request is sent python grpc_shutdown_repro.py mm --addr localhost:50051 --pid \ --model-dir --media-delay 1.5 --sigterm-after 0.05 Options for stream and handoff: --hold [KIND] keep an RPC open on the SIGTERMed server that only ends when the client or server ends it: a router's SubscribeKvEvents stream (kv-events, needs the server's --kv-events-config), or a reflection stream (reflection, the default, works on any server) --second-sigterm S send another SIGTERM S seconds after the first handoff only: --concurrency K --sigterm-during-prefill [--sigterm-delay S] K prefills with distinct prompts, SIGTERM S seconds (default 0.3) after sending them, while they run --wave2 W --wave-gap G send the last W of them G seconds after the others, so they reach a server that is busy with the first ones Prompt token ids are synthetic; any model with a vocabulary > 30000 works. The stream must outlive the old 5 s grace by a wide margin, so pick --max-tokens for the model's single-stream speed (e.g. 4000 with --enforce-eager). """ import argparse import json import os import random import signal import threading import time import uuid from collections import Counter from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer from io import BytesIO from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit import grpc import psutil from grpc_reflection.v1alpha import reflection_pb2, reflection_pb2_grpc from smg_grpc_proto import vllm_engine_pb2 as pb from smg_grpc_proto import vllm_engine_pb2_grpc as pb_grpc from smg_grpc_proto.generated import common_pb2 def make_request(input_ids, max_tokens, stream, kv=None): kwargs = {} if kv is not None: kwargs["kv_transfer_params_json"] = json.dumps(kv) return pb.GenerateRequest( request_id=str(uuid.uuid4()), tokenized=pb.TokenizedInput(input_ids=input_ids), sampling_params=pb.SamplingParams( max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True ), stream=stream, **kwargs, ) def prompt(args, i): if args.concurrency == 1: return list(range(1000, 1000 + args.prompt_len)) # Distinct prompts so the prefills miss every prefix cache. rng = random.Random(i) return [rng.randrange(1000, 30000) for _ in range(args.prompt_len)] class ExitWatcher: """Records when pid exits, polling from the moment SIGTERM is sent.""" def __init__(self, pid, second_after=None): self.pid = pid self.exited = None os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM) self.sigterm = time.monotonic() self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._poll, daemon=True) self.thread.start() if second_after is not None: timer = threading.Timer(second_after, self._second) timer.daemon = True timer.start() def _second(self): if self.exited is None: os.kill(self.pid, signal.SIGTERM) print(f"second SIGTERM at {self.since()}", flush=True) def _poll(self): while True: try: if psutil.Process(self.pid).status() == psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE: break except psutil.NoSuchProcess: break time.sleep(0.05) self.exited = time.monotonic() def since(self, t=None): return f"+{(time.monotonic() if t is None else t) - self.sigterm:.1f}s" def report(self, timeout): self.thread.join(timeout) if self.exited is None: return "still running" return f"{self.since(self.exited)} after SIGTERM" class Hold: """An RPC that stays open until the client or the server ends it.""" def __init__(self, addr, kind): self.release = threading.Event() self.ended = None self.result = None channel = grpc.insecure_channel(addr) if kind == "kv-events": stub = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(channel) self.responses = stub.SubscribeKvEvents(common_pb2.SubscribeKvEventsRequest()) self.responses.initial_metadata() # the stream is up else: # The client never half-closes the request stream. def requests(): yield reflection_pb2.ServerReflectionRequest(list_services="") self.release.wait() stub = reflection_pb2_grpc.ServerReflectionStub(channel) self.responses = stub.ServerReflectionInfo(requests()) next(self.responses) # the stream is up self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._drain, daemon=True) self.thread.start() def _drain(self): try: for _ in self.responses: pass self.result = "OK" except grpc.RpcError as e: self.result = f"{e.code().name}: {e.details()}" self.ended = time.monotonic() def report(self, watcher, timeout): self.thread.join(timeout) self.release.set() if self.ended is None: return "still open" return f"{self.result}, ended {watcher.since(self.ended)} after SIGTERM" def run_stream(args): hold = Hold(args.addr, args.hold) if args.hold else None stub = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.addr)) ids = prompt(args, 0) tokens, finish, error, watcher = 0, None, None, None try: for resp in stub.Generate(make_request(ids, args.max_tokens, stream=True)): if resp.HasField("chunk"): tokens += len(resp.chunk.token_ids) else: finish = resp.complete.finish_reason if watcher is None and tokens > 0: watcher = ExitWatcher(args.pid, args.second_sigterm) time.sleep(0.5) try: late = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.addr)) next(iter(late.Generate(make_request(ids, 1, stream=False)))) print("late RPC: accepted (unexpected)") except grpc.RpcError as e: print(f"late RPC: {e.code().name}") except grpc.RpcError as e: error = f"{e.code().name}: {e.details()}" t_end = time.monotonic() if watcher is None: raise SystemExit(f"stream produced no tokens: finish={finish} error={error}") print( f"stream: tokens={tokens}/{args.max_tokens} finish={finish} error={error} " f"ended={watcher.since(t_end)} after SIGTERM" ) if hold is not None: print(f"held RPC: {hold.report(watcher, args.exit_timeout)}") print(f"server exit: {watcher.report(args.exit_timeout)}") def generate(stub, req, timeout=None): """One non-streaming Generate: (complete, error).""" try: complete = None for resp in stub.Generate(req, timeout=timeout): complete = resp.complete return complete, None except grpc.RpcError as e: return None, f"{e.code().name}: {e.details()}" def prefill_then_decode(args, sigterm_pid=None): prefill = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.prefill)) decode = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.decode)) prompts = [prompt(args, i) for i in range(args.concurrency)] hold = Hold(args.prefill, args.hold) if sigterm_pid and args.hold else None pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(args.concurrency) watcher = None first = len(prompts) - getattr(args, "wave2", 0) futures = [] t_send = time.monotonic() for i, ids in enumerate(prompts): if i == first and i: time.sleep(args.wave_gap) futures.append(pool.submit( generate, prefill, make_request(ids, 1, stream=False, kv={"do_remote_decode": True}))) if sigterm_pid and args.sigterm_during_prefill: time.sleep(max(t_send + args.sigterm_delay - time.monotonic(), 0)) watcher = ExitWatcher(sigterm_pid, args.second_sigterm) prefills = [f.result() for f in futures] t_prefilled = time.monotonic() errors = [e for _, e in prefills if e] reasons = Counter(c.finish_reason for c, _ in prefills if c) handed_off = sum(1 for c, _ in prefills if c and c.kv_transfer_params_json) print(f"prefill done: {handed_off}/{len(prefills)} handed off " f"finish={dict(sorted(reasons.items()))} errors={errors[:3]}") if watcher is not None: print(f"prefill RPCs returned {watcher.since(t_prefilled)} after SIGTERM") elif sigterm_pid: watcher = ExitWatcher(sigterm_pid, args.second_sigterm) time.sleep(args.delay) jobs = [] for ids, (complete, _) in zip(prompts, prefills): if complete is not None and complete.kv_transfer_params_json: params = json.loads(complete.kv_transfer_params_json) req = make_request(ids, args.max_tokens, stream=False, kv=params) jobs.append(pool.submit(generate, decode, req, args.exit_timeout)) decodes = [j.result() for j in jobs] ok = [c for c, _ in decodes if c and c.finish_reason == "length" and len(c.output_ids) == args.max_tokens] finishes = sorted({f"{c.finish_reason}:{len(c.output_ids)}" for c, _ in decodes if c}) errors = [e for _, e in decodes if e] print(f"decode: {len(ok)}/{len(prompts)} ok (finish:tokens {finishes}, " f"max_tokens={args.max_tokens}) errors={errors[:3]}") if hold is not None: print(f"held RPC: {hold.report(watcher, args.exit_timeout)}") if watcher is not None: print(f"prefill exit: {watcher.report(args.exit_timeout)}") def run_handoff(args): prefill_then_decode(args, sigterm_pid=args.prefill_pid) class SlowMedia: """Serves one random PNG over HTTP, each answer after ?delay= seconds.""" def __init__(self, size): from PIL import Image buf = BytesIO() Image.frombytes("RGB", (size, size), os.urandom(size * size * 3)).save(buf, "PNG") png = buf.getvalue() class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): time.sleep(float(parse_qs(urlsplit(self.path).query)["delay"][0])) self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "image/png") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(png))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(png) def log_message(self, *args): pass self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler) threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start() def url(self, delay): port = self.server.server_port return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/image.png?delay={delay}&n={uuid.uuid4().hex}" def run_mm(args): from transformers import AutoTokenizer text = ( "<|im_start|>user\n<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" "Describe this image.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n" ) ids = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_dir).encode(text, add_special_tokens=False) media = SlowMedia(args.image_size) stub = pb_grpc.VllmEngineStub(grpc.insecure_channel(args.addr)) def request(delay): return pb.GenerateRequest( request_id=str(uuid.uuid4()), tokenized=pb.TokenizedInput(input_ids=ids, original_text=text), media_refs=pb.MediaRefs(items=[pb.MediaRef( modality=common_pb2.Modality.Value("IMAGE"), url=media.url(delay))]), sampling_params=pb.SamplingParams( max_tokens=args.max_tokens, temperature=0.0, ignore_eos=True), stream=False, ) def outcome(complete, error): if complete is None: return f"finish=None error={error}" return (f"finish={complete.finish_reason} " f"tokens={len(complete.output_ids)}/{args.max_tokens}") print(f"control (no media delay): {outcome(*generate(stub, request(0), 300))}", flush=True) t_send = time.monotonic() future = ThreadPoolExecutor(1).submit(generate, stub, request(args.media_delay), args.exit_timeout) time.sleep(max(t_send + args.sigterm_after - time.monotonic(), 0)) watcher = ExitWatcher(args.pid) result = future.result() print(f"mm request (media fetch {args.media_delay}s, SIGTERM {args.sigterm_after}s after " f"sending): {outcome(*result)}, ended {watcher.since()} after SIGTERM") print(f"server exit: {watcher.report(args.exit_timeout)}") def main(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="mode", required=True) stream = sub.add_parser("stream") stream.add_argument("--addr", required=True) stream.add_argument("--pid", type=int, required=True) stream.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=4000) handoff = sub.add_parser("handoff") handoff.add_argument("--prefill", required=True) handoff.add_argument("--prefill-pid", type=int, required=True) handoff.add_argument("--decode", required=True) handoff.add_argument("--delay", type=float, default=8.0) handoff.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) handoff.add_argument("--sigterm-during-prefill", action="store_true") handoff.add_argument("--sigterm-delay", type=float, default=0.3) handoff.add_argument("--wave2", type=int, default=0) handoff.add_argument("--wave-gap", type=float, default=0.0) mm = sub.add_parser("mm") mm.add_argument("--addr", required=True) mm.add_argument("--pid", type=int, required=True) mm.add_argument("--model-dir", required=True) mm.add_argument("--media-delay", type=float, default=1.5) mm.add_argument("--sigterm-after", type=float, default=0.05) mm.add_argument("--image-size", type=int, default=1024) mm.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) mm.add_argument("--exit-timeout", type=float, default=120.0) # Control: the same prefill -> decode handoff with no SIGTERM. pd = sub.add_parser("pd") pd.add_argument("--prefill", required=True) pd.add_argument("--decode", required=True) pd.add_argument("--delay", type=float, default=0.0) pd.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) for p in (handoff, pd): p.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=1) for p in (stream, handoff): p.add_argument("--hold", nargs="?", const="reflection", default=None, choices=("reflection", "kv-events")) p.add_argument("--second-sigterm", type=float, default=None) for p in (stream, handoff, pd): p.add_argument("--prompt-len", type=int, default=512) p.add_argument("--exit-timeout", type=float, default=120.0) args = parser.parse_args() if args.mode == "stream": args.concurrency = 1 run_stream(args) elif args.mode == "handoff": run_handoff(args) elif args.mode == "mm": run_mm(args) else: prefill_then_decode(args) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
`pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/launchers/grpc_server.py tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_grpc_shutdown.py` passes: ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy (3.11) and the repository's local checks. No model evaluation is needed. The change only affects process shutdown, not sampling, scheduling or outputs. ## Details **Root cause (P/D flow, NIXL pull mode)** 1. The router sends the prefill leg to P with `kv_transfer_params={"do_remote_decode": true}`. 2. P runs prefill. `request_finished` delays the block free and grants a lease (`kv_lease_duration`, 30 s by default). The Generate RPC returns the handoff params: block ids and the side-channel host and port. 3. The router sends the decode leg to D. D starts heartbeating P as soon as the request enters its scheduler, which extends the lease while the request waits. 4. SIGTERM reaches P. `server.stop(grace=5.0)` returns at once, because the prefill RPC has already finished. `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` then runs without a timeout, so `CoreEngineProcManager.shutdown(None)` calls `shutdown(procs, None)`, which sends SIGTERM, joins for 5 s, and then sends SIGKILL. EngineCore's drain mode (`_handle_shutdown`) would keep stepping while `Scheduler.has_finished_requests()` still counts requests waiting on delayed connector frees, but EngineCore is killed before D reads. 5. D schedules the request, and its NIXL handshake or read fails. With `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"` the request finishes with an error. With `"recompute"`, D recomputes the prompt. The more decode requests that are queued and heartbeating against blocks held by one prefill, the more requests a single prefill restart fails. Plain streams are also cut: any RPC still running 5 s after SIGTERM is cancelled. **Fix** With `shutdown_timeout > 0`, one deadline covers both: 1. `server.stop(grace=max(N, 5 s))` refuses new RPCs at once and resolves when no RPC is live; grpc.aio resolves `stop()` once no live RPC remains. RPCs still running at the deadline are cancelled, which aborts their requests. The 5 s minimum is the grace RPCs already get with `0`. 2. EngineCore keeps running normally while anything could still send it a request. An `_InflightRpcs` server interceptor counts the in-flight `VllmEngine` RPCs, excluding subscriptions (`SubscribeKvEvents`): an RPC counts from the moment the server dispatches it, before its request message is received, until the task that grpc.aio serves it in finishes, whether or not its handler ran. `AsyncLLM.get_num_unfinished_requests()` covers requests that outlive their RPC. Both are checked every 0.1 s, and idle has to hold on two checks in a row, which covers an RPC that gRPC accepted before SIGTERM but has not yet handed to its task. The interceptor costs about 10 µs of server CPU per RPC and nothing measurable per streamed message: in a grpc.aio micro-benchmark on the same machine, 153.5 → 163.0 µs per unary call and 16.6 → 16.7 µs per streamed message. EngineCore has to keep running: it rejects every request it reads once its shutdown has started, including ones the frontend forwarded before SIGTERM (the in-flight row) and ones still being preprocessed (the preprocessing row). Running normally, it also keeps serving NIXL reads. 3. `AsyncLLM.shutdown(timeout=remaining + 5 s)` then runs in an executor, as `launcher.py` does. EngineCore receives SIGTERM, enters drain mode, finishes connector work such as unread NIXL blocks, and exits. The 5 s floor keeps EngineCore's teardown (KV connector, device memory, shm) from being skipped when a request used the whole budget; before this PR it always had a 5 s join. 4. RPCs still open 5 s after EngineCore has stopped, such as a `SubscribeKvEvents` stream, are cancelled. 5. A second SIGTERM or SIGINT calls `server.stop(None)`, which cancels every RPC and so aborts their requests. EngineCore is then left with connector work only. **Why EngineCore is not signalled at SIGTERM, unlike HTTP** The in-flight row. The HTTP path signals the engine first and relies on `_reject_add_in_shutdown` for requests that arrive during the drain; #61562 documents that requests still queued at that point return `finish_reason=abort`. Here `server.stop()` already refuses new requests, so EngineCore does not need to reject any, and keeping it running until the in-flight requests are done serves all of them. Connector work gets the same deadline either way. **Limitations** - RPCs still running at `max(N, 5 s)` are cancelled. - A prefill holding blocks that no decode will read waits for the lease to expire (`kv_lease_duration` after the last heartbeat) or until `max(N, 5 s) + 5 s`. - The 5 s floor covers a normal teardown. An EngineCore whose workers do not exit within `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` takes longer, and is SIGKILLed at the deadline plus 5 s when a request used the whole budget. - A second signal does not cut connector work short. - An RPC that gRPC accepted before SIGTERM but has not handed to its task within one check interval (0.1 s) is not counted yet, and its request can be rejected by EngineCore, as on the HTTP path. - Supervisors must allow more than `max(N, 5 s) + 5 s`; for example, Kubernetes `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` must exceed that. - The Rust frontend's `--grpc-port` listener is a separate path and is not changed. **Not a duplicate** I searched `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open` for "grpc shutdown", "grpc shutdown-timeout", "grpc drain", "gRPC graceful" and "grpc_server grace". No open PR touches this shutdown path. #56886 is the Rust frontend's discovery withdrawal, and #61562 is the HTTP multi-API-server path. **AI assistance** Claude Code traced the shutdown path and drafted the patch, the reproducer and this description. I reviewed every line and ran the validation myself. ---
