commits.pr_title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Enable PCP with PP or DP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Relax the model-level PCP compatibility checks for text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA CUDA to enable the existing PCP + PP and PCP + DP execution paths. The underlying MRV2 implementations are already provided by #59139 (PP) and #57075 (DP). No other open PR was found enabling these model-specific combinations; #49246's generic DP approach was superseded by #57075, while #63106 addresses cross-stage cache relay with PCP=1.

## Claims

- Remove the blanket PP=DP=1 restriction when PCP is enabled, allowing the existing PP or DP execution paths. Combining PP + DP is allowed when TP=1 or expert parallelism is disabled; DCP must remain 1.
- Add PP2 + PCP2 and DP2 + PCP2 cases to the existing `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py`, using real-weight serving and generation.

## Validation

**Hardware**: 1 node with 8 H20(96G) GPUs.

**Image**: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-df3bd094aeea829f27baa0a5282830464f601d9f`

**Startup Command**:

PP+PCP（`VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26`）：
```bash
VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26 vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18001 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --moe-backend humming --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager --no-async-scheduling --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

DP+PCP：
```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18001 --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --moe-backend humming --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager --no-async-scheduling --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

4. **GSM8K**
   - EvalScope 1.11.1，GSM8K full 1319，4-shot，batch 64，temperature 0，top_p 1，seed 42，max_tokens 8192。
   - PP+PCP：`1286/1319 = 97.50%`，0 API error。
   - DP+PCP：`1282/1319 = 97.19%`，0 API error。

## Details

The runtime change is confined to the NVIDIA model's compatibility checks. PP/PCP execution, stage-entry Engram handling, and DP/EP communication reuse their existing implementations. The existing PCP test file adds generation cases for the newly enabled combinations: the PP case uses Flash's `14,26` partition, and the DP case sends a request to each replica.

With PCP enabled, PP>1 and DP>1 are rejected only when TP>1 and expert parallelism is enabled: PP currently disables the model's sequence-parallel path required by DP+PCP AgRs MoE communication in that topology. TP=1 or disabled expert parallelism passes this combined-topology gate; these additional combinations still require GPU validation. DCP must remain 1; KV transfer, microbatching, and MegaMoE remain disabled. Preserve main's fixed-length DSpark support with PP=1 and the existing PR's exclusion of speculative decoding with PCP + PP. Prefix caching still requires SWA bounded replay.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change. The human submitter remains responsible for line-by-line review; validation beyond the two configurations reported above remains pending.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Update FlashKDA pin, consume row-strided QKV directly
commits.pr_body:
## Overview GLM-5.3-Flash prefill hands FlashKDA packed Q/K/V views (`3 * H * D` token stride, contiguous H/D rows), and `_flashkda_prefill` copied them into three contiguous buffers because the kernel required dense inputs. FlashKDA #15 (vllm-project/FlashKDA#15) accepts row-strided Q/K/V, so this PR pins that revision and passes the views directly. This is the consumer-side alternative to producing dense QKV in the convolution itself. ## Claims - Removes the three per-layer Q/K/V copies from GLM-5.3-Flash prefill; profiles show 4 -> 1 copy kernels (the remaining one is the beta transpose). - Serial A/B/A on H200, ISL2048/OSL1: saturated prefill throughput **21.37 -> 21.78 req/s (+1.9%)**, median TTFT **-2.1%**. - GSM8K is unchanged within sampling noise: 0.9163 (A1) / 0.9125 (candidate) / 0.9170 (A2), i.e. 1204 / 1199 / 1205 of 1314 questions. ## Validation Environment: 4 x H200, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint, BF16 KDA projections, serial A/B/A on the same host. Server: ```sh vllm serve --served-model-name glm53flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' ``` Client (three runs per arm at each rate, 256 prompts per run): ```sh vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8234 \ --model --served-model-name glm53flash --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 --ignore-eos \ --request-rate <20|inf> --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 256 --seed <101+> ``` | Arm | rate=inf (req/s) | rate=20 (req/s) | median TTFT (ms) | GSM8K | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A1 base | 21.37 / 21.46 / 21.38 (mean 21.40) | 16.69 / 18.51 / 18.63 | 1456.9 | 0.9163 | | B candidate | 21.72 / 21.77 / 21.86 (mean 21.78) | 18.81 / 18.41 / 18.91 | 1425.5 | 0.9125 | | A2 base | 21.35 / 21.27 / 21.40 (mean 21.34) | 18.72 / 18.12 / 19.17 | 1456.6 | 0.9170 | At 20 req/s the arms overlap; the first A1 repetition is a cold run and the bracketing A2 matches the candidate. GSM8K is 5-shot, greedy, 1314 questions: the two baselines answer 1204 and 1205 correctly (0.07 pp apart) and the candidate answers 1199, 5-6 questions fewer (about 0.4 pp). One binomial standard error on 1314 questions at this accuracy is about 0.8 pp, so the difference is not distinguishable from sampling noise, but it is larger than the spread between the two baseline runs. Profile (captured on the earlier producer-side revision that removed the same three copies; the copy removal is identical here since the convolution output is unchanged): - Before: [trace](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33468759/baseline-dp0_pp0_tp0_dcp0_ep0_rank0.perfetto.pt.trace.json.gz) — - After: [trace](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33468763/producer-dp0_pp0_tp0_dcp0_ep0_rank0.perfetto.pt.trace.json.gz) — ## Details - The change is two lines: pin FlashKDA `17a037d` -> `47fc9fec` in `cmake/external_projects/flashkda.cmake`, and drop `q/k/v.contiguous()` in `vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`. `g`, `beta`, states, workspace and output handling are unchanged, as is the tensor operator schema. - FlashKDA #15 accepts any aligned token stride as long as the H/D rows are contiguous, the base pointer and row starts are 16-byte aligned, rows do not overlap and the B*T flattening is uniform. The merged convolution output satisfies all of these, including the 16-byte alignment (`3 * H * 128 * 2` bytes is always a multiple of 16). - Beta still needs the transpose inside FlashKDA; that is unchanged and is the single remaining copy kernel in the profile. - The pin also brings FlashKDA #15's standalone `launch_prepare` / `launch_recurrence` signature change. Nothing in vLLM `main` calls those launchers today (main pinned `17a037d`, which predates them), but the in-flight KCP work (vllm#59304) should pass `0` / its strides when it rebases. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

commits.pr_title: [NIXL] Bump NIXL version to 1.5.2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bump the NIXL pin from 1.5.0 to [1.5.2](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/releases/tag/v1.5.2) for both CUDA 13 (`requirements/kv_connectors.txt`) and CUDA 12 (`requirements/kv_connectors_cu12.txt`) images. This replaces the reverted 1.5.1 bump (#63817, reverted in #64085).

## Claims

- CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 images both install NIXL 1.5.2. The two pins move together.
- No EFA regression: 1.5.2 drops the accidental libfabric 2.7.0 bump that caused the 1.5.1 revert (ai-dynamo/nixl#2528). The LIBFABRIC plugin needs the same libfabric symbol versions as 1.5.0.
- Picks up these LIBFABRIC fixes:
  - Fallback for context-independent CUDA allocations, such as mapped VMM memory (ai-dynamo/nixl#2470).
  - EFA unsolicited write recv is disabled regardless of build headers (ai-dynamo/nixl#2529).
  - All endpoint/CQ/AV calls are serialized with the rail EP lock (ai-dynamo/nixl#2542).
- The UCX path does not change.

## Validation

- **Dependency resolution**, x86_64 and aarch64, both files: `nixl`, `nixl-cu12` and `nixl-cu13` all resolve to 1.5.2.
  ```bash
  uv pip compile --python-version 3.12 --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --torch-backend cu129 requirements/kv_connectors.txt
  # repeated for aarch64-manylinux_2_28 and requirements/kv_connectors_cu12.txt
  ```
- `pre-commit run --files requirements/kv_connectors.txt requirements/kv_connectors_cu12.txt`: passed.
- **ELF check** of `libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so` in `nixl_cu13` cp312 x86_64. None of the wheels bundle `libfabric.so`.

  | Version | Required libfabric symbol versions |
  |---|---|
  | 1.5.0 | `FABRIC_1.0`, `1.1`, `1.7` |
  | 1.5.1 (reverted) | `FABRIC_1.0`, `1.1`, `1.10` |
  | 1.5.2 | `FABRIC_1.0`, `1.1`, `1.7` |

- **Not yet run:** GPU P/D serving with `NixlConnector` on CUDA 12 and CUDA 13, LIBFABRIC over EFA, and the aarch64 Rubin NIXL source build. `requirements/kv_connectors.txt` is in the run-all patterns (`.buildkite/ci_config.yaml`), so CI runs the NIXL integration and P/D accuracy tests.

- Tested on 2 x AWS p6-b300.48xlarge, Kimi K3 disagg

## Details

`release/1.5.0...v1.5.2` touches only:

- version strings and attributions

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Size AITER MLA persistent metadata for every decode query length
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`AiterMLAMetadataBuilder` sizes its persistent decode metadata buffers with one `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` call at `reorder_batch_threshold` (#45227), but it builds metadata for every query length up to that threshold, and aiter's buffer needs are not monotonic in the query length. A bf16 DSpark draft overflows the buffers and faults. This PR sizes them for the largest need of any query length up to the threshold.

Found by Hyperloom.

## Claims

- Fixes `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` during warmup for Kimi-K3 with its DSpark draft (TP4, `num_speculative_tokens: 7`, bf16 KV cache).
- No change without speculative decoding (threshold 1, the same single call as before), or for 16-head fp8 KV caches up to threshold 8. Other configurations can get larger buffers, e.g. 32-head fp8 on gfx950, which is 64-wide at query length 3 and 128-wide at query length 4.
- Adds `test_builder_sizes_metadata_for_every_decode_qlen`.

## Validation

aiter v0.1.26 called directly on MI355X: 16 heads, 1024 requests, non-causal, bf16 Q/KV and metadata, compared with a PyTorch reference.

| Query length | Buffers sized for | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8 | memory fault |
| 7 | 7 | matches (max abs err 0.003) |
| 5, 6 | 8 | memory fault |
| 4 | 8 | matches (max abs err 0.004) |

Kimi-K3 truncated to 8 layers (`--hf-overrides`, `--load-format dummy`) with its DSpark draft (`target_layer_ids` remapped), TP4, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, CUDA graphs on, vLLM built from main at b3b0bc3059. Main faults during warmup; this PR starts and serves 24 concurrent requests.

Unit tests on MI355X against the built tree, `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py`: this PR 113 passed. Main fails 21: the new test, and the cases of `test_builder_init_sizes_decode_metadata_and_filters_dcp_maps`, which now expects one sizing call per query length.

## Details

On gfx950, aiter tiles the `num_heads x qlen` packed query rows of a bf16 block by 64 when there are fewer than 128 of them, and by 128 otherwise. With 16 heads and 1024 requests, query lengths 5-7 need `work_info_set` (2558, 8) and `reduce_final_map` (2048, 2), while query length 8 needs (1279, 8) and (1024, 2). A DSpark draft runs `k`-token blocks under a `k + 1` threshold, so `k = 7` lands on the larger case. At 1024 requests the larger sizing adds about 55 KB of int32 buffers.

CI does not run a DSpark draft on MI355X. The results above use dummy weights; a real-weight Kimi-K3 run was not done. #41016 (closed) sized the batch dimension of these buffers; this PR sizes the query-length dimension.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and prepare this change. I reviewed every changed line and reproduced the results above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Keep KDA prefill checkpoints with the gluon backend
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since #59552, the gluon KDA prefill backend (AITER `chunk_kda`) is the default on CDNA4. It switches Kimi-K3's KDA prefill checkpoints off, because AITER `chunk_kda` cannot export the mid-prefill state. This PR keeps the checkpoints on with gluon: only prefill steps that carry checkpoint metadata go to the fused HIP kernel, and every other step stays on gluon.

## Claims

- With `kda_prefill_backend="gluon"` and the fused kernel built, `get_kv_cache_spec` reserves the prefill checkpoint block (alignment `KDA_CHECKPOINT_ALIGNMENT`), as the `fused` backend does. Previously it reported 0 blocks.
- A step whose `checkpoint` metadata is set runs `chunk_kda_prefill(backend="fused")`. Steps without checkpoint metadata keep the configured backend.
- If the fused kernel is missing (`is_fused_kda_chunk_supported()` is False), gluon still opts out of checkpoints, so behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Kernel and spec tests, run on MI355X (1 GPU) in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392`, with this diff applied to the image's vLLM (its `kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` matches the base commit):

| Command | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py -k gluon_backend` | `test_gluon_backend_keeps_the_checkpoint` fails: `assert 0 == 1` on `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks` | 2 passed |
| `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py` | n/a | 28 passed |
| `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_chunk.py` | n/a | 77 passed (includes the gluon parity tests and the new handoff test) |
| `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_chunk.py` (no AITER) | n/a | 98 passed, 6 skipped (gluon needs AITER) |

The new `test_gluon_hands_checkpoint_steps_to_fused` test prefills one 1024-token sequence in three steps: gluon `[0, 256)`, then fused `[256, 768)` with a checkpoint at token 512, then gluon `[768, 1024)`. It compares the result with a single Triton prefill of the whole sequence:
- Output: atol/rtol 2e-2.
- Final state: 5e-3.
- Checkpoint versus a Triton prefill of the 512-token prefix: 5e-3.

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `test_amd_kda_checkpoint.py` has 11 metadata-builder failures (`KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder builds its own FLA chunk metadata ... 'aiter_flydsl'`). They fail the same way on the unpatched image, and this PR does not touch them.

End-to-end check: Kimi-K3 TP8, DCP8, DSpark with 4 drafts and real rejection sampling, `--enable-prefix-caching` (mamba cache mode `align`), `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, on the same image. Both arms use the default `auto` KDA prefill backend, which resolves to gluon.

| | Without this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Server log | `KDA prefill backend: gluon` | `KDA prefill backend: gluon`, `KDA prefill checkpoint enabled.` |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions (flexible / strict) | 0.9560 / 0.9553 (±0.0056) | 0.9659 / 0.9651 (±0.0050) |
| Prefix-cache check (below) | PASS | PASS |
| Tracebacks in server log | 0 | 0 |

The GSM8K prompts are shorter than one mamba block, so they never reach a checkpoint (`prefix_cache_hits_total` grows only during the prefix check). GSM8K therefore shows that steps without a checkpoint still serve correctly on gluon. The prefix check is what exercises the checkpoint.

The prefix check sends four prompts of about 3.8k / 9.4k / 20.6k / 45.2k tokens. Each prompt is a list of facts plus a question about one of them, run with greedy decoding:
1. Request A, cold.
2. Request B: the same facts and a different question, served from the cache A left.
3. Request B again, after `/reset_prefix_cache`.

| Prompt tokens | B cached tokens, without / with | Answers correct (A, B warm, B cold), without / with |
|---|---|---|
| 3771 | 1536 / 1536 | 3/3 / 3/3 |
| 9371 | 7680 / 7680 | 3/3 / 3/3 |
| 20644 | 18432 / 18432 | 3/3 / 3/3 |
| 45151 | 43008 / 43008 | 3/3 / 3/3 |

Cached lengths are the same with and without the PR. Without it, the scheduler gets the same snapshot by ending the prefill step at the block boundary and running the tail as an extra step. With the PR, the snapshot comes out of the fused kernel inside the step, and the warm answers, which resume from it, are correct. This host is thermally throttled, so the time saved by dropping the extra step was measured on another node (below).

**Time to first token.** Kimi-K3 TP8 on one unthrottled MI355X node, same image, default `auto` (gluon) backend, `--enable-prefix-caching`, DSpark with synthetic acceptance. Two server configurations from the InferenceX Kimi-K3 recipe:
- c1: DCP1, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`.
- c16: DCP8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`.

The client sends one random prompt at a time with 1 output token, after a warmup, using the same seeds in both arms. No prompt hit the prefix cache. Each cell is the median of 10 prompts (6 at 32768 and 65536), in ms.

| Prompt tokens | c1 without | c1 with | Δ | c16 without | c16 with | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 203.4 | 199.7 | −1.9% | 198.6 | 197.2 | −0.7% |
| 4096 | 413.0 | 237.2 | −42.6% | 398.6 | 244.9 | −38.5% |
| 8192 | 484.5 | 373.8 | −22.9% | 489.5 | 383.2 | −21.7% |
| 16384 | 793.3 | 686.3 | −13.5% | 905.1 | 905.5 | 0.0% |
| 32768 | 1537.8 | 1540.0 | +0.1% | 1733.7 | 1737.3 | +0.2% |
| 65536 | 3263.1 | 3143.7 | −3.7% | 3670.8 | 3544.1 | −3.5% |

Where the PR removes the split, it saves 107–176 ms per prompt. The unchanged rows are expected:
- With DSpark's block drop, the checkpoint sits one 1536-token block before the last full block.
- 1024 is shorter than one block, so there is no checkpoint.
- At 32768 the checkpoint (30720) is already a chunk boundary at both chunk sizes, so neither arm splits.
- At 16384 with c16, the checkpoint (13824) falls in a chunk that is not the prompt's last, where both arms stop anyway.

<details>
<summary>prefix_check.py</summary>

```python
"""Prefix-cache check for Kimi-K3 KDA prefill checkpoints.

Per prompt length: a cold request A (facts + question about fact i), then B
(same facts + question about fact j) which should hit the prefix cache, then
B again after a prefix-cache reset (cold). B's answer must be right both ways.
"""
import json, random, sys, time, urllib.request

URL = "http://localhost:8000"
TOK = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/model"
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(TOK, trust_remote_code=True)

def post(path, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL + path, data=json.dumps(body or {}).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    t = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=3600) as r:
        raw = r.read()
    return (json.loads(raw) if raw.strip().startswith(b"{") else raw.decode()), time.time() - t

def metrics():
    with urllib.request.urlopen(URL + "/metrics") as r:
        txt = r.read().decode()
    out = {}
    for ln in txt.splitlines():
        for k in ("vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total", "vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total"):
            if ln.startswith(k):
                out[k] = out.get(k, 0) + float(ln.split()[-1])
    return out

def build(n_tokens, seed):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    lines, facts = [], []
    while True:
        name = "".join(rnd.choice("BCDFGHJKLMNPRSTVZ") + rnd.choice("aeiou") for _ in range(3)).capitalize()
        code = rnd.randint(1000, 9999)
        facts.append((name, code))
        lines.append(f"Record {len(facts)}: the access code for the city of {name} is {code}.")
        if len(lines) % 50 == 0 and len(tok.encode("\n".join(lines))) >= n_tokens:
            break
    return "\n".join(lines), facts

def ask(doc, name):
    p = (f"Below is a list of records.\n\n{doc}\n\nQuestion: What is the access code for "
         f"the city of {name}? Answer with the four-digit number only.\nAnswer: The access code for the city of {name} is")
    r, dt = post("/v1/completions", {"model": "moonshotai/Kimi-K3", "prompt": p, "max_tokens": 8,
                                      "temperature": 0, "seed": 0})
    c = r["choices"][0]["text"]
    cached = (r.get("usage", {}).get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens")
    return c, r["usage"]["prompt_tokens"], cached, dt

res = []
ok_all = True
for n, seed in ((3000, 1), (9000, 2), (20000, 3), (45000, 4)):
    doc, facts = build(n, seed)
    rnd = random.Random(seed + 100)
    (na, ca), (nb, cb) = facts[rnd.randrange(len(facts))], facts[rnd.randrange(len(facts) // 4)]
    post("/reset_prefix_cache")
    a = ask(doc, na)
    m0 = metrics()
    b_warm = ask(doc, nb)
    m1 = metrics()
    post("/reset_prefix_cache")
    b_cold = ask(doc, nb)
    row = dict(target_tokens=n, prompt_tokens=a[1],
               A=dict(expect=ca, text=a[0], ok=str(ca) in a[0], cached=a[2], s=round(a[3], 2)),
               B_warm=dict(expect=cb, text=b_warm[0], ok=str(cb) in b_warm[0], cached=b_warm[2], s=round(b_warm[3], 2),
                           hit_tokens=m1.get("vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total", 0) - m0.get("vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total", 0)),
               B_cold=dict(text=b_cold[0], ok=str(cb) in b_cold[0], cached=b_cold[2], s=round(b_cold[3], 2)),
               warm_eq_cold=b_warm[0] == b_cold[0])
    ok_all &= row["A"]["ok"] and row["B_warm"]["ok"] and row["B_cold"]["ok"]
    res.append(row)
    print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
print("PREFIX_CHECK", "PASS" if ok_all else "FAIL")
```

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause:** `can_checkpoint` required `kda_prefill_backend == "fused"`. When `auto` resolved to gluon, the spec reserved no checkpoint block. The scheduler then fell back to splitting the final prefill chunk at the block boundary (`scheduler.py`), which costs an extra step per prompt and drops the interior checkpoints.
- **Why route to fused, not export from gluon:** AITER `chunk_kda` (amd-aiter 0.1.25 / 0.1.26 and AITER main) has no checkpoint output. The proper fix is to export the state from the chunk walk inside the kernel; that needs an AITER change first. This PR is the vLLM-only bridge. When AITER grows that output, the routing can be replaced by a signature check.
- **Trade-off:** checkpoint metadata is per step, so a batched prefill step in which any request crosses a snapshot position runs entirely on the fused kernel. Steps without a checkpoint keep gluon's speed. Decode throughput was not part of this measurement.
- **Related PRs (not duplicates):**
  - #56036 adds a separate `flashkda` prefill backend and does not touch checkpoint gating.
  - #61951 adds Triton prefill checkpoints for GLM-5.3-Flash KDA through a host-side split.
  - #61466 moves the prefill checkpoint alignment into `MambaBase.get_prefill_checkpoint_alignment()` and edits the same `get_kv_cache_spec`. Whichever lands second needs a small rebase; the gating condition here carries over unchanged.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf]  Enable prefix-cache SWA replay on gfx950
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Re-enable DeepSeek-V4.1 prefix-cache sliding-window bounded replay on gfx950. Decoder replay is a separate path and is already enabled by #59039 when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is on. This PR only restores the prefix-cache path from #57906.

The AITER sparse MLA path consumes slot IDs that `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` has already clamped to `replay_start`. The ROCm force-off in `attention.py` stays in place for every ROCm GPU other than gfx950, including gfx942. On gfx950 the sliding-window cache follows `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay`.

## Claims

- On gfx950, prefix-cache SWA replay is no longer forced off. The flag still defaults on, and `--no-swa-bounded-replay` still disables it. Other ROCm GPUs stay on the existing force-off path.
- On our best MI355X config, end-to-end throughput is 13.5% higher at concurrency 128 and 12% higher at concurrency 256.
- GSM8K and RULER NIAH are unchanged between stock and replay.

## Validation

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, all questions in flight:

| Arm | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| Stock, replay off | 0.904
| Replay on | 0.902

RULER `niah_single_1` (single needle, word key, number value, repeated haystack), 131,072 tokens, 5 samples, temperature 0:

| Arm | Score |
|---|---:|
| Stock, replay off | 1.0 |
| Replay on | 1.0 |

Prefix-cache sweep across the prefill-chunk boundary. Each point primes eight DP replicas with a shared prefix plus 128 new tokens, then repeats the query. `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` is the hit signal. Every second-wave request completed on both arms, with no GPU fault.

| Prefix tokens | Stock hit tokens | Replay hit tokens |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,920 | 15,360 | 15,360 |
| 2,048 | 16,256 | 16,384 |
| 2,176 | 17,280 | 17,408 |
| 4,096 | 32,640 | 32,768 |

A separate single-request check on an otherwise stock nightly (`00b6c4c`, chunk 2048, DEP8, one request, token-id prompts) shows the config-flag A/B. Warmed requests:

| Shape | Stock | Replay |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8k TTFT | 492 ms | 316 ms |
| 32k TTFT | 1.84 s | 1.23 s |
| 128k TTFT, 1k output | 7.42 s | 4.83 s |
| 128k prefill | 17,667 tok/s | 27,136 tok/s |
| 128k decode | 52 tok/s | 49–62 tok/s |

Decode does not change. A decode step is already one new token inside the window.

CI does not have this MI355X checkpoint, so Buildkite does not cover this path.

## Details

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 40 layers. KV is written at layers 2, 8, 14, and 20. The sliding window is 128 tokens. After layer 20 has written KV for a token, layers 21–39 only need the last 128 tokens. That trim is decoder replay (#59039). It is built from `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` and is already active on ROCm when the flag is left on.

This change is the prefix-cache half. On a prefix-cache hit, the SWA cache replays from `replay_start` instead of storing the full sliding window. gfx950 can take that path because AITER sparse MLA uses the already-clamped slot list. The old force-off assumed an extra clamp inside the FlashInfer and FlashMLA prefill kernels, which this path does not use. gfx942 cannot take AITER sparse MLA, so it stays forced off.

To enable it on a gfx950 recipe that sets `VLLM_NO_SWA_BOUNDED_REPLAY=1`, remove that setting. Keep model runner V2 and breakable CUDA graphs. A 4096-token prefill chunk is above the 768-token replay trim threshold, so it uses the trimmed graph.


## ROCm consumers

CDNA4 keeps prefix-cache SWA replay. Both ROCm consumers clamp to replay_start:

- Opt-in AITER sparse MLA reads slot ids from _compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel, which clamps start_pos.
- The default Triton gather path clamps the prefill gather length in ComputePrefillMetadataKernel and clamps swa_start again in combine_topk_swa_indices.

Every other ROCm GPU, including CDNA3, stays forced off. get_cdna_version() != 4 is the gate.
Limitations:

- Measured on gfx950 with the AITER Triton sparse MLA path.
- The flag defaults on, so gfx950 behavior changes for every DeepSeek-V4.1 server that does not pass `--no-swa-bounded-replay`.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Qwen4Exp: compute HyperConnection and PLE gate row offsets in int64
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Qwen4Exp HyperConnection kernels (`nvidia/ops/hc.py`, `amd/ops/hc.py`) and the PLE gate kernel (`common/ops/ple.py`) compute each token row's address as `ptr + row * stride` with `row = tl.program_id(0)`, so the product is evaluated in int32 and wraps once it exceeds 2**31 - 1. This widens the row index to int64 once per kernel.

## Claims

- For a 2560-wide hidden state with 4 HC streams, the HC row stride is 10240 elements and the PLE key/value row stride is 12800. The products wrap from row 209,716 and row 167,773 respectively, so any forward pass over 167,774 or more tokens loads and stores at the wrong rows. The startup profile run alone reaches this when `max_num_batched_tokens >= 167,774`.
- After the change every row offset in the 11 kernels is int64. Column, group, stream and tile indices stay int32.

## Validation

- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_row_offsets.py` (new) runs every HC op and `ple_gate` on inputs whose third row starts 2**31 + 8192 elements into its storage. It compares the result with the same rows stored contiguously, with `atol=0, rtol=0`. On CPU under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`:
  - on `main` (`212f3666`) both tests crash (SIGSEGV);
  - on this branch both pass.
- Compiled for sm90 with Triton 3.6.0, no GPU needed: `_grouped_gemma_rmsnorm_kernel` on `main` emits `arith.muli %row, %stride_x : i32` (PTX `mul.lo.s32`), and on this branch `arith.muli %row_1, %x : i64`. `_ple_gate_kernel` behaves the same way for `t * key_rs`, `t * value_rs` and `t * HC * H`.
- A CPU-interpreter run of each kernel at rows 209,715 / 209,716 / 262,143 (and 167,772 / 167,773 for the PLE gate), with Flash-Next-sized row strides, reads the row at the int32-wrapped offset on `main`. On this branch it reads the right row. The NVIDIA and AMD variants behave the same.
- Not run on a GPU, and performance was not measured. The change adds one int64 conversion per program. The AMD kernels get the identical one-line change but no ROCm test.

## Details

- `hc_silu`'s own row strides (336/320) stay below the limit at these sizes. It is widened anyway so that every kernel in the file follows one rule.
- The test is in a new file because `test_hc_ops.py` is CUDA-only at module level, and some of its bit-exact comparisons do not hold under the interpreter. The new file holds only stride-invariance checks. It is added to the `models_basic` test area.

commits.pr_title: [Pooling] Speed up ColBERT reranking with batched token heads
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Batch token-embedding casts and projections across requests, then finish slicing and normalization per request only when their settings differ. This removes repeated ColBERT head launches without adding kernels or GPU-specific tuning.

## Claims

- Higher ColBERT throughput with matching settings; mixed dimensions/normalization now also share projection.
- Late chunking, chunked prefill and batch-invariant execution retain the existing path and output ownership. This complements #62940's task-dispatch optimization.

## Validation

**Latest refactor, main → branch:** `answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1`, MRV2, BF16 backbone/FP32 head, TP1, eager. 32 documents plus a query per request, L128, C32, four API workers. H100 and B300 each used two fresh-server runs per variant in balanced order, 256 warmups and 4,096 timed requests/run; all **32,768 NVIDIA requests succeeded**. The MI355X row is from a separate AMD rerun and is not included in that request count. Values are per-metric medians.

| GPU | Requests/s | Gain | p50 ms | p99 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 138.26 → 193.91 | +40.2% | 228.87 → 163.23 | 289.60 → 217.28 |
| B300 | 181.62 → 242.00 | +33.2% | 172.12 → 129.61 | 208.45 → 155.49 |
| MI355X | 204.15 → 331.89 | +62.6% | 156.18 → 92.08 | 197.30 → 134.16 |

**Accuracy:** the latest code passes the existing ColBERT/HF comparison on H100. On H100 and B300, eight real-model requests mixing normalized and raw outputs match main, including norms (maximum absolute error **7.15e-7**). The 48 head cases on each of those two GPUs also cover mixed dimensions, late chunking, batch-invariant mode and buffer reuse (maximum absolute error **1.19e-6**, `atol=2e-6, rtol=1e-4`).

**Earlier SciFact evaluation (not rerun for this refactor):** BM25 top-50 reranking, 300 queries / 5,183 documents. HF FP32 reference: NDCG@10 **0.73519**, MRR@10 **0.71167**.

| GPU | NDCG@10, main → branch | MRR@10, main → branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| H100 | 0.73143 → 0.73143 | 0.70707 → 0.70707 |
| B300 | 0.73185 → 0.73185 | 0.70757 → 0.70757 |

## Details

**Tests:** 124 pooling/head/late-interaction cases pass on each of H100 and B300; local pre-commit checks also pass. Three compact CPU cases check projection count and output parity; the existing ownership test also covers an identity head. The previous PR implementation fails the two mixed-setting projection-count checks; the updated implementation passes. Four added cases overall, no new test file or CI job.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][LoRA][MoE] Use the shrink/expand kernels for MoE-LoRA batches of up to 64 tokens
commits.pr_body:
Diff: 3 files, +262 / -17.

This PR was split into a stack. Its earlier revisions (problem-sized configs, threshold 256, fp32 intermediate, removal of the small-batch kernel) moved to:

1. this PR: shrink/expand for batches of up to 64 tokens
2. #64746: problem-sized shrink/expand configs, threshold 256
3. #64747: fp32 intermediate, single output rounding
4. #64748: remove the small-batch kernel

## Purpose

For `max_lora_rank <= 128` and `fully_sharded=False`, `_fused_moe_lora` on main always uses the single-launch one-shot or small-batch kernel. Each program in them runs the whole K loop serially, so at decode the grid is a few dozen programs and the kernels run far below memory bandwidth. The existing `_fused_moe_lora_shrink` + `_fused_moe_lora_expand` path spreads the work over more programs.

## Changes

- Batches of up to `FUSED_MOE_LORA_TWO_KERNEL_MAX_TOKENS = 64` tokens use shrink/expand. Larger batches keep the one-shot / small-batch kernels. With the current default configs (from the base-MoE `get_default_config`), shrink/expand wins at every size up to 64 tokens and is mixed above, so the threshold is 64. #64746 raises it to 256 together with configs sized for the LoRA problem.
- TMA descriptors need 16-byte aligned strides. Shrink/expand now also runs small ranks, so TMA is used only when `max_lora_rank * element_size % 16 == 0` (rank 4 in bf16 would otherwise fail with `strides must be 16-byte aligned`).
- The TMA descriptor calls import `TensorDescriptor` where they use it. `import triton` does not load `triton.tools.tensor_descriptor`; on main it is only loaded as a side effect of other imports (in a server, `fused_moe/config.py` through `triton_kernels`). Once small batches reach these calls, `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` fails 18 cases with `AttributeError: module 'triton.tools' has no attribute 'tensor_descriptor'` after #64748.

## Kernel time

bf16, CUDA graph over N layers with distinct LoRA weights (at least 512 MB in total, so the weights do not stay in L2), the second-best of 7 timed trials, µs per call. "main" is e49ea84e9. E=128, top_k=4, hidden=6144, moe_intermediate=768, rank 32, max_loras 1:

| M | GB200 w13 main | GB200 w13 this PR | GB200 w2 main | GB200 w2 this PR | H200 w13 main | H200 w13 this PR | H200 w2 main | H200 w2 this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 72.2 | **18.9** | 14.2 | **6.0** | 60.1 | **25.8** | 13.5 | **7.0** |
| 2 | 72.1 | **19.7** | 14.5 | **6.8** | 78.0 | **30.4** | 16.7 | **8.7** |
| 4 | 104.0 | **23.3** | 19.6 | **9.1** | 95.3 | **49.7** | 20.3 | **14.1** |
| 8 | 56.5 | **26.4** | 40.9 | **13.3** | 54.1 | **30.7** | 43.5 | **14.8** |
| 16 | 84.1 | **28.8** | 59.5 | **19.8** | 70.0 | **38.0** | 63.3 | **21.9** |
| 32 | 89.2 | **35.5** | 113.4 | **31.0** | 79.4 | **59.8** | 114.5 | **35.4** |
| 64 | 99.5 | **49.2** | 133.6 | **38.4** | 90.5 | **77.2** | 159.1 | **32.4** |
| 96 | 107.6 | 107.6 | 135.0 | 135.0 | 91.1 | 91.5 | 160.7 | 160.1 |
| 256 | 87.3 | 87.5 | 124.9 | 124.9 | 109.1 | 109.3 | 164.1 | 164.9 |

Over 5 MoE shapes (the one above, Qwen3-30B-A3B, OLMoE, Mixtral TP8, DeepSeek-V3 TP8) x rank 8/16/32/64 x max_loras 1/4 x w13/w2 (80 problems per M), geomean speedup over main of this PR's kernel path (measured on the previous head 389e07498, which has the same dispatch and kernels):

| M | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB200 | 2.10x | 2.23x | 2.41x | 2.53x | 2.51x | 2.20x | 2.00x |
| H200 | 2.04x | 2.02x | 1.96x | 2.27x | 2.08x | 1.84x | 1.86x |

## Accuracy

Kernel level, max |out - ref| / max |ref| against an fp64 reference, divided by the error from rounding the fp64 result to bf16 (1.0 = exact up to output rounding), 80 problems x M 1-64 on GB200: main 1.171 geomean / 2.163 max, this PR 1.289 / 2.163. Shrink/expand rounds the rank-sized intermediate to bf16, which the small-batch kernel did not; #64747 removes that rounding.

Model level, OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct with `jeeejeee/olmoe-instruct-text2sql-spider`, 6147 teacher-forced tokens scored with `max_num_batched_tokens=64` (every forward goes through shrink/expand), mean |Δ logprob| against an fp32 HF reference: GB200 main 0.0624 / this PR 0.0635, H200 0.0574 / 0.0576. This PR differs from main by 0.0165 / 0.0125 nats mean, the same as two runs of main differ from each other (0.0164 / 0.0151). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the logprobs are bit-identical to main. Full setup and tables are in #64747.

## Test Plan

- `test_fused_moe_lora_token_threshold_dispatch`: 23 shapes (naive and sorted assignment, top_k 1-8, rank 4-128, bf16/fp16, w13- and w2-like shapes, split-K 4) check the path chosen on each side of the threshold and the result against a torch reference. `m16-topk1-r4-naive` covers the TMA alignment check.
- `test_fused_moe_lora_expert_parallel`: shrink/expand and one-shot with an `expert_map`; non-local experts must leave the output unchanged.
- The early-exit and zero-grid tests now run on both paths. The NPID and bad-`BLOCK_SIZE_M` tests use more than 64 tokens so they still reach the one-shot kernel.

## Test Result

- `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` on 1 GPU: 451 passed, 12 skipped (GB200 and H200). With the whole stack (#64748): 468 passed, 12 skipped; without the import change, 18 of them fail.
- The new and changed tests on the parent with only the 64-token constant added: 22 failed, 21 passed (every dispatch assertion below the threshold fails). Without the TMA alignment check, `m16-topk1-r4-naive` fails with `AssertionError: strides must be 16-byte aligned`.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` (0.14.0) clean; mypy reports no new errors on the changed files.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Parse closed Qwen3 tool parameters once while streaming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A Qwen3 XML tool call that repeats closed parameters makes `_qwen3_arg_converter` re-scan every parameter on each streaming conversion, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call until the event loop saturates and liveness fails. This parses each closed parameter once. It is the Qwen3 counterpart of #64535 (GLM) and covers every parser on the Qwen3 converter: `qwen3_coder`, Nemotron-3, Step-3.5, Step5, Seed-OSS, MiniCPM-V and Granite thinking.

## Claims

- Streaming a call with N closed parameters matches the parameter regex N times in total. On main every conversion matches all closed parameters again and the value extender scans them twice more: 2,051,331 matches for N = 401 in the new test.
- Streamed deltas and non-streaming results are unchanged.
- For a call looping on two parameters, the cost per 4-token engine step at 64K output chars drops from 6.4 ms to 92 us, and a replay at 200 tok/s no longer fails liveness (main: killed at 335 s).
- On a real server (Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, one H200), that loop to 256K chars keeps the API server 100% busy on main from 148 s, and `/health` answers no probe within 10 s for the last 150 s of the stream. With this PR the API server is 7% busy and `/health` p99 is 0.9 ms.
- No new config, flag or API. `MiMoParser` keeps its own converter and is unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py::TestArgValueExtender::test_closed_params_are_parsed_once` | `AssertionError: assert 2051331 == 401` | passed |
| Qwen3 parser tests | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py` | 84 passed, 2 failed (the new tests) | 86 passed |
| Parser suite | `pytest tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | 6570 passed, 93 errors | 6574 passed, 93 errors (same set) |
| Files that need Hugging Face | `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_step3p5_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py` | 427 passed | 427 passed |
| Resumed parse against main (below) | random argument texts grown piece by piece, two calls sharing one cache | | 0 mismatches in 700,709 growth steps |
| Streaming equivalence (below) | Qwen3 tokenizer, `qwen3_coder` + `nemotron_v3`, `parse_delta` at chunk sizes 1, 3, 4, 7, 64, plus `parse` | | 114 of 114 records identical |
| Cost per step (below) | parameter loop, through `OutputProcessor` and `chat_completion_stream_generator` | 1741 us at 16K chars, 6435 us at 64K | 57 us at 16K chars, 92 us at 64K |
| Looping stream replay (below) | 200 tok/s, liveness 30 s / 5 s / 3 | liveness kill at 335 s | no kill in 1200 s, loop 10% busy at 240K tokens |
| Server run (below) | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on one H200, forced parameter loop to 256K chars | API server 394.8 s CPU (90% busy), 16 `/health` timeouts of 10 s | 26.8 s (7%), `/health` p99 0.90 ms, no timeout |

Unit tests, equivalence and replays ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The 93 parser-suite errors are the same set on both: 70 in the three files that need Hugging Face access (the fifth row, run with access), and 23 in `tests/parser/mistral/test_reasoning.py`, which fails the same on main with the image's mistral-common. `ruff`, the repo's `mypy` hook and the CI-wiring hook pass.

CI coverage: `tests/parser` jobs are disabled since #63609, so CI will run the new tests once that job is back.

<details>
<summary>Resumed parse against main</summary>

Each case builds two calls' raw arguments from fragments: whole and split `<parameter=...>` openers, `</parameter>` and `< / parameter >` closers with prefixes of both, repeated names, newlines, `>`, `=`, non-ASCII and value text. Each call grows in random 1-9 char pieces through one shared cache. After every piece, the converter with the cache must return main's `_qwen3_arg_converter` output for `partial=True` and `partial=False`, and the extender must be `None` exactly when main's is and then stream the same text for every later piece. Seeds 1-3, 4,000 cases each.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Streaming equivalence</summary>

Each output is tokenized with the Qwen3 tokenizer and streamed as token-id chunks through `ParserManager.get_parser("qwen3_coder", "nemotron_v3")`. Every delta's content, reasoning, tool-call name and arguments are recorded, plus one non-streaming `parse`. The outputs: content, CJK content, reasoning, an open Python, HTML and CJK value, a parameter loop, a call loop, an open JSON array, a long value under a repeated name, and 9 repeated-name cases (a different, identical, extending or prefix value, a repeat that is not last, a third occurrence restoring the first value, another name after the repeat, an unclosed repeat, a second call).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cost per step and looping stream replay</summary>

The stream is `<tool_call>\n<function=Edit>\n` followed by `<parameter=old_string>\ntotal = 0\n</parameter>\n<parameter=new_string>\ntotal = 1\n</parameter>\n` repeated, with the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer. Cost is the endpoint's time per 4-token engine step (`chat_completion_stream_generator` with `qwen3_coder` and `nemotron_v3`, prompt with reasoning closed).

| Output chars | 1K | 4K | 16K | 64K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 127 us | 642 us | 1741 us | 6435 us |
| This PR | 56 us | 51 us | 57 us | 92 us |

The replay feeds the same stream through the streaming parser on a virtual clock: 200 tokens/s in 4-token steps, one `parse_delta` per event-loop pass for every token emitted since the previous pass, measured parser time doubled for a slower server CPU, and kubelet liveness (30 s period, 5 s timeout, 3 failures) replayed on those passes.

| Stream time | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 60 s, 12K tokens | loop 48% busy | 1% |
| 120 s, 24K tokens | 92% | 1% |
| 210-330 s | liveness fails 3 of 3 (12-70 s waits), kill at 335 s | 2-3%, no probe failure |
| 1200 s, 240K tokens, 818K chars | | 10% |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server run</summary>

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --enable-auto-tool-choice` from the CUDA CI image of main `8084f0624d`, one H200 per server, Model Runner V2, no speculative decoding. The PR server runs the same image with `vllm/parser/qwen3.py` first on `PYTHONPATH`. A test logits processor forces the token ids of the cost-per-step stream, closed with `</function></tool_call>`, at temperature 0, so both servers generate the same output; weights, engine, detokenizer, parser and HTTP server are real. The client streams `/v1/chat/completions` with an `Edit` tool, probes `/health` every 0.5 s with a 10 s timeout and samples the API server process's CPU time.

| Run | main: API-server CPU, busy, `/health` p99, timeouts, stream time | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Forced, 64K chars (18,804 tokens) | 41.8 s, 49%, 11.4 ms, 0, 86 s | 4.0 s, 5%, 0.90 ms, 0, 86 s |
| Forced, 256K chars (75,153 tokens) | 394.8 s, 90%, 10 s, 16, 440 s | 26.8 s, 7%, 0.90 ms, 0, 389 s |
| Forced, 64K chars, 8 streams at once | 185.1 s, 96%, 10 s, 12, 193 s | 17.5 s, 13%, 1.8 ms, 0, 132 s |
| Unforced `Write` of a Python module | 0.86 s, 4%, 0.76 ms, 0, 20 s | 0.90 s, 5%, 0.72 ms, 0, 20 s |

- On main at 256K chars, the API server is 100% busy from 148 s. `/health` takes over 1 s from 216 s, and from 287 s until the stream ends at 437 s no probe answers within 10 s. A kubelet liveness probe with a 30 s period, 5 s timeout and 3 failures would restart the container by about 380 s, before the call finishes. With 8 streams at 64K chars, no probe answers from 68 s to the end at 193 s.
- The load also slows the streams on main: 440 s against 389 s at 256K chars, and 193 s against 132 s for the 8 streams.
- Streamed arguments are identical between the two servers in every run, and across the 8 streams. The unforced run's arguments parse as JSON on both.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` converts the whole raw argument text whenever the open-value extender is inactive: between parameters, and while the open parameter repeats an earlier name (the extender needs the open value to be the last JSON value). Qwen3 sets no `arg_structural_chars`, so every argument delta in those states converts.
- `_qwen3_arg_converter` runs `_PARAM_RE.finditer` over every closed parameter, then `_PARAM_RE.sub` over the whole text to find the open one. After each conversion that extends the streamed JSON, `_param_value_extender` runs both again.
- A model looping on closed parameters keeps every delta in those states, so the cost per delta is linear in the call and the total is quadratic. Merging deltas under load does not bound it, because each merged pass converts the whole text again.

**Change.**
- `_qwen3_parse_params` takes an optional `_ClosedParams` cache, and `Qwen3Parser` binds one per instance into its converter and extender after `super().__init__`, as `Glm47MoeParser` does since #64535. A text that starts with the cached text resumes after the last closed parameter. Any other text parses from the start, and the cache moves forward whenever a scan closes a new parameter.
- A Qwen3 value also closes where the next `<parameter=` begins (the lookahead in `_PARAM_RE`), and holds only while that opener follows. So the cached text runs through that opener, and the scan resumes at the end of the value. Appending text cannot change a parameter closed within the cached text, so resuming is exact. `test_value_closed_by_next_parameter_needs_that_parameter` covers a text that shares the prefix but not the opener.
- The extender's repeated-name check uses the closed names from the same parse in place of a second `finditer`.
- A parser built with a custom `arg_converter` keeps the uncached path (identity check in `__init__`), as in #64535.

**Cost.** What stays linear in the text per conversion is C-level work: `startswith` against the cached text, the join of text outside the parameters for the open-parameter search, and the engine's own argument concatenation. That is the 10% busy at 818K chars in the replay.

**Not in this PR.** #64535 also set `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` for GLM, on the argument that a delta without `>` cannot close a key or value. That does not hold for Qwen3, where a value closes at `<parameter=` before any `>`, and the cache alone passes the replay. Measured with the gate added: 39 us per step at 64K chars for the parameter loop, and 385 us against 1247 us for many distinct parameters.

**Unchanged here and the same on main.**
- Many distinct parameters in one call: each conversion still serializes every parameter, so the cost per step grows with their number (1.2 ms at 64K chars, against 6.2 ms on main).
- A long value under a repeated name: `_param_value_extender` refuses any repeated name, so each delta converts the whole value (11.7 ms per step at 64K chars, against 17.6 ms on main). Letting it accept a repeated last name, as GLM's extender does, is a separate change.
- `MiMoParser` keeps its own converter with the full scan.

**Not a duplicate.** #55497 (open) narrows the parameter-name group of `_PARAM_RE` and `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE`; the cache works with either pattern and the overlap is textual. #59821 (open) edits `Qwen3Parser.__init__` for tool markup in reasoning; whichever lands second rebases. #63277 (open) changes zero-argument calls in the tool adapter. No open PR covers re-parsing closed Qwen3 parameters.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the analysis, the change, the tests and this description.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Parser] Skip tool-argument conversions after a replaced value
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a tool call repeats a key whose value was already streamed, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` fails the prefix check before it installs the argument value extender. Every later delta then re-converts the whole argument text, only to fail the same check, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call. This installs the extender with streaming off on that failure. Follow-up to #61253 and #64535.

## Claims

- On GLM-4.7/GLM-5.x, a long value written under a repeated key costs 15.1 us per engine step at 66K output chars, against 2514 us on main. From 64K to 256K chars the mean is 17.3 us against 6.16 ms.
- On a real server (GLM-4.7-Flash, one H200), streaming that call to 256K chars costs the API server 14 s of CPU against 215 s on main, and `/health` p99 stays at 0.8 ms against 17.9 ms.
- Streamed arguments are unchanged in every case checked, and so are non-streaming results. One case groups deltas differently: a repeated key whose new value starts with the text already streamed for the old value. It streams the rest of the value when the value closes, while main streams it at the next delta containing `>`.
- The change is in `engine/` because the wasted conversion follows any failed prefix check, whatever the parser. Only GLM's extender accepts a value under a repeated key today, so Qwen3 and DSML streams are unchanged (see Details).
- No new config, flag or API.

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py::TestStreamedToolArguments::test_replaced_value_conversions_do_not_grow` | `AssertionError: assert 135 == 1215` | passed |
| Parser suite | `pytest tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | 6570 passed, 93 errors | 6571 passed, 93 errors (same set) |
| Errored files, with Hugging Face access | `pytest tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py` | 71 passed | 71 passed |
| Streaming equivalence (below) | real tokenizers, `parse_delta` at chunk sizes 1, 3, 4, 7, 64, plus `parse` | | 343 of 348 records identical; 5 differ in grouping only, arguments identical in all 348 |
| Cost per step (below) | GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `glm47` + `glm45`, through `OutputProcessor` and `chat_completion_stream_generator` | 2514 us at 66K chars | 15.1 us |
| Server run (below) | GLM-4.7-Flash on one H200, forced repeated-key stream to 256K chars | API server 214.7 s CPU (33% busy), `/health` p99 17.9 ms | 14.1 s (2%), p99 0.83 ms |

Tests ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. Of the 93 errors, 70 are the three files in the third row, which need Hugging Face access the first run did not have. The other 23 are in `tests/parser/mistral/test_reasoning.py`, which fails the same on main with the image's mistral-common. `ruff`, the repo's `mypy` hook and the CI-wiring hook pass.

CI coverage: `tests/parser` jobs are disabled since #63609, and `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py` is on the tethering allowlist with them, so CI will run the new test once that job is back.

<details>
<summary>Streaming equivalence</summary>

Each output is tokenized with the model's real tokenizer and streamed as token-id chunks through `ParserManager.get_parser(...)`. Every delta's content, reasoning, tool-call name and arguments are recorded, plus one non-streaming `parse`. The outputs cover every case shape below for each family, plus 9 repeated-key cases: a different new value, an identical value, a new value that extends the old one, a new value that is a prefix of the old one, a repeated key that is not the last key, a third occurrence that restores the first value, another key after the repeat, an unclosed repeat, and a second call.

| Parsers (tokenizer) | Records | Identical | Grouping differs, arguments identical |
|---|---|---|---|
| `glm47` + `glm45` (GLM-5.3) | 120 | 115 | 5 (`dup-last-extends-old` at all 5 chunk sizes: 112 deltas to 13 at size 1) |
| `deepseek_v41` + `deepseek_v41` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) | 114 | 114 | 0 |
| `qwen3_coder` + `nemotron_v3` (Qwen3) | 114 | 114 | 0 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cost per step</summary>

`Write` with `file_path`, `content` set to `x`, then `content` again holding a long HTML file, streamed in 4-token engine steps. The cost is the endpoint's per-step time (`chat_completion_stream_generator` with the `glm47` tool parser), mean of the 195 steps at each mark.

| Output chars | 3K | 6K | 18K | 66K | 66K-256K mean | Whole stream (94K tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 94.5 us | 210 us | 662 us | 2514 us | 6165 us | 116 s |
| This PR | 13.9 us | 13.5 us | 13.7 us | 15.1 us | 17.3 us | 0.8 s |

Both stream the same 7 frames (1,867 bytes).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server run</summary>

`vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice` from the CUDA CI image of main `8084f0624d`, one H200 per server, Model Runner V2, no speculative decoding. The PR server runs the same image with the changed file first on `PYTHONPATH`. A test logits processor forces the token ids of the cost-per-step stream at temperature 0, so both servers generate the same output; weights, engine, detokenizer, parsers and HTTP server are real. The client streams `/v1/chat/completions`, probes `/health` every 0.5 s and samples the API server process's CPU time.

| Run | Output | main: API-server CPU, busy, `/health` p99 / max | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forced, 64K chars | 23,464 tokens in 130 s | 16.1 s, 12%, 4.1 / 4.2 ms | 3.3 s, 2%, 0.78 / 0.91 ms |
| Forced, 256K chars | 93,963 tokens in 648 s | 214.7 s, 33%, 17.9 / 38.0 ms | 14.1 s, 2%, 0.83 / 2.1 ms |
| Forced, 64K chars, 8 streams at once | 8 x 23,464 tokens in 175 s | 109.7 s, 63%, 38.1 / 39.9 ms | 8.2 s, 5%, 0.82 / 1.0 ms |
| Unforced `Write` of an HTML page, thinking off | 41,649 argument chars in 45 s | 1.9 s, 4% | 2.0 s, 4% |

- Streamed arguments are identical between the two servers in every run, and across the 8 streams. The forced runs end at `{"file_path": "/repo/a.html", "content": "x` on both, the flush truncation under Details. The unforced run streams in 8,473 events on both, and its streamed arguments parse as JSON.
- No `/health` probe failed on either server.
- GLM-5.3 itself needs 8 GPUs per server and was not run. GLM-4.7-Flash uses the same `glm47` and `glm45` parsers.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.**
- A model that repeats a key replaces that key's value in the converted JSON. The JSON then stops extending `slot.streamed_json`, so `_compute_arg_delta` returns at `if prev and not safe_json.startswith(prev)`. That return comes before `slot.extend_open_value` is set.
- GLM sets `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, so every later delta containing `>` runs `arg_converter`, `_fix_arg_types` and `_safe_arg_prefix` over the whole argument text, then fails the same check.
- HTML, JSX and most code put a `>` in nearly every engine step. So the cost per step is linear in the argument and the total is quadratic. Merging deltas under load caps it near one conversion per pass, so on its own this saturates the event loop without failing liveness (replayed on `f4efba72e6`, which has the same path).

**Change.**
- On that failure, set `slot.extend_open_value` from `self._arg_value_extender(slot.args)` and set `slot.open_value_streams = False`. The existing branch at the top of `_compute_arg_delta` then returns `None` for a delta that only extends the open value, without converting.
- The extender returns `None` at the value's closing tag. The next delta then converts, and streaming resumes if the JSON extends `streamed_json` again. The final flush converts the full text as before.
- A delta that only extends the new value can make the JSON extend `streamed_json` again only when the new value starts with the text already streamed for the old one. That is the grouping difference in the equivalence table.

**Which parsers.** The change applies to every parser with an `arg_value_extender`. GLM's extender accepts an open value under a repeated key when that key is the last one. `_param_value_extender` (Qwen3) and `_dsml_arg_value_extender` (DeepSeek V3.2/V4) return `None` for any repeated key, so for them this installs nothing. On main they still pay a conversion per delta for a long value under a repeated key: 5.5 ms per step at 64K chars for `deepseek_v41` and 29.6 ms for `qwen3_coder`. Replayed at a production pod's measured API-server load, the `deepseek_v41` stream fails liveness and is killed at 335 s. Letting those extenders accept a repeated last key, as GLM's does, would be one follow-up per parser.

**Unchanged here and the same on main.** When the repeated key closes with a value that does not extend what was streamed, the flush withholds the final JSON, so the client gets truncated arguments. #53739 (open) addresses that flush.

**Not a duplicate.** #63385 (open) rewrites this block of `_compute_arg_delta` for incremental type repair and keeps the same early return on a failed prefix check. The overlap is textual, and whichever lands second rebases. #53739 (open) changes the flush fallback. #64196 (open) and #58780 (merged) cover DSML open values, and #61253 and #64535 (merged) cover GLM open values and closed pairs. No open PR covers conversions after a failed prefix check.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the analysis, the change, the tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Reject Anthropic-defined tools by type in /v1/messages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/messages` rejects Anthropic-defined tools (`web_search_20250305`, `bash_20250124`, ...) with `input_schema: Field required`. This changes the 400 to name the unsupported tool type instead.

Tracking: #64810. Related: #46790 (Claude Code's WebSearch fails against vLLM). Alternative to #46797, which accepts these tools and drops them; see Details.

## Claims

- A request with an Anthropic-defined tool gets one 400 error: `tool type 'web_search_20250305' is not supported; only custom tools with an input_schema are supported`.
- Custom tools are unchanged, with or without an explicit `"type": "custom"`, and they still require `input_schema`.

## Validation

New unit tests in `TestToolDefinitions`, run on the base `protocol.py` and with this fix (macOS, CPU-only):

```
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestToolDefinitions
# base
E       assert "'web_search_20250305' is not supported" in 'Field required'
E       assert "'bash_20250124' is not supported" in 'Field required'
2 failed, 3 passed
# this PR
5 passed
```

The full `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` run gives 132 passed and 3 failed. The 3 failures are `TestDetectMergeInlineSystem::test_probes_non_jinja_renderer[deepseek-*]` (`Failed to infer device type`), and they fail the same way on base on a machine with no accelerator.

The response through the real Anthropic router (FastAPI `TestClient` with `attach_router` and the validation exception handler):

```
400 {"error":{"message":"1 validation error:\n  {'type': 'value_error', 'loc': 'body.tools.0', 'msg': \"Value error, tool type 'web_search_20250305' is not supported; only custom tools with an input_schema are supported\", ...
```

`test_messages.py::test_anthropic_server_tool_is_rejected` sends the same request end to end with the Anthropic SDK through `RemoteOpenAIServer`. **I have not run that test locally (no GPU here); it runs in the existing `entrypoints/anthropic` CI step.**

## Details

**Root cause.** `AnthropicTool` models only custom tools: `input_schema` is required and there is no `type` field. Anthropic-defined tools carry a versioned `type` and no `input_schema`, so pydantic reported the missing field. A `mode="before"` validator now rejects any `type` other than `custom` before field validation runs, so the error the client sees is about the tool type.

**Why reject instead of dropping the tool (#46797).** The Anthropic API never drops a server tool it can't run:
- With web search disabled for the org, it returns `400 invalid_request_error` saying web search is not enabled, not an error inside a search result ([docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool)).
- Bedrock lists server tools as unsupported ([docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock#features-not-supported)) and reports `ValidationException: tool type 'web_search_20250305' is not supported for this model`.

If vLLM drops the tool, a client that asked for search gets an answer from training data with no error and no citations. #46797 also drops `bash_*` and `text_editor_*`. Those are Anthropic-defined *client* tools: the client runs them, and Bedrock supports them. Dropping them means the model can never call a tool the client is waiting to run.

**Limitations / follow-ups**
- Supporting Anthropic-defined client tools (`bash_*`, `text_editor_*`, `memory_*`) properly would mean supplying their built-in schemas to the chat template. That's a feature, left for a separate PR; until then they get the same named 400.
- Request-body validation errors on `/v1/messages` still use the shared OpenAI-style envelope (`"type": "Bad Request"`) rather than Anthropic's `{"type": "error", "error": {"type": "invalid_request_error", ...}}`. That is pre-existing and not changed here.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Decode streamed custom-tool input incrementally
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

For a Responses `custom` tool, every streamed argument delta re-runs `partial_json_parser` over the whole accumulated arguments, so the API server's cost per delta grows with the tool input. This decodes only the new tail of the input string. Follow-up to #57322.

## Claims

- Cost per streamed delta at 64K chars of tool input drops from 1.59 ms to 4.3 us, and at 256K chars from 14.9 ms to 11.4 us.
- On a real server (GLM-4.7-Flash, one H200), streaming a 256K-char `apply_patch` input over `/v1/responses` costs the API server 22 s of CPU against 563 s on main, and `/health` p99 stays at 0.9 ms against 42.8 ms.
- Streamed `response.custom_tool_call_input.delta` events are unchanged. After every delta the streamed payload equals `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix` of the arguments so far.
- Arguments that do not start the way `encode_custom_tool_input` writes them (`{"input": "`) keep the full decode, as does every delta after the payload string closes.
- No API, event or config change. Scope is non-Harmony Responses streaming (`responses/streaming_events.py`, `responses/utils.py`).

## Validation

| Check | Command | main `8084f0624d` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cost test | `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_streaming_events.py::TestCustomToolStreaming::test_payload_deltas_do_not_reparse_the_input` | `AssertionError: assert 44 == 404` | passed |
| New equivalence test | `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_streaming_events.py::TestCustomToolStreaming::test_streamed_payload_matches_prefix_decode` | passed | passed |
| Responses tests | `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses` | 313 passed, 85 errors | 316 passed, 85 errors (same set) |
| Fuzz (below) | 12,000 random inputs, 7 argument forms, random delta sizes | | 0 mismatches in 251,923 deltas |
| Server run (below) | GLM-4.7-Flash on one H200, forced `apply_patch` call to 256K chars, `/v1/responses` | API server 563.2 s CPU (88% busy), `/health` p99 42.8 ms | 22.2 s (3%), p99 0.86 ms |

Cost per `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` call, a patch streamed in 12-char deltas (one 4-token engine step):

| Tool input | 1K chars | 4K | 16K | 64K | 256K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 23.7 us | 80.8 us | 328 us | 1588 us | 14899 us |
| This PR | 3.9 us | 2.4 us | 2.5 us | 4.3 us | 11.4 us |

Tests and measurements ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:074c83a09a0b872cec92e244d91adf2b3c55e41b-arm64-cpu` with the branch tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The 85 errors are server tests that download models; the container has no Hugging Face access, and they fail the same on main. `ruff` and the repo's `mypy` hook pass on the changed files.

<details>
<summary>Fuzz</summary>

Each input is a random payload (quotes, backslashes, control characters, `\x85`, `\u3000`, CJK, emoji, ZWJ sequences), encoded with `ensure_ascii` on or off in one of 7 forms: the canonical shim, compact separators, `input` after another key, `input` before another key, raw unescaped text after the head, an invalid `\U` escape, and a dangling high surrogate before the close. The arguments go through `emit_simple_tool_call_open` and `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` in deltas of 1 to 64 chars. After every delta, `state.tool_call_payload` is compared with `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix(state.accumulated_text)`. Seeds 1-3, 4,000 inputs each: 251,923 deltas, 122,443 of them on the incremental path, 0 mismatches.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server run</summary>

`vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice` from the CUDA CI image of main `8084f0624d`, one H200 per server, Model Runner V2, no speculative decoding. The PR server runs the same image with the two changed files first on `PYTHONPATH`. The request is a streaming `/v1/responses` call with a `custom` tool `apply_patch`. A test logits processor forces the token ids of an `apply_patch` call carrying a patch at temperature 0, so both servers generate the same output; weights, engine, detokenizer, parsers and HTTP server are real. The client probes `/health` every 0.5 s and samples the API server process's CPU time.

| Run | Output | main: API-server CPU, busy, `/health` p99 / max | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forced, 64K chars | 23,290 tokens in 130 s | 53.7 s, 41%, 4.6 / 4.9 ms | 5.3 s, 4%, 0.86 / 1.5 ms |
| Forced, 256K chars | 93,110 tokens in 640 s | 563.2 s, 88%, 42.8 / 73.7 ms | 22.2 s, 3%, 0.86 / 1.3 ms |
| Forced, 64K chars, 8 streams at once | 8 x 23,290 tokens in 174 s | 157.4 s, 90%, 44.5 / 70.6 ms | 15.9 s, 9%, 1.3 / 1.6 ms |
| Unforced `apply_patch` of a new module, cut at 16,000 output tokens | 86 s | 40.1 s, 47%, 5.2 / 5.7 ms | 3.4 s, 4%, 0.85 / 0.86 ms |

- In every forced run, on both servers, the concatenated `response.custom_tool_call_input.delta` text equals the `done` input and the final item's input, and equals the forced patch exactly (64,014 and 256,014 chars), across the 8 streams too.
- The event count differs under load: main merges more tokens per event (51,406 events against 82,769 at 256K chars) because its event loop is busy. The streamed text is identical.
- The unforced run streams the same text on both servers. It ends at the token limit, inside the call; see Details.
- No `/health` probe failed on either server.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` appends each delta to `state.accumulated_text` and calls `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix` on all of it. That runs `partial_json_parser.loads`, which strips and completes the whole text in Python on every call. Cost per delta is linear in the input and the total is quadratic. Custom tools carry freeform input such as patches, so long inputs are the normal case for Codex-style clients.

**Change.**
- `extend_custom_tool_input_prefix` returns the same payload as `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix`, decoding only the arguments after the end of the previous call. It matches `partial_json_parser` on a partial string:
  - it decodes up to the last complete escape;
  - it holds back a trailing high-surrogate escape, so a pair is never split between calls;
  - it holds back trailing whitespace, which `partial_json_parser` strips before completing the string.
- When the tail does not decode as a JSON string body (the closing quote, a raw control character, an invalid escape), it returns `None`. The state then uses `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix` for the rest of the call.
- `SimpleStreamingState.tool_call_payload_end` records where decoding stopped, or -1 after the fallback. `tool_call_payload` already holds the decoded payload, since `_emit_custom_tool_input_delta` stores every payload it gets.

**Cost.** The work that stays linear in the input on each delta is C-level: `accumulated_text +=`, `payload + chunk` and the `startswith` in `_emit_custom_tool_input_delta`. That is the 11.4 us at 256K chars.

**Limitations.** Arguments in another form keep the full decode on every delta. The shim arguments come from the tool parsers' `json.dumps`, which writes the canonical head.

**Unchanged here and the same on main.** A call cut off by `max_output_tokens` leaves the shim JSON unclosed. `decode_custom_tool_input` then returns the raw arguments, so `emit_simple_tool_call_done` resends them in full as a last delta, and the `done` event and the output item carry the raw JSON. In the unforced server run, both servers stream 106,815 decoded chars followed by the 109,606-char raw `{"input": "...` text. That is a separate fix.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for `decode_custom_tool_input_prefix`, `emit_simple_tool_call_delta` and Responses custom-tool streaming. #56418 (open) changes custom-tool naming for namespaces and leaves the streaming decode as is. #56285 (open, inactive since 2026-09-18) is the original that #57322 split out.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used for the analysis, the change, the tests and this description.
