commits.pr_title: [Feature] Default EPLB num_redundant_experts to minimum valid value
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

EPLB requires enough physical experts for every expert-parallel rank. This PR
lets `num_redundant_experts` default to `None`, then normalizes it during
`VllmConfig` initialization to the minimum non-negative value that makes the
total number of physical experts divisible by the effective EP size.

## Changes

- default `EPLBConfig.num_redundant_experts` to `None`
- compute the effective EP size as `TP × PCP × DP`
- compute the default as:

  ```text
  (ep_size - num_logical_experts % ep_size) % ep_size
  ```

- normalize disabled EPLB to zero while preserving explicit non-negative values
- reject explicitly negative values
- keep downstream consumers typed against the post-initialization `int` invariant

## Tests

- EPLB enabled with the omitted default
- EPLB disabled normalization
- explicit values remain unchanged
- negative-value validation
- TP / PCP / DP combinations, including PCP values greater than one
- focused Ruff and mypy validation for the touched configuration contract

The full Python 3.10–3.13 pre-commit matrix, DCO, and Buildkite checks on the
current PR head are the final verification gates.

## Scope and provenance

- Fixes #30075.
- GitHub search and the issue history identify this as the only open PR covering
  #30075; maintainers closed the competing duplicates in favor of this PR.
- AI assistance was used to inspect reviewer feedback, verify the Pydantic/mypy
  boundary, and run the focused checks. The amended commit records that
  assistance with an `Assisted-by` trailer.
- Model evaluation is not applicable because this changes configuration
  normalization only; it does not change kernels, model weights, or inference
  outputs.

commits.pr_title: [Config] Move V2-only checks into V1 model runner unsupported features
commits.pr_body:
use_v2_model_runner special-cased HiSparse, custom speculative methods and watermarking to force Model Runner V2. These are just features the V1 model runner doesn't support, so list them in
_get_v1_model_runner_unsupported_features() alongside the other V2-only features and let _validate_v1_model_runner() reject them.

Since V2 is already the default, use_v2_model_runner no longer needs to inspect them. The behavior change is that watermarking with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 now raises instead of silently overriding the env var, consistent with the other V2-only features.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Step-5-Preview support on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

ROCm support for [stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview](https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview), complementing the NVIDIA support added in #61727. This PR adds a self-contained amd/ implementation under vllm/models/step5/ and moves the platform-independent Step-5 sparse-attention code from nvidia/ to common/.

The primary support and validation target is **MI300X/MI325X (gfx942)**. **MI355X (gfx950)** is also supported and has secondary validation from [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith).

## Claims

- Step-5-Preview FP8 weights serve at TP8 on ROCm with text and image input.
- Compressed sparse attention (CSA) runs on the 23 sparse layers for prefill, chunked prefill, decode, and MTP verification.
- The main paged K/V cache uses ROCm AITER unified attention. The sparse summary cache, speculative tail ring, region scoring, and split-K decode code are shared with the NVIDIA Step-5 path.
- Sparse layers support the default BF16 K/V cache and FP8 E4M3 K/V. FP8 K/V requires `--block-size 32`.
- Three-token MTP works through the Step-3.5 MTP proposer with comparable accuracy and about 2.3x speedup in the earlier GSM8K run.
- Prefix caching and P/D disaggregation are supported. NIXL and Mooncake keep compressed summary pages whole and reject unsupported page splitting.
- CSA uses the existing KV-cache lifecycle and does not require scheduler changes or GPU-to-CPU synchronization.

### Serving command (ROCm, MTP enabled)

<details>
<summary>Serve Step-5-Preview on 8x MI300X</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --reasoning-parser step5 \
  --tool-call-parser step5 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

| Flag | Why |
|---|---|
| `--moe-backend triton` | Required. Every MoE layer clamps SwiGLU at 7, and AITER's block-FP8 MoE does not apply that clamp yet. |
| `--mm-encoder-*`, `--limit-mm-per-prompt` | Image input through the perception-encoder tower. |
| Default K/V dtype | BF16 sparse K/V. |
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 32` | Optional FP8 E4M3 sparse K/V. |

</details>

### How this fits with #61727

| | #61727 (NVIDIA) | This PR (ROCm) |
|---|---|---|
| Platforms | SM90, SM103 | gfx942 primary; gfx950 secondary |
| Main paged attention | NVIDIA backends | ROCm AITER unified attention |
| Sparse state | Summary cache + speculative tail ring | Same cache contracts |
| Region scoring / decode | Triton and FlashInfer adapters | Shared Triton scoring and split-K decode |
| Indexer Q/W | Sharded by provider group | Sharded by provider group |
| MTP | Yes | Yes, through the Step-3.5 MTP proposer |
| Parsers | `step5` | `step5` |

Like nvidia/, amd/ imports nothing from the other platform and does not use or change model_executor/models/step3p5*; nvidia/ changes are import paths only.

## Validation

### Primary: gfx942

**Model setup:** 8x MI300X, TP8, `max-model-len 32768`, vLLM ROCm nightly `3f1bcfd82` with this branch applied.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, full 1319, 5-shot chat (earlier revision) | 97.2%; 97.4% with MTP |
| GSM8K, 200-question sample, MTP (final model revision) | 96.0% |
| Needle in a haystack, 4K / 16K / 30K, 3 depths, 3 trials | 27/27 |
| Image input: shapes, counting, reading text | 3/3 correct |
| Prefix caching, shared ~22K-token prefix | 66% of prompt tokens from cache; answers correct |
| MTP acceptance, 3 draft tokens (earlier revision) | Mean acceptance length 3.1 to 3.3 |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, long chunked prefill + 15 concurrent decodes | No syncs |
| Prefill, 26K-token prompt | TTFT 2.7 s |
| `step5` parsers, stream and non-stream | Pass |
| `tests/models/test_initialization.py` | Pass |

The latest focused tests were also run on MI325X (gfx942). They cover gated four-token MTP verification, short-history decode, true nonzero-offset chunked prefill, equal-length prefill versus decode metadata, scored-prefill warmup discovery, and compressed-page checks through the real NIXL and Mooncake connector constructors.

### Secondary: gfx950

Validation by [@jamesETsmith](https://github.com/jamesETsmith):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 | 96.97% strict / 97.27% flexible; 96.59% / 97.04% with MTP |
| GPQA-Diamond, 198-question, zero-shot CoT | 85.86% (170/198); 85.35% (169/198) with MTP, raw lower bounds with a 16K generation budget |
| RULER-style single-key and multikey-2/3 NIAH | 100% at 32K / 128K / 256K, with and without MTP |

The focused CSA and connector tests also passed on MI355X (gfx950). Full validation details are in [James's comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61837#issuecomment-6206831125).

About 8% of GSM8K items timed out in lm-eval's client at concurrency 64 because of long reasoning traces. They were re-asked with the same settings and scored with lm-eval's strict regex. Raw lm-eval scores were 89.2% for CSA and 88.7% for CSA + MTP.

#### In-tree reorganization (latest commit)

Same session, 8x MI300X, TP8, median TPOT (ms) over 3 runs, before vs after the reorganization:

| K/V | 1K in, 1 req | 8K in, 1 req | 1K in, 16 conc |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | 38.97 / 39.42 | 86.67 / 87.01 | 45.10 / 44.80 |
| FP8 E4M3, `--block-size 32` | 39.41 / 39.32 | 91.96 / 91.90 | 44.85 / 45.66 |

Raw lm-eval GSM8K is unchanged (89.4% before; 89.4% BF16 K/V and 89.2% FP8 K/V after), and the real checkpoint loads the same tensors and values. The scored-prefill warmup cuts the first cold 9K-token prompt from 3.46 s to 1.14 s.

The same comparison on 8x MI350X (gfx950), BF16 K/V:

| | 1K in, 1 req | 8K in, 1 req | 1K in, 16 conc | GSM8K raw (flexible / strict) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 24.83 | 79.10 | 32.18 | 89.9% / 89.7% |
| After | 24.83 | 79.17 | 32.32 | 89.1% / 88.6% |

The GSM8K gap is within one standard error (±0.86) and matches the extra client timeouts on long reasoning traces (101 before, 110 after).

The 600B checkpoint does not fit in CI, so model-level results come from real hardware. The focused kernel, metadata, configuration, warmup, and connector tests are CI-sized.

## Details

- **Layout:** `vllm/models/step5/{common,nvidia,amd}` with platform dispatch from `vllm/models/step5/__init__.py`. ROCm code lives only in `amd/`
- **Main K/V:** written by `unified_kv_cache_update` and consumed directly from the AITER unified paged layout.
- **Sparse state:** an FP8 summary cache plus a tail ring for incomplete and speculative regions, both attached to the existing KV-cache lifecycle.
- **Decode and MTP:** summary scoring, per-row top-k, and split-K paged attention support ordinary decode and four-row MTP verification, including the head-wise attention gate.
- **Scored prefill:** histories longer than `topk * region_size` use packed summary scoring. Startup warmup now covers this path  on ROCm it dispatches to `amd/warmup.py`
- **Indexer sharding:** Q and W are `ColumnParallelLinear` sharded by provider group; K and Z stay replicated.
- **P/D:** NIXL and Mooncake preserve compressed pages for compatible layouts and fail early if a layer-outer transfer would split one compressed state page. This check applies to every compressed-cache model.
- **MoE:** the shared expert runs inside FusedMoE, and the combined output is all-reduced once in the model dtype.
- **Graphs:** the CSA op is a graph-splitting op and uses real per-step metadata. Piecewise CUDA graphs are supported.

### Limitations

| Limitation | Follow-up |
|---|---|
| Piecewise CUDA graphs only | Make CSA metadata safe for full graphs |
| `--moe-backend triton` required | Add the post-SiLU clamp to AITER block-FP8 MoE |
| Sparse top-k still has unfused work | Fuse and optimize region selection |

---

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Covers BF16/FP8 K/V, prefill, chunked prefill, decode, MTP, the head-wise gate, warmup, and connector page geometry, with model validation on real gfx942 and gfx950 hardware.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps the platform-specific model code under `amd/` and shares platform-independent code through `common/`
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Documents the current implementation, commands, limitations, and validation results.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Run MI355 MoE Kernels on a full MI355 instead of DPX
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`:amd: (MI355 DPX) MoE Kernels` failed in shards 2-5 of the nightly [amd-ci#15747](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15747). Each of these shards ran one case of `test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4` (added in #62976), and all four failed with `Expected this MXFP4 DSV4 shape to set aiter's internal output_aux flag`. Shard 1 passed only because pytest-shard placed none of the four cases there.

The test relies on aiter selecting a tuned DSV4 MXMOE kernel, which sets `output_aux`. aiter keys its tuned MoE configs by `(gfx, cu_num, ...)`, and `dsv41_fp4_tuned_fmoe.csv` only has `gfx950,256` rows. The DPX agents expose 128-CU partitions, so aiter falls back to a heuristic FlyDSL config without `output_aux`. No gfx950 MoE config in aiter has 128-CU rows.

This PR moves the step from `mi355_dpx` to `mi355_1` (full MI355X, 256 CUs). 

## Test Plan
Full MI355X (gfx950, SPX, 256 CUs), in the `rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base` image with aiter 0.1.26, vLLM at 617135eed3.
The whole step ran as in CI: its three commands from `test-amd.yaml`, 5 shards in parallel with one GPU each, and the `run-amd-test.sh` environment.
The DSV4 cases were also run on their own:
```bash
cd tests
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py \
  -k test_aiter_moe_sort_backend_dispatch_env_matrix_mxfp4
```

## Test Result
| Shard | DPX, 128 CUs ([amd-ci#15747](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15747)) | Full MI355X, 256 CUs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | passed | passed (7.4 min) |
| 2 | failed (`[ck]`) | passed (10.2 min) |
| 3 | failed (`[auto]`) | passed (8.9 min) |
| 4 | failed (`[opus]`) | passed (11.8 min) |
| 5 | failed (`[adaptive]`) | passed (6.6 min) |

All 15 commands exited 0 on 256 CUs, with no other failures.

AI-assisted tooling was used to analyze the CI logs and to run the validation. The results and the change were manually reviewed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix multi-layer MTP module selection for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen3.5-family MTP drafters (`Qwen3_5MTP`, `Qwen3_5MoeMTP`; also used by Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 and Intern-S2 checkpoints) and Qwen3-Next (`Qwen3NextMTP`) ran **MTP module 0 for every draft step** when a checkpoint has more than one MTP module, instead of the module trained for that step. This PR makes each draft step use its own module on Model Runner V2, including in the default compiled configuration.

Not a duplicate: #35607 proposed only the `forward` part of this (closed unmerged in Mar 2026, as published Qwen3.5 checkpoints ship one MTP layer); no open PR addresses it.

## Claims

- **Bug fix (MRV2):** multi-module Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next drafting now uses module `i` for draft step `i`, in eager, default compiled (`VLLM_COMPILE` + CUDA graphs), and breakable-CUDA-graph modes. Previously every step reused module 0.
- **No behavior change for shipped checkpoints:** all published Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8 / Intern-S2 checkpoints have one MTP layer; their drafter keeps its current execution mode (compiled or CUDA graphs), and outputs and acceptance are identical to `main` (below). No published checkpoint of any MTP family changes routing.
- **Lossless:** the target verifies every draft token; this affects draft acceptance (speedup), not output.

## Validation

**Regression test through `LLM` (new):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_steps_use_their_own_module`. It adds a second MTP module with random weights to the real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` checkpoint (the original shard is symlinked; only module 1 is written), runs MRV2 with the default compiled drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=2` and `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`, and checks that step 1 is accepted (module 0 intact) while step 2 is rejected (module 1 really used).

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_steps_use_their_own_module
# main (7128f568ac):
E       AssertionError: module 1 acceptance 0.419: module 0 was reused
# previous revision of this PR (eager-only fix, no compile gating):
E       AssertionError: module 1 acceptance 0.350: module 0 was reused
# this PR:
1 passed in 102.01s
```

Per-position acceptance on that two-module checkpoint (MI350x, greedy, 100 prompts):

| runner / mode | step 1 | step 2 |
|---|---|---|
| MRV2, default compiled | 0.807 | **0.000** |
| MRV2, `enforce_eager` | 0.805 | **0.000** |
| MRV2, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` | 0.805 | **0.000** (previous revision: `AttributeError: 'Qwen3_5Config' object has no attribute 'num_nextn_predict_layers'`) |
| MRV1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | 0.776 | 0.422 (module 0 reused; see limitations) |

**Routing unit test (real configs):** `tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py::test_mtp_num_hidden_layers_selects_multi_module_mtp` builds real `Qwen3_5Config` / `Qwen3_5TextConfig` configs (multimodal and text-only) through `ModelConfig` + `SpeculativeConfig`. On `main` the two-module cases fail with `assert False is True`; with this PR all 16 tests in the file pass.

**No regression on shipped checkpoints:** `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base` (one MTP layer), MRV2 compiled, `num_speculative_tokens=3`: output tokens identical to `main`, and acceptance identical on a paired run (415 drafts, per-position `[0.7663, 0.4458, 0.2458]` on both; run-to-run noise on `main` alone is ±3 drafts). The drafter is still compiled (`[eagle_head] torch.compile took 7.7 s`).

Also passed: `pytest v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/` (5 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip), `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`, `tests/test_config.py` (2 failures need gated `meta-llama` access, unrelated).

**Qwen3-Next (local only, no small checkpoint for CI):** `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, MRV2 compiled, `num_speculative_tokens=2`. Shipped one-module checkpoint: drafts, acceptance (`[0.9487, 0.8063]`) and outputs identical to `main`; drafter still compiled. With a second, random-weight MTP module (`num_nextn_predict_layers=2`, module-1 FP8 scales x100 so it dominates the residual): step-2 acceptance 0.000 with this PR vs 0.688 on `main`.

The Qwen3.5 MTP CI step did not run for changes to these model / config files; its `source_file_dependencies` now include them.

## Details

**Root causes (all needed for multi-module drafting to work):**
1. `Qwen3_5MTP.forward` / `Qwen3NextMTP.forward` did not pass `spec_step_idx` to the inner predictor, which selects `self.layers[spec_step_idx % num_mtp_layers]`. Their `**kwargs` silently accepted and dropped it; it is now a named parameter and `**kwargs` is removed (no caller passes anything else).
2. `use_multi_module_mtp()` only read `num_nextn_predict_layers`, but Qwen3.5 declares `mtp_num_hidden_layers` (nested in `text_config` for multimodal checkpoints), so it never routed to `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, the only speculator that varies `spec_step_idx`. `SpeculativeConfig.num_mtp_modules()` now reads the `n_predict` that `hf_config_override` already normalizes for every MTP family, so new multi-layer models use the multi-module speculator by default. `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator.capture()` uses the same count (it read `num_nextn_predict_layers` unconditionally, which Qwen3.5 configs lack).
3. **Compiled drafters reused module 0.** vLLM compiles the drafter once with all Dynamo guards dropped, so the Python-indexed module chosen on the first trace was replayed for every step. The other multi-module drafters (Inkling, Step-3.5, MiMo-V2, Qwen4Exp, MiniMax-M3) are not compiled, which is why this did not surface. The Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next drafter is now compiled only when it runs single-module (`support_torch_compile(enable_if=...)`); multi-module drafters run eager with full CUDA graphs over the draft loop, like the other multi-module drafters. Since #51012 the CUDA Qwen3.5 drafter is no longer compiled, so this gate now applies to Qwen3-Next and the ROCm Qwen3.5 drafter.
4. With multi-module routing, the local-argmax path calls `get_top_tokens(hidden_states, spec_step_idx=...)`; `Qwen3_5MTP` now accepts and ignores it, since the MTP modules share one `lm_head` (as in `compute_logits`).

**Scope:** Qwen3-Next already routed correctly via `num_nextn_predict_layers`; it needed only (1) and (3). Drafts with MTP index sharing (`index_share_for_mtp_iteration`, from the checkpoint or the override) and MiniMax-M3 stay on the single-module speculator, with TODOs: index sharing is only implemented there, and MiniMax-M3 is not yet verified with the multi-module speculator.

**Files:** since #51012, CUDA loads `Qwen3_5MTP` from `vllm/models/qwen3_5/nvidia/mtp.py`, while ROCm and Intern-S2 (`InternS2MobiusMTP`) still use `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`. Fixes (1) and (4) are applied to both files.



**Limitations:** Model Runner V1 never passes `spec_step_idx` for any MTP family (only Step-3.5's proposer does), so multi-module drafting there still uses module 0; MRV1 is deprecated and this PR targets MRV2. Multi-module Qwen drafters trade the compiled drafter for eager + full CUDA graphs; no shipped checkpoint takes that path.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep offline DP ranks' collectives aligned with async scheduling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Offline data parallelism (`LLMEngine` with the in-process client, e.g. `distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher"`) hangs with async scheduling when one DP rank gets a step that runs no model forward. `LLMEngine.step()` now runs `execute_dummy_batch()` for such a step when DP is on, as `DPEngineCoreProc.run_busy_loop` already does for `vllm serve`.

## Claims

- Offline DP2 with async scheduling no longer hangs when the ranks' workloads differ; both Model Runner V2 and V1 finish.
- The V1 runner's `external_launcher`-only `_dummy_run(1)` (#28774) is removed, since the engine now runs the dummy batch for every in-process DP backend and V1 would otherwise sync twice.

## Validation

Reproducer (`torchrun --nproc-per-node 2`, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, `data_parallel_size=2`, `distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher"`, `async_scheduling=True`, greedy; rank 0 runs 1 prompt with `max_tokens=8`, rank 1 runs 4 prompts with `max_tokens=256`, `ignore_eos`), one GB200 node:

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
import os

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
    data_parallel_size=2,
    distributed_executor_backend="external_launcher",
    async_scheduling=True,
    max_model_len=1024,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.3,
    seed=0,
)
prompts = ["The capital of France is"] * (1 if rank == 0 else 4)
params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8 if rank == 0 else 256, ignore_eos=True)
outs = llm.generate(prompts, params)
print(f"rank {rank} done: {[len(o.outputs[0].token_ids) for o in outs]}", flush=True)
```
</details>

| | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model Runner V2 | hangs (killed after 300 s) | rank 0 `[8]`, rank 1 `[256, 256, 256, 256]` |
| Model Runner V1 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) | | rank 0 `[8]`, rank 1 `[256, 256, 256, 256]` |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, offline DP2 + EP with the same launcher and async scheduling, DSpark K=5 (probabilistic drafting, standard rejection sampling), GSM8K test set split across the two ranks, 5-shot, greedy, max 1024 tokens, lm_eval's strict-match regex (a small offline harness, since lm_eval cannot drive `external_launcher` DP; its few-shot prompt and stop strings differ from lm_eval's, so the score is not comparable to lm_eval GSM8K). On main this configuration hung; with this PR both ranks finish all 1319 questions: strict-match 0.903 (591/660 + 600/659), DSpark acceptance length 3.54 (89,337 accepted tokens over 35,115 drafts).

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine.py -k "dummy_batch or mm_processor_cache_misses"  # 3 passed
```

The new test fails on main for the step that ran no forward.

## Details

- Root cause: the offline loop needs every rank to run exactly one forward, and so one DP sync, between two `has_unfinished_dp()` all-reduces. With async scheduling, a rank whose only remaining request already reaches `max_tokens` through placeholders schedules 0 tokens (or only pops a queued batch). The V2 runner then returns before `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp`, so that rank goes on to the `has_unfinished_dp()` all-reduce while the other rank waits in its forward's DP sync: the two ranks wait in different collectives.
- `InprocClient.get_output()` records whether its step executed the model, and `LLMEngine.step()` runs the dummy batch when it did not. Multiprocess clients don't set the attribute, so their behavior is unchanged: `DPEngineCoreProc` already runs the dummy batch itself.
- Related: #43547 reports a similar DP desync on the V1 runner with the ray / mp backends; this PR does not change those backends.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse quantization into RMSNorm and attention output.

| producer | consumer (quant key) | kernel |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma add-RMSNorm | attn `qkv_proj`, GDN `in_proj_qkvz` (static FP8 or NVFP4) | new Triton `gemma_add_rms_norm_quant`; for GDN it also writes the bf16 normed input that `in_proj_ba` reads |
| post-attention Gemma add-RMSNorm | MLP `gate_up_proj` (NVFP4 or static FP8). Only used by dense layers | same kernel |
| GDN gated RMSNorm | `out_proj` (static FP8) | FP8-output option on `fused_gdn_gated_rms_norm` |
| attention sigmoid output gate | `o_proj` (static FP8) | FP8-output option on `fused_sigmoid_gate_mul` |

Related:
- #56530 (AR+norm+quant at TP>1, complementary)
- #61073 (same contract for generic `RMSNorm`)
- #45364 / #45855 / #42469 / #61783 / #59553 (other norm+quant fusion efforts).

No open PR covers the Qwen3.5 NVIDIA no-compile path.

**Which checkpoints engage (first-party census)**

| checkpoint | quant layout | fusions engaged |
|---|---|---|
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | attn q/k/v/o + GDN in_qkv/z/out static FP8; MLP NVFP4 g16 | all four (192 quant kernels/step, runtime-verified) |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` | attn/GDN static FP8; MoE experts NVFP4 | the three FP8 fusions (post-attn norm feeds the bf16 router) |
| `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | dynamic per-token FP8; MLP NVFP4 | NVFP4 norm fusion only |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B/397B NVFP4` | experts-only NVFP4 | none
| official `Qwen/Qwen3.5-*-FP8`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-*-FP8` | block-FP8 128x128, dynamic | none |

## Claims

- **1.7–2.0× faster than the unfused norm+quant chain** at decode batch sizes and **1.1–1.6×** at large M, for every fused kernel at every M from 1 to 8192.
- **2.2–6.7% lower TPOT** serving `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` on B300 at TP1 (up to 6.5% at TP2 c64)
- **Unchanged accuracy**: full GSM8K within noise of main.
- Everything that does not match the contract (block/per-token/dynamic FP8, padded NVFP4, BF16, W4A16, LoRA, MoE router input) keeps the existing path, verified by the audit matrix in Details.

## Validation

### Microbenchmarks

- GB300, FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2 (rotating buffers > 3× L2); real checkpoint norm weights and scales; median of 5 shuffled processes (range < 2%).
- Unfused is the serving chain: in-place `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` (or the existing gated-norm/gate kernel) + `scaled_fp8_quant` / `scaled_fp4_quant`.

**attn in-norm + FP8 (5120)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.64 | 2.69 | 1.73× |
| 32 | 5.12 | 2.66 | 1.92× |
| 512 | 8.29 | 5.44 | 1.52× |
| 8192 | 71.23 | 44.03 | 1.62× |

**GDN in-norm + FP8 + bf16 y (5120)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.67 | 2.75 | 1.70× |
| 32 | 5.15 | 2.75 | 1.87× |
| 512 | 8.32 | 5.95 | 1.40× |
| 8192 | 71.23 | 56.51 | 1.26× |

**post-norm + NVFP4 (5120)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.42 | 3.26 | 1.36× |
| 32 | 4.99 | 3.30 | 1.51× |
| 512 | 7.87 | 6.85 | 1.15× |
| 8192 | 69.60 | 50.02 | 1.39× |

**gated norm + FP8 (6144)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.81 | 1.89 | 2.02× |
| 32 | 4.19 | 2.27 | 1.85× |
| 512 | 10.66 | 7.71 | 1.38× |
| 8192 | 78.37 | 52.35 | 1.50× |

**gate + FP8 (6144)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.71 | 1.92 | 1.93× |
| 32 | 4.00 | 2.05 | 1.95× |
| 512 | 7.55 | 4.58 | 1.65× |
| 8192 | 69.12 | 42.24 | 1.64× |

Fused outputs match the chain: residual bitwise, bf16 y within 1 ulp (different sum-of-squares reduction order), FP8/FP4 codes within 1 step (≤1e-4 of elements; bitwise on B300 — not guaranteed across archs).

### E2E perf

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, B300, random 8k/1k, 10 warmups, c1 × 32 / c16 × 160 /
c64 × 640 prompts; median TPOT. Base is current main (includes #64425). TP1: two runs
with reversed arm order (A B B A). TP2: one run (A B).

TP1, TPOT (ms), both runs:

| Concurrency | Main | Branch | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.263 / 5.263 | 4.882 / 4.934 | −6.7% |
| 16 | 8.756 / 8.752 | 8.065 / 8.264 | −6.7% |
| 64 | 23.246 / 23.268 | 22.825 / 22.663 | −2.2% |

Base-vs-base (noise floor): ≤0.1% at all concurrencies; branch-vs-branch ≤2.4%.
Change is the average of the two runs.

TP2, TPOT (ms), one run:

| Concurrency | Main | Branch | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.135 | 4.070 | −1.6% |
| 16 | 6.209 | 6.063 | −2.4% |
| 64 | 15.637 | 14.614 | −6.5% |

### E2E accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions, CUDA graph, same checkpoint and node:

| Task | Main | Branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 0.9492 | 0.9545 |

Reproduce:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 16384 [--tensor-parallel-size 2]
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-warmups 10 --max-concurrency {1,16,64} --num-prompts {32,160,640}
```

## Details

Dispatch logic
- Entrypoint: `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer.forward`, per norm, one of three paths:
  - TP>1 with the FlashInfer fused all-reduce+norm: AR+norm wins, quant runs separately. AR+norm+quant in one kernel is #56530's scope.
  - Consumer takes `kFp8StaticTensorSym`, or `kNvfp4Dynamic` with zero K padding and `K % 64 == 0` (the norm writes whole 4-column scale tiles): norm+quant.
  - Otherwise the existing plain norm. Eligibility is checked per call through `get_input_quant_key`, since keys appear after weight loading and LoRA hides them.
- The fused kernels assert on layout violations. One exception: `fused_sigmoid_gate_mul` takes a quantized eager fallback for a strided gate view (num_heads == 1 per TP rank).
- The gate fusion lives in `Qwen3NextAttention`, so a Qwen3-Next checkpoint with a static-FP8 `o_proj` also engages it; the norm fusions are Qwen3.5-only. Only the gated-norm, gate and layer-0 fusions engage at TP>1 (65 of 192 quant kernels/step).

Limitations:
- Per-token and 128x128 block FP8 are not included
- The warp-dispatch rule was swept on GB300 (SM103) only; a B200 re-sweep may move the last few percent.

<details>
<summary>Audit matrix, PDL, warmup, follow-ups</summary>

| case | result |
|---|---|
| TP1 `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (the target) | all four fusions, 192 quant kernels/step removed (instrumented) |
| TP2/4/8 with FlashInfer AR | AR+norm on norms after layer 0; gated norm, gate, layer-0 norm fused; per-norm choice, no conflict |
| TP>1 without FlashInfer AR | same as TP1 |
| all-NVFP4 W4A4 | norms → NVFP4 (GDN with bf16 side output); dummy-weight run engages in eager and graph |
| block / per-token / dynamic FP8 | fallback; dummy MoE block-FP8 run: no fusion, no crash |
| NVFP4 K padding or `K % 64 != 0` | fallback (dispatch gate) |
| BF16 / W4A16 | fallback (no key) |
| eager vs CUDA graph | both; QA produced and consumed inside a graph segment |
| MTP / spec decode | target layers fused; bf16 MTP layer falls back (the official 27B checkpoint ships no MTP head, so exercised by unit tests, not e2e) |
| layer 0 (residual None) | plain norm + quant; residual = input |
| MoE (`qwen3_5_moe_text`) | input norms fused; post-attn norm keeps bf16 (router); dummy MoE static-FP8 run engages |
| weight reload | scales read from the layer per call, as in the unfused path |
| LoRA | wrapper sets `requires_unquantized_input` → fallback |
| non-contiguous inputs | fused norm and gated norm assert; sigmoid gate takes the quantized eager fallback |

**PDL.** The fused norm launches with `launch_pdl=True` unconditionally (one fat CTA per
row, `gdc_wait` before the first load, `gdc_launch_dependents` after the stores). A/B on
B300, M = 1..32768, FP8 and NVFP4: neutral-to-faster in self-chain (−0.2% to −15%) and
production-like chains (−0.4% to −3.6%); an adversarial early-trigger predecessor costs
at most +4% at M=128, nothing at M ≥ 1024. Outputs bitwise identical with PDL on/off.
At M ≤ 128 the kernel also launches its dependents immediately after `gdc_wait`,
overlapping the consumer GEMM's weight load (~2% chain win); above that the prelaunched
consumer grid steals SMs (fp8 +4-7% at M ≥ 192), so it is gated by M.

**Warmup.** Not in the dedicated JIT-warmup registry (as before this PR); all reachable
variants compile during the standard dummy-run and capture-size sweeps. The jit-monitor
E2E lane is currently skipped (#49349).

**Follow-ups (not in this PR).** AR+norm+quant at TP>1 (#56530); block-FP8 consumer
contract for the official `Qwen/*-FP8` checkpoints; B200 warp re-sweep; earlier
`gdc_launch_dependents` beyond M=128 if the consumer grid is small; split rows across
CTAs at small M for NVFP4. Also related: #41021 (per-shard FP8 scaling — would turn the
static-per-tensor gate here into a fallback), #41457 (fusing `in_proj_ba` into `in_proj`
would remove the bf16 side output).
</details>

## Test plan

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_gemma_add_rms_norm_quant.py
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_sigmoid_gate_mul.py
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py tests/models/test_qwen3_5.py
  tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py`: **98 passed on B300**. The new test
  is wired into a new `:nvidia: (B200) Qwen3.5` step in
  `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` (the tests/kernels/core lane is H200 MIG,
  where this SM100 test would only skip).
- Dummy-weight dispatch runs (eager and CUDA graph): all-NVFP4 W4A4, MoE static FP8,
  MoE block FP8.
- `pre-commit run` on all changed files passes.

AI assistance: written with Claude Code; reviewed and hardened with Kimi Code and a
Codex second-opinion review. A human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and
benchmarks above.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove every remaining `device: a100` declaration — the fleet is retired and the generator never emits those steps, but they still render on ci.vllm.ai/sharding as never-run jobs that count against automatic-shard enrollment. The two steps with live AMD mirrors keep those mirrors as standalone AMD steps. Supersedes #60596, which went stale and now conflicts with main.

## Claims

- Removes the `(A100) LM Eval Humming Default/Act INT8 TEMPORARY` steps, the `(A100) Batch Invariance` and `(A100) Distributed` declarations, the commented-out 4xA100 block in `lm_eval.yaml`, and the five `humming/config-a100-*.txt` shard lists only the Humming steps referenced.
- The two live AMD mirrors keep running as standalone steps, under the same emitted keys, labels, queues, commands and timeouts: `amd-distributed-tests-4xa100` (:amd: (MI355) Distributed) and `amd-batch-invariance-a100` (:amd: (MI250) Batch Invariance).
- Under a diff touching the three changed test-area files, the generated pipeline is unchanged job-for-job except one benign prefix (Details): no job is added, removed or altered. Selection under a `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` diff was validated separately (Details, behavior change 2).
- Difference from #60596, why this is not a plain duplicate: it predates the now-live `:amd: (MI250) Batch Invariance` mirror on `batch-invariance-a100`, so merging it as-is would delete a running job; this PR preserves both mirrors as standalone steps instead (its own description names this as the needed follow-up).

## Validation

- Generated the full Buildkite pipeline with ci-infra's pipeline generator (ci-infra@9d2935b5) for `main`'s YAML and for this change, per-key diffed, under three triggering diffs: (a) a touch of the three changed test-area files — every job identical except the prefix below; (b) `VLLM_CI_ONLY_STEP_KEYS=["amd-..."]` to force each converted job to emit — same result; (c) a `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` touch — `amd-batch-invariance-a100` still runs in both layouts, `amd-distributed-tests-4xa100` moves to the deferred list (behavior change 2).
- Repro: run `pipeline-generator --pipeline_config_path .buildkite/ci_config.yaml` from a checkout at this PR's head and at `main`, with `get_ecr_cache_registry` stubbed, and diff per-key.
- `tools/pre_commit/check_buildkite_step_keys.py` and `tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py` pass; no test loses its CI job.
- Repo-wide grep: no remaining reference to any deleted `config-a100-*.txt`.
- No GPU run locally; a `/ci run` plus a scoped build of the two `amd-` keys exercises the converted steps for real. Recorder builds were code-read only: `_kernrec_applies`/`_fnrec_applies` see the same outcome because `KERNREC_SKIP_STEPS` names neither key.

## Details

- The converted steps keep their `amd-`-prefixed keys rather than getting fresh ones: it preserves job identity for retries, scoped builds and dashboard history, and native AMD steps with `amd-` keys already exist (e.g. `amd-kernels-mi355`).
- Each standalone step carries the fields its mirror inherited from the base step explicitly: `optional: true` and `num_devices: 4` (Distributed), and the base's commands for Batch Invariance, whose mirror had none of its own. `source_file_dependencies` are the union the generator applied to the mirror (base + mirror lists).
- Behavior change 1 (commands): the native AMD path prepends `export VLLM_TEST_GROUP_NAME=<key>` to the command string; the mirror path didn't. Harmless: nothing on main reads that variable.
- Behavior change 2 (selection): mirrors auto-run on PRs that change `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` even when optional (`_amd_mirror_should_run`); native steps use plain dependency matching. For the (MI250) Batch Invariance step this PR restores the old behavior by adding `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` to its `source_file_dependencies`, matching the other native AMD steps (`misc.yaml`). For the optional (MI355) Distributed step it is accepted instead of emulated — `optional: true` short-circuits file-dependency selection, so such PRs get it at the nightly or via manual unblock, same as every other native optional AMD step.
- Reviewer call (carried over from #60596): `humming/Qwen3-4B-mixed-quant-RTN-humming.yaml` is kept although only the deleted A100 shard lists referenced it, in case it should move to an H100 list.
- Out of scope: the commented-out, already-disabled NixlConnector A100 block in `disaggregated.yaml` (never parsed), and ci-infra's now-unused A100 queue constants.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Run the model-level post-load hook once at the end of every load and reload
commits.pr_body:
PR 1 of the direct weight reload stack (RFC #54477). It replaces #57733. The code is the same, plus the Llama4 DP-vision fix that #57733 dropped when it was narrowed.

## Problem

RL weight updates do not load a model in one `load_weights` call. The weight-transfer engines (NCCL, IPC, M2N, sharded RDT) and `reload_weights` call it once per bucket, or once per tensor, between `initialize_layerwise_reload` and `finalize_layerwise_reload`. On main, three things go wrong with that:

1. **The model-level hook never runs after a reload.** `finalize_layerwise_reload` only finishes the layers. The model's `process_weights_after_loading()` runs only from the cold-load path. So any state a model derives from its weights in that hook, such as fused buffers or broadcast copies, keeps the old weights' values after an update.
2. **Some models do that work inside `load_weights` instead.** It then runs once per bucket, on partial weights. Under layerwise reload it runs while the layers are still on meta, which fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. This affects DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, the DFlash/DSpark drafters and Muse Spark.
3. **Checks on "what this call loaded" fire on every bucket.** A bucket that happens not to contain a layer or head raises "MTP layer N weights missing", or silently sets the DSpark `confidence_head` to `None`.

## Fix

- **One finish step.** New `finalize_model_weights(model)` calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. It is called once at the end of a cold load (as before, after per-layer quant processing) and once at the end of every `finalize_layerwise_reload`. That covers `reload_weights` and the NCCL, IPC, M2N and sharded-RDT engines.
  - The sparse NCCL engine patches weights in place without layerwise reload; its `finish_weight_update` now calls `finalize_model_weights` once.
  - An M2N update whose plan is all direct does not call `finalize_layerwise_reload`, so it still skips the hook, as on main.
  - The torchao reload decorator and the expert-substitution error path finish the layers in the middle of a load. They now call `finalize_layerwise_processing`, so they do not run the model hook early.
- **Post-load work moves from `load_weights` into the hook.** Each `load_weights` below now only loads, and the hook runs at the end:
  - DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA, V4.1 NVIDIA/AMD: the mHC broadcast (V4.1 AMD's `finalize_mega_moe_weights` is a no-op).
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA: the Engram checkpoint page-cache drop and THP collapse. They now also run after every reload and after dummy loads; both are harmless to repeat.
  - DeepSeek-V4 XPU target, MTP and DSpark: `finalize_mega_moe_weights`. The lazy call in MegaMoE `forward()` is removed, since dummy loads run the hook too.
  - Qwen3 DFlash / Qwen3 DSpark / Gemma4 DSpark / Muse Spark DSpark: `_build_fused_kv_buffers`.
    - The hook now runs after quant processing.
    - In Qwen3 DFlash/DSpark and Gemma4 DSpark, the fused path that reads `.weight` directly is used only when the projections are unquantized and not CPU-repacked (`_reads_raw_weights`). Otherwise each projection runs through its quant method.
    - Muse Spark DSpark still slices `qkv_proj.weight` directly, now after quant processing, so a quantized or CPU-repacked Muse Spark drafter would read kernel-layout weights.
    - Qwen3 DFlash's MXFP8 context K/V projection copied the K/V rows of each layer's QKV weight and scales, which is only valid before quant processing. It is now created at construction and loaded from the checkpoint's K/V tensors as they stream through `load_weights`, so its own post-load step runs and a reload refills it in place.
  - Muse Spark AMD and Muse Spark DSpark: `materialize_residual_path_constants`.
- **The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers drop their workaround.** They had reordered the weight stream so that the language model's in-`load_weights` finalization saw all its weights (`stream_language_model_first`, `finalizes_weights_during_load`, `_weights_finalized`). That is no longer needed and is removed.
- **"Complete load" checks are gated on `is_mtp_completeness_check_enabled()`**, which the weight-transfer engines turn off during an update:
  - The MTP layer checks in DeepSeek-V3.2 AMD, GLM5-next and Kimi-K3 (AMD/NVIDIA).
  - The DSpark `confidence_head` drop in Qwen3, Gemma4 and DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 (NVIDIA/AMD).
  - The Qwen3 DSpark vocab checks.
  - `AutoWeightsLoader._check_skipped_aliases`.
- **dots3 vision: the block compile runs once.** The vision hook now reruns after every reload, and main's `compile_block_modules` would wrap the blocks in another `torch.compile` each time. It now compiles in place with `Module.compile` (parameter names keep no `_orig_mod`) and only once. The vision MoE is unchanged from main: its hook fuses the experts into FP8 once, deletes the checkpoint experts and returns early afterwards, so a reload leaves the vision experts as they are.
- **Llama4 DP vision (`mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`).**
  - Before: the vision attention used `ReplicatedLinear`, and `load_weights` gathered `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and called `torch.cat` once all three had arrived. An update that sends them in separate calls failed on `torch.cat` of `None`.
  - Now: it uses `QKVParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` with `disable_tp=True` in DP mode, so q/k/v go through the normal stacked mapping and each part is written into its rows as it arrives. `_consolidate_qkv_weights` is removed.
- **Raw Tensorizer loads use the shared loader path.** Loading a non-vLLM-tensorized checkpoint used its own `_load_model_serialized_cpu`, which ran the model hook but skipped per-layer `process_weights_after_loading`. It now goes through `BaseModelLoader.load_model`.

## Not in this PR

- **Weights combined from several checkpoint tensors inside `load_weights`.** A weight plus its scale, or a fused FP8 qkv, still need every part in the same call, as on main:
  - the FP8 indexer `wk` dequant;
  - GLM5-next MLA projections;
  - MiMo-V2 fused qkv;
  - Molmo/Molmo2 split embedding.

  These are later PRs in the stack (PR 6).
- **Drafters that still finish inside `load_weights`, unchanged from main:**
  - LiLiCorr: the coverage check and `materialize_inference_buffers`.
  - Laguna DFlash: the fused KV build.
  - Qwen3 XPress: the `mix.L` check, `fold_from_raw_` and the fused buffers. It also inherits the new DFlash hook, so at cold start its fused KV buffers are built twice, the second time after quant processing.

  A bucketed update of these drafters behaves as on main. LiLiCorr and Laguna are in the F9 follow-up.
- **Hooks that are not safe to rerun.** Every model-level hook reachable from a top-level model was checked for a second run on reloaded weights. These are not fixed here:
  - **DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (model, MTP, DSpark): a reload now fails instead of leaving wrong weights.**
    - On main this hook ran only at cold start, so a reload left the mega-MoE experts and the preshuffled attention and gate/up weights unshuffled or stale.
    - With this PR it reruns at the end of a reload. With `fuse_shared_expert`, the first run sets `shared_experts = None` (`finalize_mega_moe_weights`), so the second run raises `AttributeError` in `load_shared_expert`.
    - Without it, the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early (stale experts), and `prepare_attn_preshuffle` / `prepare_gateup_preshuffle` shuffle in place again, so layers that the update did not resend are shuffled twice.
  - **dots3 vision MoE: stale, as on main.** Making it reloadable without keeping the BF16 experts resident (about 11 GiB per GPU on dots3-note-prev-fp8 TP4) needs a loader that quantizes each expert into the fused FP8 buffers as it arrives; that is a follow-up.
  - **Muse Spark NVIDIA: stale, as on main.** The router multiplier is folded once and then dropped, and the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early after dropping `w13_weight`.
  - **DeepSeek-V4 XPU mega-MoE: guarded, as on main.** `finalize_weights` returns early once the weights are transformed. The XPU runtime currently rejects mega-MoE, so the hook is a no-op.
  - **Rebuilt as new tensors.** Kimi-K3 AMD's MLA `_w_fold` and Muse Spark's residual `alpha`/`beta` are re-created by the hook, so a captured CUDA graph keeps reading the old ones.
    - On main Kimi-K3's hook did not run on reload, and Muse Spark rebuilt them the same way from `load_weights`, so neither is worse than main.
    - The DFlash/DSpark (Qwen3, Gemma4, Muse Spark) and Beam DFlash2 context K/V buffers, and Kimi-K3 NVIDIA DSpark's `_context_kv_norm_weights`, are also re-created. The V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads the context K/V buffers, so after a reload it reads freed memory and draft acceptance drops (Beam DFlash2 TP4, split reload: 7.03 → 4.89; MiniMax-M3.1 MXFP8 DSpark TP4: 5.70 → 4.07). commits.pr_title: [CPU][MRv2] Enable MRv2 for non-triton CPU backends
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Context: MRv1 is getting removed https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63373, and the MRv2 code uses triton, which does not yet have mature enough support on a lot of platforms. 

This PR:
- enables MRv2 (by default) for CPUs where triton isn't available - Arm CPUs, IBM Z, IBM PowerPC, RISCV CPUs
- only applies to CPU backend when triton support is not available, i.e. doesn't apply to x86
- completely disentangles GPU MRv2 code from CPU, as we all agreed in the cpu-sig meeting - so GPU maintainers updating the GPU code path for MRv2 won't be blocked on CPU failures from changes in the shared path.

## Design

As per our design meeting last week, the approach taken for supported configs is:
- everything has to be under `vllm/v1/worker/cpu` and no changes / dependencies on `vllm/v1/worker/gpu` for MRv2. My approach here is a bit too conservative, I think there are parts of GPU MRv2 that are stable enough for us to share/reuse, but I thought it's better to be on the safe side for now. We can always revisit this later.
- copy MRv2 GPU code verbatim as much as possible - this is the code that the CPU MRv2 in the previous approach (see older commits) used to inherit from subclassing the GPU MRv2
- where copying is not possible, tweak with only the changes necessary to make it work on CPU (e.g. copy the orchestration / wrapper code, but replace a triton kernel call with a C++ kernel call)
- Do not support everything under the sun yet (I avoided spec decode support for now as PR is already huge, we can either add later or hopefully we won't need to if we pull-off triton-cpu fast enough :crossed_fingers:)
- non-triton MRv2 kernels use:
    - pytorch (with torch.compile where useful) for tensor transformations like output and prompt logprobs, token ranks, min-p
    - C++ Ops for cases where pytorch impl is not fast enough: gumbel argmax, block-table writes, slot mapping, M-RoPE
    - Python / numpy for some metadata and request state: thinking budgets, trace replay, state book-keeping 

## Support

We support the following model families:
- Default decoder state: Dense decoder-only and supported multimodal models
- Mamba-hybrid state: Non-speculative hybrid attention/SSM models; GDN was validated 
- Encoder-only state : Pooling, classification, token-level, and scoring workflows
- Encoder-decoder state : Ordinary generation and beam search 

The CPU Sampler supports:
- Greedy and per-request-seeded random sampling using the CPU Gumbel-max/argmax kernel.
- Temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, repetition/frequency/presence penalties, logit bias, allowed-token
    IDs, bad words, and minimum-token stop suppression.
- Structured-output masks, thinking budgets, trace replay, watermarking, and sampling masks.
- Prompt/output logprobs, requested-token logprobs, sampled-token ranks, and chunked prompt-logprob
    accumulation.
- Top-k/top-p currently use the PyTorch implementation - A fused C++ is available in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62440

We do not yet support:
- models previously unsupported by CPU on MRv1.
- Diffusion Models
- Models with custom `ModelStates` that are not part of the supported families above
- Speculative decoding
- Prompt embeddings
- Decode context parallelism
- Prefill context parallelism
- Batch-sharded sampling
- mm encoder-only

## Performance (on Arm Neoverse-V2 cores)

The best perf indicator here is a small model (< 1b) where the new MRv2 flow and kernels would be a bottleneck and take a consequential percentage of runtime (as apposed to a big model that spends 99.9% of its time in GEMMs)

Here are some perf results with Qwen3.5-0.8B, 256 prompts, 256 input / output tokens

Perf with greedy decoding:

| Concurrency | Throughput | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | +9.6% | -2.5% | -9.5% |
| 32 | +7.0% | -0.8% | -7.8% |

Perf with random sampling (t=1, topp=1):

| Concurrency | Throughput | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | +13.8% | -3.1% | -13.1% |
| 32 | +8.4% | -0.2% | -9.4% |


## Accuracy validation (on Arm Neoverse-V2 Cores)

### Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | GSM8k with TP=2

HF vs vLLM (TP=2) for 100 samples of gsm8k:

```
lm_eval \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args "pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B,dtype=bfloat16,enable_thinking=False" \
  --model <vllm|hf> \
  --limit 100 \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --output_path out \
  --batch_size 100 \
  --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=512" \
  --log_samples
```

HF Results:
```
hf ({'pretrained': 'Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B', 'dtype': 'bfloat16', 'enable_thinking': False}), gen_kwargs: ({'max_gen_toks': 512}), limit: 100.0, num_fewshot: None, batch_size: 100
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value|   |Stderr|

|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  | 0.97|±  |0.0171|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  | 0.97|±  |0.0171|
```

vLLM Results, with TP=2

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSA] Read BF16 logits directly in persistent top-k
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Merged by WoosukKwon on 2026-10-30 as [`e31cf3dec7cf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0), following approval of final PR head `5ff957619959`. The validation revisions and their scope are recorded below.

Let the existing persistent top-k backend read BF16 indexer logits and widen loaded scores to FP32 inside its kernels. On SM100 decode without DCP, this removes the full FP32 logits allocation whenever `auto` resolves to persistent, as well as for explicit persistent.

Query chunking is separate work. This PR complements [#62172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172), which implements BF16 input for cooperative top-k. This change implements persistent, filtered and sampled paths instead. Open-PR searches found no separate persistent-BF16 implementation. The caller uses the same `takes_bf16_logits()` capability-interface design as #62172; cooperative support remains with that PR.

## Claims

- Keep the existing backend selection and top-k algorithms. Scores loaded from BF16 widen to FP32 before binning/refinement; register score arrays remain FP32.
- Remove the dense FP32 logits copy for supported persistent decode calls, including default auto. Cooperative, DCP and prefill retain their existing behavior. No DeepSelect switch or query-row chunking is introduced.
- Preserve exact selected scores and valid top-k indices in the tested cases. Equal-score index identity/order and generated-token equivalence are not claimed.

## Validation

### Performance breakdown and memory traffic

**DeepGEMM's logits computation is unchanged.** This PR saves work **after** BF16 logits have been produced: it removes the separate BF16-to-FP32 materialization and lets persistent top-k read BF16 directly. It does not reduce Q/K projection work, the score computation, or the number of logits. The measurements below exclude DeepGEMM and are not end-to-end model speedups.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["DeepGEMM: unchanged score computation"] --> B["BF16 logits in GPU memory: unchanged"]
    B -->|Before PR| C["Separate conversion kernel: read BF16, write FP32"]
    C --> F["Full FP32 logits buffer"]
    F --> O["Load FP32 scores; existing FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    B -->|With PR: supported persistent calls| N["Load BF16 scores; widen in registers; same FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    O --> I["Top-k indices"]
    N --> I
```

| Where the saving occurs | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| External conversion | Allocate a full FP32 logits buffer; read 2 bytes and write 4 bytes per valid score | Remove this allocation and GPU conversion kernel |
| Top-k input loads | 4 bytes per FP32 score; an aligned four-score load reads 16 bytes | 2 bytes per BF16 score; an aligned four-score load reads 8 bytes and expands to four FP32 registers |
| Score arithmetic inside top-k | FP32 comparison/binning/refinement | The same FP32 algorithm, with on-load widening; register score arrays are still FP32 |

Code: [producer and conversion bypass](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L939-L954), [old allocation and conversion kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L297-L329), and [FP32/BF16 load helpers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L100).

**Measured breakdown: pre-PR `98fc6da9d735` versus PR `293880733f87`, GB200.** The PR source is unchanged by the subsequent main merges. The BF16 top-k timing includes its loads, register widening, and selection; it is not the cast alone.

| Q / valid K / top-k | External conversion: before → after (µs) | Native top-k: FP32 → BF16 (µs) | Native top-k latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 2.848 → removed | 4.832 → 5.632 | +16.56% |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 19.296 → removed | 31.232 → 30.240 | -3.18% |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 35.264 → removed | 44.800 → 42.352 | -5.46% |

The **33–44% full selection-stage improvement** in the long-row cases mainly comes from eliminating the external conversion; native top-k alone improves by only about 3–5%. The short-row native kernel is slower with BF16, while the measured complete caller still improves after removing the conversion. Smaller input loads can help, but widening adds register instructions. Halving score-input bytes does not establish that total HBM traffic or latency halves; cache behavior and multiple passes matter. No hardware-counter measurement proves a bandwidth-only explanation.

**Allocation size and accessed bytes are different quantities.** At Q=128 and valid K=100000, the removed conversion logically reads 25.6 MB of BF16 data and writes 51.2 MB of FP32 data (decimal MB). A single full scan by top-k reads 51.2 MB of FP32 score payload versus 25.6 MB of BF16 payload; this is byte accounting, not measured DRAM traffic. The full FP32 allocation is larger because it retains capacity W=262144 and padded stride=262656: about **128.248 MiB**. That temporary disappears; the original BF16 logits and existing workspace remain. CUDA graph replay does not remove conversion kernels automatically; this PR removes that node and its FP32 storage from supported captured paths.

These component timings are separate cold-cache ablations, **not additive**. The complete caller measurements below remain the primary before/after result.

<details>
<summary>Breakdown measurement method and why the columns are not additive</summary>

Baseline `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`, using the same frozen runtimes and matching fixed BF16 inputs as the full-stage table below. GB200 job 41138: A/B/B/A fresh processes, 30 cold-L2 CUPTI graph samples per stage/run (60 per arm). Conversion uses the actual `as_fp32_logits`; top-k uses the native persistent entrypoint. Input capacity W=262144, padded stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576.

These are separately captured cold-cache ablations, not timestamps of nodes in one production graph. Conversion warms its FP32 output for the following kernel, while standalone top-k starts cold. The full caller also clears the output-index buffer; this native-only ablation omits that common operation. Summing the component columns therefore does not reconstruct the full-stage table. Jointly captured conversion+FP32 top-k medians are retained separately in the raw results (6.816, 46.5755 and 78.0805 µs); the full caller table remains the primary before/after comparison.

For intuition only, one full score scan would give 2-byte BF16 read + 4-byte FP32 write + 4-byte FP32 read before this PR, versus a 2-byte BF16 read after it. This 10→2 byte accounting excludes unchanged producer writes, metadata/workspace accesses, multiple selection passes and cache effects; it is not a measured traffic reduction or a 5x speedup prediction.

Every ablation passes exact selected-score, valid/unique-index and input-preservation checks. Raw samples, identities and commands are retained in `main_vs_packed_breakdown_v1` (`bench.py`, `run.sbatch`, `SUMMARY.json`, `results/41138_*`). These component measurements do not establish full-model accuracy or end-to-end performance.

</details>

### Full selection-stage results

Recorded performance baseline: **unmodified pre-PR base `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`**. The baseline has no persistent BF16 support and widens the BF16 producer output to a full FP32 logits tensor. The PR keeps BF16 for supported persistent calls. Neither arm includes cooperative BF16 support from #62172 or the FP32-producer configuration from #64580. This table measures the whole PR against its pre-PR baseline, not an intermediate PR commit.

Job 41130 on an exclusive GB200: A/B/B/A fresh processes, CUPTI cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, 30 samples/run (60 per arm/shape). The actual indexer caller receives identical fixed injected BF16 logits. **Timing includes the required full-tensor conversion and top-k**, but excludes the real DeepGEMM producer, CPU Python dispatch and the model. Caller/provider source files match the stated revisions. Both target CUDA translation units were rebuilt; unrelated native objects/runtime are held fixed. This is a matched component comparison, not a fresh whole-main build or an end-to-end model benchmark.

| Q / valid K / top-k | Backend | Without PR / with PR median µs | Latency change | Without PR / with PR extra live MiB |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 / 4096 / 512 | cooperative (unchanged control) | 7.504 / 7.488 | -0.21% | 64.123 / 64.123 |
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | persistent | 7.616 / 6.784 | -10.92% | 66.000 / 0.000 |
| 256 / 8192 / 1024 | persistent | 15.648 / 15.456 | -1.23% | 256.498 / 0.000 |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | persistent | 47.072 / 31.392 | -33.31% | 128.248 / 0.000 |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | persistent | 78.240 / 43.488 | -44.42% | 128.248 / 0.000 |

W=262144, row stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576; valid K length is separate. Small-Q cooperative is an unaffected control: both arms still widen and consume FP32, and its 0.21% timing difference is not claimed as an optimization gain. Persistent cases skip the widening in the PR. The longer-context results include removing that conversion; they must not be described as a 33–44% speedup of the top-k kernel alone. No universal speedup or no-regression claim is made for unmeasured shapes/backends/hardware.

<details>
<summary>Per-process medians and memory interpretation</summary>

| Q / valid K / top-k | Baseline run medians µs | PR run medians µs |
|---|---|---|
| 64 / 4096 / 512 | 7.4880, 7.5200 | 7.4880, 7.4880 |
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 7.6320, 7.6160 | 6.7840, 6.7680 |
| 256 / 8192 / 1024 | 15.6480, 15.6480 | 15.4080, 15.4880 |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 46.9120, 47.2000 | 31.4555, 31.2960 |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 78.1755, 78.2400 | 43.5200, 43.3920 |

Extra live peak excludes the already allocated BF16 inputs, outputs and workspace. Zero extra allocation does not mean zero total device/model memory. Graph-private reservations agree across repeats: Q64 66→66 MiB; Q65 66→0 MiB; Q256 258→0 MiB; both Q128 cases 130→0 MiB. Allocator reservation can exceed live tensor bytes. Profiling reservation is unchanged, so increased model KV capacity is not claimed.

All four arms at each shape have identical input hashes and selected-score bit bags, pass valid/unique-index checks, preserve input bits, and witness the expected conversion/dtype/backend behavior. Baseline FP32 widening is bit-exact against the fixed BF16 scores. Prior experiments are archived under their original baselines; their numbers are not mixed into this table.

</details>

**Expanded DeepSeek configuration coverage (GB200, job 41191).** Eighteen additional persistent-path cases use checkpoint-derived top-k and capacity, covering 16K/32K/64K raw contexts, Q=128/512/1024, uniform and mixed valid lengths, empty rows, and rows shorter than top-k. All 18 measured full-stage medians improve by **5.85%–39.66%** versus the same pre-PR baseline; no cooperative performance points were rerun. Pre-commit checks passed for the final helper delta. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation and this description.

## Details

The aligned BF16 vector-load helpers use the same packed integer load and bit-expansion implementation as #62172; scalar and guarded tail loads remain available. FP32 overloads are unchanged.

### BF16 and FP32 load behavior

The helpers separate the input storage type from the existing FP32 selection arithmetic:

| Helper | BF16 input | FP32 input |
|---|---|---|
| `to_float(x)` | Widen one BF16 value with `__bfloat162float(x)` | Identity: `return x;` |
| `load_score2(ptr)` | Read 4 bytes containing two BF16 values and expand them to two FP32 values (8 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float2` load (8 input bytes) |
| `load_score4(ptr)` | Read 8 bytes containing four BF16 values and expand them to four FP32 values (16 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float4` load (16 input bytes) |
| Guarded tail load | Read only valid BF16 elements, widen individually, and fill invalid elements with negative infinity | Retain the existing FP32 predicated-load implementation |

For the aligned four-score BF16 helper, [`topk_histogram_4096.cuh:78–82`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L78-L82) contains:

```cpp
const uint2 raw = *reinterpret_cast<const uint2*>(ptr);
return make_float4(
    __uint_as_float(raw.x << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.x & 0xFFFF0000u),
    __uint_as_float(raw.y << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.y & 0xFFFF0000u));
```

`uint2` contains two 32-bit words, so the input payload is 8 bytes. Each word holds two BF16 values. The shifts and masks place each BF16 bit pattern in the upper 16 bits of its own FP32 word; `__uint_as_float` reinterprets that word as a float. `make_float4` returns four 32-bit values: **8 input bytes become 16 bytes of FP32 values, not 32 bytes**. These values feed the kernel's existing FP32 register computation; the helper does not allocate or write a full FP32 logits tensor in global memory.

The [FP32 scalar overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L73) returns its input unchanged, and the [FP32 four-score overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L75-L77) retains `*reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(ptr)`. FP32 inputs are never downcast to BF16.


Code references: [BF16-to-FP32 register conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L71-L92), [backend capability query](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py#L236-L255), and [conditional full-tensor conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L951-L954).

BF16 input is widened losslessly on load; this avoids materializing FP32 logits in global memory. All existing raw-score rereads, including exact overflow recovery, accept the input type and immediately widen it. The FP32 comparison keys, candidate/refinement logic and backend thresholds are preserved. Candidate-block selection retains FP32 compact scores for auto/persistent so this change does not alter that selection stage's arithmetic.

The capability query reports input support; it does not change `resolve_backend()` or choose a backend by measured speed. It inspects host shape/type metadata without reading GPU tensor values. Cooperative continues to receive FP32. BF16 native persistent requires at least 128 KiB opt-in shared memory and contiguous columns. Existing addressing limits remain unchanged; large-row measurements do not cross the pre-existing filtered uint32 row-offset limit.

### Integration with #62172

The two features can coexist and share `takes_bf16_logits()` plus the same BF16 load helpers. The local reconciled version was validated as described above. **Current online heads still require rebase/conflict resolution**; helper alignment alone does not make them a clean merge.

Whichever PR merges second should:

- Combine cooperative and persistent capability predicates and their test expectations, retaining the existing explicit DeepSelect support.
- Preserve main's exact-overflow correction from #62936 when rebasing the older cooperative branch.
- Retain guarded BF16 predicated loads needed by persistent, instead of importing the cooperative-only assertion that rejects that instantiation.
- Preserve small-Q auto's FP32/cooperative fallback where only the widened stride satisfies TMA alignment, and preserve FP32 compact candidate-block scores for explicit cooperative as well. These integration-policy guards were included in the local validated reconciliation.

No cooperative implementation is copied into this standalone persistent PR. Cooperative-first followed by this PR rebasing onto the shared interface is one straightforward merge order; either order requires the same reconciliation.

commits.pr_title: [RL] NCCL weight transfer: release cached memory after a weight update
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

After an NCCL weight update, release the unused memory held by torch's caching allocator: one `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` at the end of `NCCLWeightTransferEngine.finish_weight_update`. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477); independent of the other PRs.

## Claims

- After every NCCL weight update, the server's torch reserved memory is back to its cold-start level. On Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (TP=2), each rank has 3.7–4.4 GiB more free device memory after a sync than on main.
- Weights, accuracy, throughput and KV cache size are unchanged.
- Cost: the next update allocates its receive buffers again. Median sync time went from 6.67 s to 7.13 s (+7%, one run per arm).

## Validation

Both setups use GB200 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 with the server at TP=2. The trainer runs on other GPUs and sends the weights over NCCL.

**Weight-sync bench.** The [state-transition verifier](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier) `run_bench.py` setup:
- trainer `fsdp=2`, `--backend nccl`;
- 1 warmup + 3 measured syncs, each with a perturbed checkpoint;
- server `--max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`;
- every tensor is compared against a fresh server at the end.

Server memory per rank after each sync (all four syncs agree within 2 MiB):

| | allocated | reserved | device free | median sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 146.30 GiB | 150.72 GiB | 29.82 GiB | 6.67 s |
| this PR | 146.28 GiB | 146.36 GiB | 34.18 GiB | 7.13 s |

Weights compared with a fresh server: 0 mismatched, 0 moved, in both arms. Both arms also report the same 192 `moe_quant_config._w1/_w2.scale` tensors re-created by layerwise reload; that happens on main and is unrelated to this change.

**A/B after one update.** Main vs this PR on the same nightly wheel, same node, back to back:
- each arm cold starts, receives one NCCL update of the same checkpoint, then is measured;
- GSM8K: 5-shot greedy, all 1319 questions;
- throughput: `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64;
- server: `--max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`.

| | GSM8K | output tok/s | KV cache | device free after the sync | torch reserved after the sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.8954 | 8276 | 2.794M | 31.23 GiB | 147.92 GiB |
| this PR | 0.8946 | 8407 | 2.794M | 34.89 GiB | 144.27 GiB |

- **Noise:** GSM8K differs by one question and throughput by 1.6%. Running the same code as both arms gives ±1 question and 1.8%.
- **Memory:** with this PR, reserved memory after the sync equals its cold-start value. Free memory is 0.62 GiB below cold start, which is the NCCL communicator created during the first sync. On main it is 4.28 GiB below.
- **Why the gain differs from the bench (3.66 vs 4.36 GiB):** this setup uses a different nightly, a different `--max-model-len`, and one sync instead of four.

**CI:** no unit test. The effect only shows up in device memory after a real NCCL update between two processes. The existing NCCL engine tests don't run one, and a mocked test would only assert that the call happens.

## Details

After `finalize_layerwise_reload`, the caching allocator keeps the freed receive buffers and post-load temporaries reserved. Torch can reuse that memory; nothing outside torch can. That includes other processes on the GPU (e.g. a colocated trainer) and allocations that bypass the caching allocator (NCCL, e.g. a newly created communicator).

`empty_cache()` releases the unused cached segments once per update, after all weights are loaded, so the transfer itself is unaffected. Blocks still in use and CUDA graph pools are not touched. `base_loader.py` already calls `empty_cache()` after loading and after post-processing at cold start.

Only the NCCL engine is changed, as that is the path measured here. The other layerwise engines (IPC, M2N, sharded RDT) could get the same call in a follow-up.

## Overview

Build mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d once into the ROCm CI test image instead of compiling them from source at the start of every AMD hybrid-model job. This is the AMD counterpart of #58795, which does the same for the CUDA image and does not touch AMD steps, so it is not a duplicate.

## Claims

- Removes a ~3.2 min source build from every run of the MI355 DPX Language Models (Hybrid) shards, Granite Language Model Compatibility and Language Models (Extended Generation), and ~5.5 min from the nightly MI300 Language Models (Extended Generation).
- At the last 14 days' run rate (~157 runs/day of each of the three per-commit MI355 jobs, main + PRs), that frees ~25 MI355 DPX agent-hours per day.
- MI355 DPX Hybrid Shard 2 (29-31 min) is the longest AMD job in recent main builds, so the AMD part of a build finishes up to ~3 min sooner when it is the last job (2 of the last 6 main builds).
- No change to what is tested: the same mamba commit the jobs already resolve (269cbe65, 2.2.6.post3) and causal-conv1d v1.6.0 (da6dbaa9).

## Validation

CI, [build 98454](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98454): all 10 AMD jobs passed, including the one-time runtime/test-deps rebuild.

## Details

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] [Tokenizer] Preserve Hub model identity when loading tokenizer snapshots
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This fixes a tokenizer-routing regression introduced by #60825, "[Performance]
Load HF tokenizers and processors from a local snapshot." Loading tokenizer
files from a local snapshot can hide the original Hugging Face repository ID
from Transformers.

In `transformers.models.auto.tokenization_auto`,
`MODEL_IDS_TO_TOKENIZERS_BACKEND` routes specific Hub IDs, including
`deepseek-ai/deepseek-coder-*`, to `TokenizersBackend` by matching
`config._name_or_path`. When the config is loaded from the snapshot, that is a
local path, the pattern never matches, and the class declared on the Hub
(`LlamaTokenizerFast`) is used instead, which drops every space. That can change the
input token IDs passed to the model and affect generated output.

The fix retains local-snapshot loading while restoring the original Hub ID on
a copy of the config passed to `AutoTokenizer`. The original config remains
unchanged, and the tokenizer continues to report the Hub ID as its
`name_or_path`.


## Validation
