commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 token offset overflows in Qwen3.5 attention and GDN prefill kernels
commits.pr_body:
_Requested by **Simon**_ ## Overview Fixes #63759. Several Triton kernels on the Qwen3.5 prefill path multiply an int32 token index by a row stride before adding it to a pointer. Triton passes integer arguments below 2^31 as int32, and `tl.program_id`, `tl.arange` and the int32 `query_start_loc` are int32 too, so the offset wraps once `token * stride >= 2^31`. The result is wrong outputs or an illegal memory access. This PR computes those offsets in int64, one commit per kernel, each with a regression test. | Kernel | Triggers when (Qwen3.5-9B unless noted) | Fix | |---|---|---| | `_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate_kernel` (`fused_qk_norm_rope.py`) | token index >= 209,716 (qkv row stride 10,240), i.e. a 209,717-token step; hit in the startup profile run | `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` | | `store_cache_checkpoints_kernel` (`mamba/checkpoint.py`) | token index >= 174,763 (qkvz stride 12,288); real prefills with prefix caching only | int64 `token_idx` before `* x_stride_0` | | `_fused_post_conv_kernel` (`fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv.py`) | token index >= 262,144 (conv row stride 8,192) | int64 per-block base offset, int32 in-block offsets | | `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` (`chunk_delta_h.py`), spotted by reviewer Roberto (`LopezCastroRoberto`) | H=64: 2+ sequences with a later one starting at token >= 131,072 | int64 before `* V * K` (as `chunk_o.py`), also h0/ht | | `solve_tril` merge kernels (`solve_tril.py`) | H=64: a sequence with rows past 524,288, or one starting at >= 524,288 | int64 base offset and row index (16/32/64 kernels) | | `layer_norm_fwd_kernel` for `RMSNormGated` (`layernorm_guard.py`) | H=64: 262,145 tokens (`num_tokens * H * 128 >= 2^31`), when the `rms_norm_gated` custom op is enabled, e.g. `--enforce-eager` | int64 first row of each block | For the last three, thresholds double at H=32. The rest of the path (`causal_conv1d`, `layernorm_gated`, `gather_initial_states`, `scatter_states`, Mamba2 `ssd_checkpoint`, FlashInfer GDN prefill) already uses int64 offsets. The KDA and Qwen4Exp PLE exporters share the fixed checkpoint kernel. Related: #43166 (closed) fixed the same overflow in the CUDA `fused_qk_norm_rope` kernel; #51406 (open) enables the first kernel on ROCm, so ROCm gets the bug and this fix. ## Claims - On main, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --max-num-batched-tokens 209717` (or 263,168) fails in the startup profile run with an illegal memory access in `_fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate_kernel`. With this PR it starts and serves correctly. - With prefix caching, one prefill step can fill the budget. At 263,168, a 258,798-token prompt and a 262,784-token two-prompt batch serve correctly; without the checkpoint and post-conv commits they crash in those kernels. - Each kernel matches its previous output below its threshold and the reference above it. - Perf: about +1% on the gate kernel (141.2 vs 139.7 us at 8,192 tokens), +2.2% on post-conv, 0.2 us on the checkpoint export, and 0 to 3% on the follow-ups (`chunk_delta_h` 0% / -3.0%, `solve_tril` +1.1%, `rmsnorm_gated` +2.4 to +3.1%). ## Validation 1x B200, torch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, main `ffcabb8c7a`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` at `c202236235`. "Base" is main plus only the new tests. ```bash pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_gate.py -k int64_row_offset pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py -k int64_token_offset pytest -v tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -k int64_token_offset pytest -v tests/kernels/fla/test_chunk_int64_offsets.py pytest -v tests/kernels/fla/test_fla_layernorm_guard.py -k int64_row_offset ``` - Every new test fails on base (77.1% / 93.4% of q mismatched for the gate and post-conv kernels, illegal memory access for the other four) and passes with this PR. Existing tests in these files, `tests/kernels/fla`, `test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py` and `test_gdn_output_projection.py` pass. - Server (`--max-num-batched-tokens` 209,717 and 263,168, prefix caching on, compiled and eager): base fails in the profile run; this PR finds needles near the start and end of a 196,883 / 258,798-token prompt, answers both prompts of the 262,784-token batch, scores gsm 8/8, and matches base outputs at the default budget of 16,384. - Latency: kernels timed side by side with `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph` (follow-ups with `do_bench`), median of alternating rounds; a base-vs-base control gave 1.000 and outputs are bitwise equal to base. ## Details - Tests run each kernel just past its boundary on a realistic layout (packed qkv/qkvz buffers, contiguous conv output) and compare those rows with a reference. They need about 4 to 21 GB, skip when free device memory is short, and take a few seconds each. The gate test's CI step did not list `fused_qk_norm_rope.py` in `source_file_dependencies`, so this PR adds it there and to the AMD mirror; the other tests run in steps that already depend on their kernels. - Post-conv: an int64 per-token offset vector is a one-line change but costs 4.4% instead of 2.2%, so the PR uses an int64 base pointer. For `rmsnorm_gated` and `solve_tril` both approaches timed the same, so the simpler diff is kept. - Not fixed here: at these budgets Qwen3.5-9B needs a lower `--gpu-memory-utilization` than 0.92, with or without this PR (FlashInfer autotune and compiled-graph OOMs). The runs above used 0.88 at 209,717 and 0.84 at 263,168. ---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Split-vocabulary Triton argmax for the DSpark greedy draft
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Replace the DSpark greedy draft's full-vocabulary `torch.argmax` with a two-stage Triton split-vocabulary reduction. The reduction preserves int64 outputs, first-index ties, and NaN semantics, with a Torch fallback for unsupported inputs. With `num_speculative_tokens=5`, each decode step runs five dependency-chained greedy selections (`_sample_sequential`'s `for i in range(n_spec)` loop), so the per-call saving compounds five-fold per step.

Scope is limited to `draft_sample_method="greedy"`: `self.draft_logits` is allocated only for `draft_sample_method="probabilistic"`, so the `draft_logits is None` branch is exactly the greedy path. The probabilistic path (`gumbel_sample`) already reduces over vocabulary chunks and is unchanged; the draft backbone, non-greedy sampling, and verification are untouched. The generic `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` argmax is left alone — DSpark overrides `_sample_logits` and never reaches it.

Parallelism: the drafter's logits are the all-gathered, padding-narrowed output of `LogitsProcessor` (`ParallelLMHead` + all-gather when `tp_size > 1`), so every TP rank reduces the same full-vocabulary tensor. The comparator is a total order, so the result does not depend on the reduction order or on the split count, and every rank selects the same draft id. The kernel issues no collectives and no host synchronization, so it does not perturb DP/EP lockstep (DP padding is handled in `_run_model`, before sampling) and it is unaffected by sequence parallelism, which is internal to the backbone forward.

CUDA Graph and JIT: the kernels allocate only from the capturing stream's pool and never synchronize with the host, so they are captured with the rest of the DSpark draft step. They specialize on the vocabulary size, row stride, and dtype, which are fixed per deployment; the row count is only a grid dimension. They are therefore compiled once, in the profiling dummy run before capture, and do not JIT during serving.

### Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs for overlapping work (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search ...` over "dspark", "argmax draft sampling", "split argmax reduction vocabulary"). The nearest ones target different code:

- [#57319](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57319) fuses the Gumbel sampler's argmax and gather — the probabilistic path, not greedy drafting.
- [#56995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56995) implements `get_top_tokens()` for the generic MTP drafter, i.e. the TP-communication reduction (`use_local_argmax_reduction`). That path is unavailable to DSpark, whose Markov bias needs dense logits; config validation rejects the combination.
- [#50737](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50737) and [#56694](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56694) optimize the Markov head (addmm, top-k pruning) in the same loop, not the selection itself.
- [#50843](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50843) bounds tile-local argmax indices in existing sampler kernels.


## Test Result

GB200 ×4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4; NCCL DMA-BUF disabled. Baseline and candidate differ only in the greedy draft argmax. Serving config: DSpark `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `draft_sample_method=greedy`, synthetic acceptance 6.0, adaptive verification off; Mega MoE (`deep_gemm_mega_moe`); FlashMLA DSV4.1 attention with MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer; fp8 KV cache; max 128 sequences, 16384 max batched tokens, 131072 max model length; Engram embeddings shared across DP; prefix caching disabled; GPU memory utilization 0.9; seed 42.

8192 input / 1024 forced output; `3×concurrency` requests per run; identical prompt IDs and request seeds, temperature=1/top_p=0.95. Same-node baseline then optimized, three measurements per concurrency, each preceded by full-workload warmup.

Median of three runs, **baseline → optimized**, milliseconds. ITL measures streaming-event gaps, typically six tokens per event (five drafts plus the bonus token), i.e. one engine decode step.

| Concurrency | TPOT P50 | ITL P50 | ITL P90 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.516 → 1.499 | 9.105 → 8.996 | 9.243 → 9.119 |
| 16 | 2.142 → 2.216 | 11.927 → 11.768 | 12.345 → 12.210 |
| 32 | 2.966 → 2.900 | 13.583 → 13.538 | 14.210 → 14.145 |
| 128 | 8.141 → 7.878 | 19.383 → 19.105 | 23.053 → 21.701 |

Greedy argmax microbenchmark: GB200, BF16, vocabulary=129280; CUDA Graph + CUPTI, cold L2, ABBA order. Measures the full two-kernel GPU span, including the gap between them. M is the number of draft-logit rows per call, not verification tokens. These are isolated single-GPU measurements, so `5 × delta` is an upper bound on the per-step saving: ~195 μs at M=1, ~193 μs at M=8, ~182 μs at M=32, down to ~142 μs at M=128.

| M | Torch argmax μs | Split argmax μs | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 43.424 | 4.352 | 9.98× |
| 2 | 42.912 | 4.592 | 9.34× |
| 4 | 43.360 | 4.832 | 8.97× |
| 8 | 43.680 | 5.088 | 8.58× |
| 16 | 43.968 | 6.080 | 7.23× |
| 32 | 44.415 | 7.968 | 5.57× |
| 64 | 44.576 | 11.136 | 4.00× |
| 128 | 45.344 | 16.928 | 2.68× |

In situ the logits are still in L2, since the Markov-bias add has just written them. With a hot L2 (CUDA Graph, CUDA events), Torch argmax is ~26 μs across M, while the split argmax is 3.3 / 4.0 / 6.3 / 14.9 μs at M=1 / 8 / 32 / 128. The resulting 5 × 22.6 ≈ 113 μs per-step saving at M=1 matches the ~109 μs ITL P50 drop at concurrency 1.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py -k greedy_argmax -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/greedy_argmax.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py
```

- 6 greedy_argmax tests passed, covering BF16/FP32, random rows, first-index ties across blocks, NaN/Inf, vocabulary boundaries, and strided offset rows (the TP padding-narrowed layout). Flipping the comparator's tie-break to the last index makes all 6 fail.
- DEP4 serving completed with identical acceptance sequences and verification counts across arms.
- Synthetic acceptance is a performance control, not a model-quality evaluation; no task-accuracy evaluation was run. Greedy selection is bit-exact against `torch.argmax`, so acceptance behavior is unchanged by construction.
- pre-commit checks passed on all touched files.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation; every line was reviewed and the tests and benchmarks above were run by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Skip more weight formats in the tokenizer/processor snapshot
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #63925.

Since #60825, loading a tokenizer or processor first downloads every Hub file not matched by `_WEIGHT_FILE_PATTERNS`. That list misses several weight formats that classic repos still ship, so vLLM downloads unused weights before loading the model: about 1.57 GB extra for `openai-community/gpt2` and 534 MB for `google-bert/bert-base-uncased`. This adds those formats to the list.

## Claims

- The tokenizer/processor snapshot no longer downloads rust-bert (`*.ot`), TFLite, Core ML (`*.mlmodel`, `*.mlpackage/*`), NeMo, NumPy (`*.npy`, `*.npz`) or PaddlePaddle (`*.pdparams`) files.
- Tokenizer, processor and config files are still downloaded.

## Validation

New parametrized tests in `tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py` apply `_WEIGHT_FILE_PATTERNS` with `huggingface_hub.utils.filter_repo_objects` (the filter `snapshot_download` uses) to real file names from `openai-community/gpt2` and `google-bert/bert-base-uncased`. No network access.

Before (patterns reverted):

```text
$ pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[rust_model.ot]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[64.tflite]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[64-fp16.tflite]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[coreml/fill-mask/float32_model.mlpackage/Data/com.apple.CoreML/model.mlmodel]
FAILED ...::test_non_weight_snapshot_skips_weight_files[coreml/fill-mask/float32_model.mlpackage/Manifest.json]
5 failed, 22 passed
```

After:

```text
$ pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_repo_utils.py
27 passed
```

Against the live Hub file lists (captures the `ignore_patterns` passed to `snapshot_download` and filters `HfApi().model_info(repo).siblings`), files over 50 MB that the snapshot would fetch:

| Repo | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `openai-community/gpt2` | `rust_model.ot`, `64.tflite`, `64-fp16.tflite`, `64-8bits.tflite` (~1.57 GB) | none |
| `google-bert/bert-base-uncased` | `rust_model.ot` (534 MB) | none |

`tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py` and `tests/transformers_utils/test_processor.py` pass except `test_hub_processor_loads_from_local_snapshot` and `test_processor_reuses_tokenizer_snapshot`, which fail identically on main in my environment (macOS, no torchvision). `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

## Details

The `typos` hook flags the `ot` extension, so `ot` is added to `[tool.typos.default.extend-words]` next to the other short words already there (`fo`, `nd`, `ba`).

This keeps the deny-list approach from #60825. An allow-list of tokenizer/processor files would close the gap for future formats too, but it risks missing files that custom processors or `trust_remote_code` tokenizers need; happy to switch if preferred.

Not a duplicate: searching issues and PRs for `_WEIGHT_FILE_PATTERNS`, `get_non_weight_snapshot_path`, `rust_model.ot` and "tokenizer snapshot weights" finds only #60825 and #61272; #63482 touches the same module but not the patterns.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix depyf incompatibility with Inductor's set_sys_modules
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Any `torch.compile` run with `debug_dump_path` set fails once compilation reaches an autotune code block, because depyf's `load_by_key_path` hook does not accept Inductor's `set_sys_modules` argument. A compatibility shim gives the hook `**kwargs` and forwards them.

Seen on the `PyTorch Fullgraph` step in [Buildkite #93716](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93716/list?jid=01a11edf-b64d-4af0-91f8-60f8f72d7308&tab=output).

## Claims

- Fixes `InductorError: RuntimeError: Failed to run autotuning code block: patched_load_by_key_path() got an unexpected keyword argument 'set_sys_modules'`.
- Not platform-specific. The failing step is a ROCm mirror, but nothing in the cause or the fix is vendor-dependent; it needs only a cold compile cache.
- The shim is conditional on depyf's hook signature, so it disables itself if depyf ever ships a fix.
- The existing depyf test could not catch this. It was one parametrization of `test_custom_compile_config`, which reuses vLLM's on-disk compile cache, so on a persistent agent it usually verified nothing. It is now a separate test that disables the cache.
- Adds a CPU-only unit test that reproduces the incompatibility in 2.3 s, instead of only through a GPU end-to-end run.
- Costs 27 s on `PyTorch Fullgraph` and 11 s on `PyTorch Compilation`, both against budgets of 90 and 30 minutes. The other six parametrizations keep using the cache.
- Not fixed: depyf's other two hooks are unchanged. Both were audited and are already compatible.

## Validation

1× AMD MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2, PyTorch `2.13.0+git733fca1`, depyf 0.20.0, vLLM `19c0bed584`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New unit tests, CPU only | 6 passed, 2.3 s |
| End-to-end depyf test, cold cache, after the fix | passed, 50.6 s |
| Same, before the fix | failed, 25.8 s |
| Same, before the fix, warm cache | passed, 23.3 s |
| Unit tests with the shim forcibly disabled | 4 of 6 failed |

The last two rows are the ones that matter. The warm pass is why this reached `main`: with a populated cache nothing is compiled, depyf's hook is never called, and the test is green. The forced-disable run confirms the new tests measure the fix rather than the environment.

## Details

`depyf.prepare_debug` replaces `PyCodeCache.load_by_key_path` with a hook that dumps each generated kernel before loading it. The hook's signature is frozen at `(key, path, linemap, attrs)`, and `generate_and_run_autotune_block` now also passes `set_sys_modules`. The resulting `TypeError` is raised inside the `exec` of the tuning block, so it surfaces as an `InductorError` about the autotune block rather than as anything mentioning depyf.

Bumping the pin is not available: 0.20.0 is the last release upstream published, its repository has had no commits since that release, and four pull requests have been open without review. The hook is therefore patched in vLLM, in the way depyf already handles this for `lazy_format_graph_code`: accept `**kwargs` and forward them.

The shim forwards the keyword rather than dropping it. Dropping it would also make the call succeed, while quietly reintroducing the `sys.modules` exhaustion that pytorch#184285 fixed; one of the unit tests pins exactly that. Both vLLM entry points into depyf go through the shim, so neither can miss the patch.

## Overview

Fix loading sharded checkpoints from Hugging Face repository IDs. `load_weights()` previously treated the repository ID as a local path, causing shard lookup to fail.

## Claims

- Support HF repository IDs supplied through either `model` or `model_weights`.
- Honor the configured revision, download directory, and ignore patterns.
- Preserve existing handling for local directories and S3 paths.

## Validation

Added one parameterized regression test covering local checkpoints, HF repository IDs, and `model_weights` overrides. It uses real safetensors weights and mocks HF downloads and distributed parallel-state accessors.

- New regression cases before the fix: **2 failed, 1 passed**.
- Selected CPU tests after the fix, including all three regression cases: **28 passed, 6 deselected**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_sharded_state_loader.py \
  -k 'filter_subtensors or default_pattern or save_model or resolves_checkpoint_path' -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/model_loader/sharded_state_loader.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_sharded_state_loader.py
```

Full GPU integration, live HF downloads, and the RunAI backend were not tested locally.

## Details

Resolve the selected weight source using the existing `_prepare_weights()` method before searching for shard files. This converts HF repository IDs into local snapshot paths while retaining the existing handling for local directories and S3 paths.

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Initial support for fault tolerant ep using scale-down
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR adds **scale-down** to the vLLM fault tolerance (FT) framework for DP+EP
MoE deployments in external-LB mode.

The existing FT framework (`--enable-fault-tolerance`) supports `retry` —
reinitializing the DP process group after a transient fault where all ranks
survive. When a DP rank dies permanently (hardware failure, OOM kill), `retry`
is insufficient: the dead rank's expert slots are unreachable and the EPLB
placement tables reference slots that no longer exist.

**Scale-down** (`POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply` with `instruction: "scale_down"`)
removes dead DP ranks, masks the corresponding EP ranks at the all2all kernel
level, redistributes orphaned logical experts onto surviving ranks using EPLB
redundant slots, selectively reloads only the reassigned expert weights from
disk, rebuilds the DP Gloo group over the surviving slots, and resumes
inference — without a full restart.

Recovery is **orchestrator-driven**: engines detect faults, report status, and
wait for an explicit command. There is no self-recovery path.

---

## Operator Contract

This section is the interface an external controller (Kubernetes operator,
Dynamo, or any service framework) can rely on.

### Requirements

- **External load balancer mode only**: one engine per API server
  (`--api-server-count=1 --data-parallel-size-local=1`). Validated at startup
  (`arg_utils.py`); the server refuses to start otherwise. Internal LB is not
  supported.
- **MoE model with DP+EP** and an all2all backend that supports timeouts:
  `deepep_low_latency` or `nixl_ep`. Validated at worker creation
  (`WorkerSentinel.__init__`). Without one of these, a dead rank hangs the whole
  cluster and none of this document applies.
- **`scale_down` additionally requires EPLB with `num_redundant_experts > 0`** —
  redundant replicas are what survivors use to cover the removed rank. Validated
  at the worker layer; a deployment without it fails the command with a clear
  `ft_error`.
- **Not supported: prefill context parallelism** (`prefill_context_parallel_size
  > 1`). Rejected at worker creation — the TP sibling barrier and group reinit
  have no PCP equivalents.
- **`scale_down` partial weight reload supports the default weight loader only.**
  The reload goes through `get_model_loader`, and only `DefaultModelLoader`
  implements `get_all_weights`; every other loader raises `NotImplementedError`.
  This is reached only when the redistribution actually reassigns experts.

Startup flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--enable-fault-tolerance` | Turns the feature on. Also forces DP sync onto the Gloo CPU group. |
| `--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds N` | How quickly a surviving rank declares a silent peer dead. |
| `--fault-tolerance-config='{"engine_recovery_timeout_sec": 120}'` | How long a faulted engine waits for your command before giving up and exiting. |

### Endpoints

**`POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply`** — send a command. Asynchronous: returns
`202 Accepted` immediately and runs the recovery in the background. Poll
`status` for the outcome. **[implemented]**

The endpoints exist **only** under the `/v1` prefix. Earlier revisions of this
branch also exposed unprefixed `/fault_tolerance/apply|status` aliases; those
have been **removed**.

`retry` — clean up and resume, keeping all ranks:

```json
{"instruction": "retry", "params": {}}
```

`scale_down` — permanently remove dead ranks and continue without them:

```json
{"instruction": "scale_down", "params": {"removed_dp_ranks": [1]}}
```

**`GET /v1/fault_tolerance/status`** — observe everything. **[implemented]**

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "total_engines": 1,
  "engines": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "status": "unhealthy",
      "fault_info": "RuntimeError",
      "mask": [1, 0],
      "ft_state": "failed",
      "last_ft_request_id": "<uuid>",
      "ft_error": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `status` | `healthy` \| `unhealthy` \| `diagnosing` \| `dead` — engine health. |
| `fault_info` | (only when `unhealthy`) exception type, or `"Recovery failed; full restart required"` on a terminal scale-down failure. |
| `mask` | (only when `unhealthy`) which EP peers this engine lost contact with, `1` = unreachable, in **EP** coordinates. |
| `ft_state` | Lifecycle of the most recent `apply`: `recovering` (in flight) or `failed`. Absent when idle. |
| `last_ft_request_id` | The `request_id` the state refers to. Recorded at **dispatch**, so it identifies the active operation even for a request that is still running. |
| `ft_error` | Why that request failed. Only meaningful once `ft_state` is `failed`. |


### Which engines can accept a command

Commands are accepted **only while an engine is `unhealthy`** — the state it enters
after detecting a fault and before recovery:

| Status | Meaning | Accepts commands? |
|---|---|---|
| `unhealthy` | Detected a fault, waiting for you | **Yes** |
| `diagnosing` | Mask query in flight (transient) | No — keep polling |
| `healthy` | No fault detected | No — `status is HEALTHY` |
| `dead` | The engine process is gone | No — `status is DEAD` |

- **`retry` can be repeated.** If it fails, the engine stays `unhealthy` and
  accepts another attempt (send a fresh `request_id`) until
  `engine_recovery_timeout_sec` expires.
- **A failed `scale_down` is terminal.** Once it passes request validation, any
  failure moves the engine to `dead` and the instance has to be restarted —
  expert migration between ranks cannot be undone.

A `healthy` engine that never becomes `unhealthy` while its peers are faulted is
most likely wedged (e.g. blocked in a collective with no timeout). It will not
accept a command, so the deployment has to be recreated.

Consequence for a controller: if Kubernetes diagnoses a failed rank *before*
vLLM's own timeouts fire, some survivors may still report `healthy` and
`scale_down` will be rejected with `reason: "status is HEALTHY"`. Wait for every
surviving engine to reach `unhealthy` on its own, then dispatch. All survivors
are guaranteed to get there eventually (all2all kernel timeout, or Gloo group
timeout on the control path). A proactive prepare/pause path that lets a
controller start recovery immediately is not implemented.


### Admission and health during a fault

- **[implemented] Admission goes false.** While FT is enabled and engine status
  is anything other than `healthy`, `AsyncLLM.add_request` raises
  `EngineFaultedError` → **HTTP 503**, so load balancers and SDKs retry on
  another instance.
- **[implemented] `/v1/fault_tolerance/status` stays reachable** throughout —
  it is served by the API server process, independent of the engine busy loop.
- **`/health` reports liveness, not FT state.** `check_health()` raises only when
  the engine process itself is gone (`engine_dead or not is_running`), so an
  engine that is `unhealthy` but alive still returns **200**. This is
  intentional: `/health` answers "is this process up", and the FT-specific
  question "should this instance take traffic" is answered by `add_request`
  returning **503** and by `/v1/fault_tolerance/status`. Point readiness at
  `/v1/fault_tolerance/status`, not at `/health`.

### Concurrency and idempotency of `apply`

- **[implemented] One recovery at a time per engine.** A command arriving while
  another recovery is in flight is rejected with
  `reason: "another recovery is in progress"`. This rejection does **not**
  overwrite `ft_state` / `last_ft_request_id` / `ft_error`, so the controller can
  still read which request *is* running — that is the "competing recovery
  reports the active operation" behavior.
- **[implemented] Replay after success is rejected**: recovery leaves the engine
  `healthy`, and the command gate only accepts commands while `unhealthy`, so a
  replay fails fast with `status is HEALTHY`.
- **Send a fresh `request_id` per round.** The `request_id` is recorded in
  `status` and namespaces the round's coordination keys in the per-round
  recovery store; the design does not treat a repeated `request_id` as a
  duplicate to suppress. A competing recovery is rejected and reports the active
  operation through `last_ft_request_id`.

### Rules that matter

- **`removed_dp_ranks` uses original rank IDs.** Ranks keep their startup IDs
  forever; a removed rank stays as an empty slot and nothing is renumbered. The
  set is cumulative-safe: you may include ranks removed in earlier rounds (the
  increment is what gets applied) but it must contain at least one new rank.
- **Recovery is all-or-nothing across engines.** Survivors vote
  (`all_reduce(MIN)` over one success bit on the rebuilt DP group); only
  unanimous success resumes serving.
- **After the first committed `scale_down`, engines never idle.** They keep
  stepping dummy batches when there is no traffic, which doubles as continuous
  fault detection. Expect extra power draw; before the first scale-down, idle
  behavior is unchanged.
- **Invalid commands are rejected up front and are non-terminal.** Bad
  `removed_dp_ranks` or missing store params produce a recorded `ft_error`; the
  controller re-reads status and re-issues.

---

## Design

### Slots model — EP topology never changes

From vLLM's point of view a removed rank remains an **empty slot**:
`parallel_config.data_parallel_size` / `data_parallel_rank` stay frozen at their
initial values and DP rank ids never change. There is exactly one coordinate
system (original) and no densification anywhere. Only the rebuilt Gloo
`cpu_group` uses dense internal ranks over `sorted(alive)`, computed at reinit
time and never written back to config.

The all2all kernel likewise keeps the original EP world size, with dead EP ranks
masked via `update_mask()` (both `deepep_low_latency` and `nixl_ep`). Keeping the
topology fixed is what avoids model re-init, graph recompile, and CUDA graph
re-capture on the recovery path.

### Engine-level flow

1. **Validate** `removed_dp_ranks` (non-empty, in range, excludes own rank,
   leaves ≥1 survivor) and require a non-empty increment over the cumulative
   dead set. Client errors here are non-terminal.
2. **Rebuild the TCPStore** if the store master (lowest alive rank) was just
   removed.
3. **Reinit the engine DP group** over `sorted(alive)` and create the per-round
   recovery store.
4. **Dispatch** to workers via `collective_rpc`, then **vote** — a unanimous
   `all_reduce(MIN)` over one success bit.
5. **Commit only after full success.** `data_parallel_master_ip` is committed
   inside the group reinit; `_dead_dp_ranks` is committed after the vote.

### Worker-level flow

1. Sync GPU, clean worker state (execute_model_state, kv_connector_output,
   input_batch).
2. **Validate the EPLB prerequisite** (EPLB state present with redundant
   experts). This is the platform-specific validation point, keeping the
   engine/client path backend-agnostic.
3. Clean all2all buffers (this also wipes kernel mask state).
4. **Mask** the dead EP ranks — computed from the engine-supplied **cumulative**
   `dead_dp_ranks`. The worker keeps no FT history; masks from earlier rounds are
   replayed from the engine's set, so `clean_buffers` never loses them. `retry`
   runs the same clean-and-replay logic.
5. **Redistribute experts** (see below).
6. **Reinit the Gloo DP group** over the surviving slots and mount the
   cumulative dead set on the DP group coordinator for dead-column
   neutralization.

### Expert redistribution

All operations are **deterministic with stable iteration order** — every
surviving rank produces bit-identical results with no cross-rank communication:

1. Mark dead columns in `physical_to_logical_map` as `-1`.
2. Steal slots from over-replicated experts (donors with >1 replica) to cover
   missing logical experts, interleaving across EP ranks for balanced loading.
3. Rebuild `logical_to_physical_map` and `logical_replica_count`.
4. Rebuild each FusedMoE layer's `_expert_map`.
5. Selectively reload **only reassigned** expert weights from disk.

Both checkpoint layouts are handled: per-expert checkpoints reload only the
reassigned `<layer>.<expert_id>.` weights; **fused** checkpoints (Qwen3-VL MoE,
gpt-oss — one tensor per layer holding all experts) reload the whole touched
layer tensor, which is correct because the weight loader writes each expert
through the rebuilt expert map. A `(layer, expert)` pair matching neither layout
raises a clear `RuntimeError`.

### Recovery commits only on a unanimous survivor vote

After worker dispatch, surviving engines `all_reduce(MIN)` one success bit over
the rebuilt DP group. A failed `retry` leaves the engine `unhealthy` and
retryable. A failed `scale_down` past request validation is terminal — the
engine reports `dead` and exits. Invalid commands are rejected up front with an
observable `ft_error`.

### `request_id` namespaces a recovery round

All engines in one round share the `request_id`, which namespaces that round's
coordination keys in the per-round recovery store so concurrent or stale rounds
cannot cross-talk. When empty it falls back to the engine's local reinit epoch.

---

## Implementation Notes

- **TP sibling lockstep barrier (TP > 1).** `_synchronize_dp_ranks` (v1) and
  `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (v2) run a per-step Gloo barrier over the TP
  CPU group when FT is enabled and `tp_size > 1`. A sibling whose peer stopped
  arriving fails on the host within `cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds`, never
  leaving an orphaned TP collective (e.g. fused allreduce kernels without
  timeout) on its device stream. The TP CPU group is rebuilt during worker
  `retry`. This and the dead-column fill are the only FT touchpoints on the hot
  path; cost is one loopback Gloo round trip per step.
- **Dead-column neutralization.** Under the slots model the DP allreduce tensors
  keep their original width and a dead rank's column stays `0` after the SUM
  allreduce, which is not neutral for `min` / `all(==1)` aggregations. After the
  allreduce each rank locally fills dead columns (from
  `get_dp_group().dead_dp_ranks`) with aggregate-neutral values. The fill happens
  *after* the allreduce — a pre-fill would be summed across all alive ranks.
  Known gap: the v2 `max_query_len` row is left at `0`, so an all-`None` vote
  reads as `0` when a dead column is present.
- **EPLB async state reset.** An `ft_reset_epoch` on the EPLB state lets the
  async worker detect a recovery and abandon in-flight transfers instead of
  applying stale results; the async thread survives exceptions when FT is
  enabled and stays alive so EPLB can resume after a retry.
- **Side-stream mask query.** Worker `query_mask` runs on a separate CUDA stream
  so a poisoned main stream cannot block the mask read that status reporting
  depends on.
- **Recovery port coordination (bind-and-hold).** Recovery rebuilds several Gloo
  groups whose members span processes. Ports are never pre-allocated via
  `get_open_port`; instead the group's rank-0 member binds a listening socket to
  port 0, publishes the port number through the per-round recovery store, and
  group init takes ownership of the held socket — so a stolen port cannot fail
  group init, which would be terminal for `scale_down`.
- **No idle pause after a committed scale-down.** The DP wave wake-up path
  depends on the DP coordinator, which has no failover, so once the dead set is
  non-empty the engine never idle-pauses and keeps stepping dummy batches. The
  32-step `sync_dp_state` allreduce is kept (it carries the pause consensus and
  doubles as idle-time fault detection), and explicit pause/resume (RL weight
  sync) is unaffected.

---

## Test Plan

**E2E tests** — `tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_fault_tolerance_e2e.py`, gated on
`has_nixl_ep()`:

1. `test_injected_fault_retry_recovers_all_ranks` (DP=2) — injected fault, all
   ranks `unhealthy`, `retry`, all ranks `healthy` and serving.
2. `test_scale_down_removes_dead_rank_and_recovers` (DP=4, EPLB with 32
   redundant experts) — SIGKILL rank 1's worker; survivors go `unhealthy`, the
   victim's engine goes `dead` and rejects `retry` with a recorded `ft_error`;
   `scale_down(removed_dp_ranks=[1])` to all survivors; all survivors return to
   `healthy` and serve completions.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_fault_tolerance_e2e.py -v -s
```

**Manual cluster validation** — external LB, 4 independent API servers, one
engine each; DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (MoE, 64 logical experts),
`--data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 2` (EP world 8),
`--enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend nixl_ep --enable-eplb`
(64 redundant experts, async), `--enable-fault-tolerance`,
`--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds 30`, `engine_recovery_timeout_sec=500`.

**Manual PD-disaggregated validation** — 2P2D behind a proxy, KV transfer over
NIXL + Mooncake Store; each tier a separate DP=2 × TP=2 deployment (EP world 4
per tier), `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`).

---

## Test Results

### Manual scale-down validation: PD co-location, TP=2

**PASSED.** Exercises the TP=2 single-worker-kill scenario end to end.

| Phase | Observation | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| Cluster ready | 4 ranks (DP=4 × TP=2, EP world 8) initialized, serving baseline traffic | 17:49:24 – 17:50:48 |
| Fault injected | One worker of DP rank 1 (TP1 sibling, EP rank 3) killed during active inference | 17:50:48 |
| First survivor-side error | Survivors' TP1 workers hit gloo `Connection reset by peer` on the per-TP-rank DP group | 17:50:48 |
| Victim DEAD | Engine 1's executor shut down its remaining worker; busy loop cancelled → status DEAD; its API server stays up and keeps answering `/v1/fault_tolerance/status` | 17:50:57 |
| Survivors UNHEALTHY | Engines 0/2/3 raise from the nixl_ep kernel timeout with mask `[0,0,1,1,0,0,0,0]` (EP ranks 2,3 = DP rank 1, both TP workers) | 17:51:18 |
| scale_down dispatched | `POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply` `removed_dp_ranks=[1]` → 202 on R0/R2/R3 | ~17:51:44 |
| Expert redistribution | 257 (layer, expert) pairs reloaded from disk per worker (652–733 tensors); `num_dispatchers` synced to `active_rank_bound=8` | 17:51:45 |
| Scale-down complete | Gloo DP group rebuilt 4→3 (dense group ranks R0→0, R2→1, R3→2; original `data_parallel_rank` frozen); engines 0/2/3 → HEALTHY, `cumulative dead_dp_ranks=[1]` | 17:51:45 |
| Post-recovery inference | All 3 survivors resume serving `/v1/chat/completions` with HTTP 200 | 17:51:45 – 17:52:07 |

Key observations:

- Recovery itself (mask replay + redistribution + weight reload + group reinit)
  completes in ~1s once dispatched; end-to-end latency is dominated by fault
  detection — immediate for the TP1 siblings via gloo connection-reset, ~30s for
  the surviving engines via the nixl_ep kernel timeout.
- No hangs and no orphaned TP collectives: the TP sibling lockstep barrier keeps
  survivor device streams clean.

### Manual scale-down validation: PD-disaggregated + TP=2

**PASSED.** Same scenario in a prefill/decode-disaggregated deployment (2P2D)
with KV transfer over NIXL + Mooncake Store.

| Phase | Observation | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| Cluster ready | 2P + 2D instances up (each DP=2 × TP=2, EP world 4), baseline requests served through the proxy | 14:15:48 – 14:16:55 |
| Fault injected | One worker of the decode tier's DP rank 1 (TP0 sibling, EP rank 2) killed during active decode (1 in-flight request on the victim) | 14:19:31 |
| Survivor detects fault | Surviving decode instance's workers (both TP ranks) raise gloo `Connection closed by peer` on the per-TP-rank DP group; engine → UNHEALTHY | 14:19:31 – 14:19:40 |
| Victim DEAD | Victim engine's executor shuts down its remaining worker; engine → DEAD; its in-flight request is lost with the instance | 14:19:36 – 14:19:40 |
| Mooncake cleanup | Master expires the dead instance's clients and unmounts its segments (clients 8 → 6) | 14:19:41 |
| scale_down dispatched | `POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply` `removed_dp_ranks=[1]` → 202 on the surviving decode instance | 14:20:09 |
| Scale-down complete | Dead EP ranks [2, 3] masked at the nixl_ep kernel; `num_dispatchers` synced to `active_rank_bound=2`; 0 expert reassignments needed (64 redundant experts = a full second replica of every logical expert, so no weight reload); Gloo DP group rebuilt 2→1; engine → HEALTHY, `cumulative dead_dp_ranks=[1]` | 14:20:10 |
| Post-recovery inference | New requests through the proxy flow prefill → surviving decode instance (NIXL P2P + Mooncake lookup), `/v1/completions` returns 200, steady decode ~30 tok/s | 14:20:25 – 14:20:45 |

Key observations:

- The prefill tier (a separate DP group) is untouched by the decode-tier fault
  and keeps serving throughout.
- Fault detection is immediate (gloo connection reset on the DP group, including
  during a dummy batch on the idle surviving engine); recovery itself completes
  in ~1s once dispatched.
- With `num_redundant_experts` equal to the logical expert count, scale-down
  needs no expert reassignment or weight reload — every logical expert keeps a
  live replica.

### E2E pytest

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_fault_tolerance_e2e.py -v -s
```

<!-- TODO: paste CI result once the fault-tolerance e2e step runs -->

---

- **AI assistance**: this change was developed with AI assistance; every changed
  line was reviewed by the human submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Fix %% rendering in CLI reference for --safetensors-load-strategy
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

While exploring the [`--safetensors-load-strategy`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/configuration/engine_args/#-safetensors-load-strategy) feature, I noticed the CLI reference docs showed `90%%%%` instead of `90%`.

## Root cause

`arg_utils.py` unconditionally escaped `%` → `%%` in all docstring-derived help text for argparse. This is correct for terminal `--help` because argparse's `_expand_help` does `help % params`, collapsing `%%` → `%`. But `MarkdownFormatter.add_arguments` in the docs generator reads `action.help` directly, bypassing `_expand_help`, so `%%` was never unescaped before writing to markdown.

Additionally, the `load.py` docstring had `90%%` instead of `90%` (manually pre-escaped to compensate for the old unconditional escaping), causing a double-escape to `90%%%%` in the rendered output.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/load.py`: `90%%` → `90%` in docstring (source must be plain `%` with the new approach)
- `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`: extract `IS_ARGPARSE` and guard the `%` → `%%` escaping with `if IS_ARGPARSE:`, so escaping only runs on the terminal `--help` path, not when building docs

## Verification

Served docs locally with `API_AUTONAV_EXCLUDE=vllm mkdocs serve` and confirmed:

```
None (default): Uses memory-mapped (lazy) loading. When an NFS filesystem is
detected and the total checkpoint size fits within 90% of available RAM,
prefetching is enabled automatically.
```

Also confirmed `vllm serve --help` still renders `90%` correctly (argparse `_expand_help` collapses `%%` → `%` as before).

## Known limitation

[`--bin-by`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/cli/bench/sweep/plot/#-bin-by) in `sweep/plot.py` hardcodes `%%1` directly in `add_argument(help=...)`, bypassing `arg_utils.py` entirely, so `IS_ARGPARSE` has no effect there — the docs still render `%%1`. Fixing it cleanly requires refactoring `SweepPlotArgs` to use docstrings like other config classes; leaving as a follow-up.

## Notes

- No existing open PR addresses this (searched for `safetensors`, `generate_argparse`, `%%`)
- AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and implement this fix

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Fix Case 4 math rendering in hybrid KV cache manager
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the two Case 4 equations in the Hybrid KV Cache Manager design document that render as literal LaTeX on the published documentation site. Resolves #64178.

## Background and fix status

Issue #64178 records that the published Case 4 equations appear as literal LaTeX. The underlying `main` Markdown lacks blank lines around display math inside numbered list items; the full MkDocs build reproduces raw `$$` in the generated HTML. This PR proposes the four-line spacing fix. It is open for review and has not been merged or deployed.

### Before and after screenshots

**Before — published documentation page:**

![Before fix: Case 4 displays literal LaTeX instead of equations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hechengkai/vllm/3b5d25d2a07dbbb04da5a071441fb0cb158d8357/issue-evidence/64178/published-case4-before.png)

**After — local MkDocs preview of this PR (not yet merged or deployed):**

![After fix: Case 4 equations render as display math](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hechengkai/vllm/9634757d652a9c6f5b0f667a5eefc70a0fd31aaa/issue-evidence/64178/local-case4-after.png)

## Claims

- Add the blank lines required for Arithmatex to parse display math inside numbered list items.
- Preserve the existing equations and the display-math style used elsewhere in this document.
- This does not duplicate #63717 or #63728: those PRs modify other equations in the same file, while this PR changes only Case 4.

## Validation

- Base: `6376fda7a95904abf8977011af526c693c4c3004` (`main`).
- `API_AUTONAV_EXCLUDE=vllm PYTHONUTF8=1 python -m mkdocs build --clean`: completed before and after the change using the repository's pinned docs dependencies.
- In the generated Case 4 HTML, Arithmatex nodes changed from 1 to 3 and literal `$$` delimiters changed from 4 to 0. The malformed `<em>` tag disappeared.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pre-commit run markdownlint-cli2 --files docs/design/hybrid_kv_cache_manager.md`: passed.
- Browser automation could not inspect localhost due to its URL security policy. The human submitter reviewed the four-line diff and confirmed the local document change before submission.
- The full pre-commit hook could not complete in the Windows environment while initializing unrelated hook environments; the targeted Markdown lint and full docs build above completed.

## Details

Arithmatex requires block math to be separated by empty lines. In Case 4, the opening `$$` followed the numbered-list text immediately, so Markdown emitted raw delimiters and interpreted underscores in the first equation as emphasis. Adding blank lines before and after the two display-math blocks makes them parse like other block equations in the same document. No formula content or vLLM runtime code changes.

AI assistance was used to investigate the Markdown rendering, prepare the four-line change, and run the documentation builds. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and validated the rendered page before submission.

commits.pr_title: [Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Speculator config classes and custom speculators
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Lets users plug their own speculator into Model Runner V2. Each speculator now has a declarative config class that describes its behavior, replacing the speculative-method name checks spread across config, scheduler, KV cache and model code.

## Claims

- **Custom V2 speculators.** A plugin registers a method name with `register_speculative_method(name, config_cls)`, typically from a vLLM general plugin, and users select it with `method="<name>"`. The implementation is a `BaseSpeculator` subclass, usually via `DraftModelSpeculator` or `TargetDependentARSpeculator`. A config that subclasses a built-in one (e.g. `Eagle3SpeculatorConfig`) inherits that speculator's draft-model setup and behavior. Custom methods require MRV2. A custom speculator can take its own options via `speculator_options`.
- **Declarative speculator configs.** Each V2 speculator has a `SpeculatorConfig` subclass in an import-light `config.py` next to it. The class declares traits such as `uses_target_hidden_states`, `uses_aux_hidden_states`, `num_lookahead_tokens`, `max_model_len`, `supports_watermarking` and `supports_pcp`, and names its implementation class. Callers query `speculative_config.speculator_config` (or shortcut properties for the most widely used traits) instead of comparing method names. The scheduler process never imports a speculator implementation.
- **Per-method setup moves out of `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`.** It goes into the config classes: `default_model`, `configure`, draft-checkpoint hooks (`adapt_draft_model_config`, `resolve_num_speculative_tokens`), and `apply_options` for method-specific options. Each config lists the method-specific options it accepts in `supported_options`, and passing another one fails at startup.
- **Draft models declare their speculator.** A draft model sets `speculator_config_class` to its speculator's config class (new `SpeculativeDraftModel` interface, exposed through the model registry by qualified name). This replaces the hardcoded draft-architecture lists used to select DFlash2, LiLiCorr, XPress, DSpark and Gemma4 MTP.
- **Checkpoint detection never overrides an explicitly configured method.** For example, an explicit `mtp` could previously be rewritten to `eagle` by the draft checkpoint's name. An explicit method is now checked against the speculator the draft model declares, if any, and a mismatch fails with an explanatory error. This incorporates the intent of #41834 / #47490.
- `BaseSpeculator` now provides defaults for the members the runner reads (`supports_mm_inputs`, `draft_logits`, `prepare_watermarking()`), so speculators, custom ones included, only define what they use.

## Validation

Unit tests run on the NVIDIA GCP cluster (GB200), on this branch with current main merged in:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode` (excluding the slow e2e/acceptance tests), `tests/test_config.py`, `tests/config`, `tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py`, `tests/models/test_registry.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, workspace / EAGLE3 aux-hidden-state / PP embedding-sharing worker tests | 2125 passed, 1 failed (gated `meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout` download, unrelated) |
| Tests that fake the speculative config: KV offload scheduler, Kimi K3 KDA metadata, fused shared expert, DSpark MLA, DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP, MRV2 model runner | 659 passed |
| e2e `draft_model/test_async.py::test_no_sync_with_spec_decode[eagle-mla-deepseek]` | passed |

Each draft model module that declares a speculator, and each speculator config module, was also imported in a fresh process to check for import cycles.

New tests are in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py`. They cover:
- registration, validation and V2-only enforcement;
- `init_speculator` construction;
- the import-light check for all speculator config modules;
- checkpoint resolution, explicit-method mismatch errors, and selection via draft model declarations.

Not yet done: an end-to-end run of a custom speculator plugin, and e2e spec-decode acceptance runs (EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash/DSpark) to confirm there are no behavior changes.

## Details

- **Line count.** About +1430/−750 non-test lines. Much of this moves existing per-method logic out of `speculative.py` (which shrinks substantially) into per-speculator config modules.
- **V1 runner.** `SpeculativeConfig` is shared with the V1 runner, so V1-only pieces are grouped in `v1_speculator_configs.py` (suffix, V1 `custom_class` proposers) or marked "V1 model runner only", to be deleted along with V1. The V1 `custom_class` proposer interface is unchanged on V1 and still rejected by V2. V1-only checks (e.g. P-EAGLE `parallel_drafting`, heterogeneous vocab) stay as method checks rather than declared traits, and `parallel_drafting` is now documented as deprecated.
- **`base_method`.** `method` keeps the registered custom name, for logging, usage stats and the config hash. `SpeculativeConfig.base_method` gives the built-in method a custom config is based on, and is what the `use_*` predicates and model-specific checks consult.
- **Behavior-preserving trait moves.** Upstream logic is kept but expressed as traits:
  - the draft max-model-len cap from #63251 (`SpeculatorConfig.max_model_len`);
  - DSpark's separate workspace lane (`uses_separate_workspace_lane`);
  - target input-embedding sharing under PP, now inferred from the draft model class;
  - the draft-pass `max_num_active_seqs` limit (`max_num_draft_seqs`).
- **Speculators-format checkpoints.** The speculators override no longer replaces a custom method that is based on the checkpoint's method. It rejects one that's based on a different method.
- **Docs.** See "Custom Speculators (Experimental)" in `docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md`.
- **Reviewing.** The branch has accumulated review and merge commits, so it's best reviewed as a whole diff.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][DSpark] Batch-sharded sequential block
commits.pr_body:
## Context

Under batch-sharded sampling, #64356 shards verification and the draft logits cache by batch position: request `i` is owned by rank `i % tp_size`. The DSpark sequential (Markov) block still runs replicated, though. Every rank computes full-vocab draft logits and samples every request at every draft step, even though each rank only keeps the draft logits of the requests it owns.

## This PR

This PR shards the DSpark sequential block along the same ownership rule, so each rank runs the Markov loop only for its own requests.

**`DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential_sharded`.** Each rank owns at most `capacity = cdiv(num_reqs, tp_size)` requests, so every shape depends only on `num_reqs` and the step is captured in the existing draft CUDA graphs. No second graph set is needed. Each step:
1. Each rank computes its vocab shard of the base draft logits (`compute_draft_logits_local`) for every request, in owner-major order. Padding slots read request 0's rows and are discarded.
2. An all-to-all re-shards the logits from the vocab dimension to the batch dimension, so each rank holds full-vocab logits for its own requests.
3. The Markov loop (`_sample_markov_chain`, now shared with the replicated path) samples those rows and writes the owner's draft logits rows. Padding lanes pass `-1` and write nothing.
4. An all-gather of the drafts (plus the confidences, under adaptive verification) restores batch order on every rank.

**Single NCCL communicator.**
- `PyNcclCommunicator.all_to_all_single` (new) does a variable-split all-to-all, and is graph-capturable when the split sizes are fixed.
- Verification's logits exchange now goes through the same TP PyNCCL communicator, via `all_to_all_vocab_shards` (which replaces `all_to_all_logits`) and `get_tp_pynccl_comm()`.
- A separate c10d all-to-all would make NCCL allocate a second set of point-to-point buffers, about 1.1 GiB per GPU on GB200.
- The c10d path remains as a fallback when PyNCCL is unavailable.

**When the loop stays replicated.** It logs the reason and runs replicated when:
- the draft logits cache is replicated (PCP, a draft watermarker, or a draft model whose fused `sample_sequential` writes the full cache);
- the online acceptance estimator is used;
- top-k Markov sampling is configured;
- the draft model lacks a vocab-sharded `compute_draft_logits_local`;
- PyNCCL is unavailable.

**Models.** `compute_draft_logits_local` is added for DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 DSpark (NVIDIA) and Qwen3 DSpark.

## Benchmarks

**Setup:**
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, K=5, probabilistic drafting.
- 4× GB200, TP4, `max_num_seqs=256`, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching off, natural EOS.
- Arms: **main** (55b677b2d1, loop replicated) vs **this PR** (loop sharded). Both use `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, so the comparison isolates the sharded loop.
- 4 boots, ordered PR, main, main, PR.
- SPEED-Bench `low_entropy`, `throughput_2k`, temperature 1. GSM8K: 1319 questions, temperatures 0 and 1.
- Latencies are medians.

### Speed (this PR vs main)

| | c1 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 | c128 | c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITL, AV off | +1.0% | −0.1% | −0.4% | −0.6% | −0.7% | −1.5% | **−2.6%** |
| tok/s, AV off | +1.6% | −0.4% | +1.5% | +2.4% | −0.4% | +4.3% | **+5.4%** |
| ITL, AV on | +1.9% | +0.7% | −0.6% | −0.4% | −0.9% | −2.2% | −1.4% |
| tok/s, AV on | +0.4% | +1.3% | +2.7% | +2.4% | +3.2% | +2.3% | +1.7% |

With AV off, ITL at c256 goes from 48.43 to 47.16 ms; the two boots of each arm agree within about 0.05 ms. Throughput and the AV-on runs are noisier. At c1 the extra collectives cost about 1%. A minimum batch size for the sharded loop (no extra CUDA graphs needed) could remove that cost as a follow-up.

### Accuracy and acceptance (main → this PR)

| | GSM8K t0 | GSM8K t1 | Acceptance length c64 | Acceptance length c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AV off | 0.898 → 0.901 | 0.800 → 0.797 | 3.54 → 3.54 | 3.54 → 3.54 |
| AV on | 0.898 → 0.910 | 0.809 → 0.810 | 3.28 → 3.27 | 3.35 → 3.36 |

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py  # 59 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pynccl.py  # 17 passed, incl. the new test_pynccl_all_to_all_single
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py  # 92 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py  # 2 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py  # 12 passed
```

`test_pynccl_all_to_all_single` covers uneven and zero-row splits, plus CUDA graph replay. `test_dspark_sharded_sampling_equivalence` (new) runs Qwen3-4B-FP8 + DSpark at TP2. It checks that the draft logits cache and the loop are sharded only when the flag is on, and that greedy and seeded outputs match replicated sampling up to near-tie noise. The general e2e test covers verification's all-to-all, which now runs on PyNCCL.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DI][CI]  Add DeepSeek-V3 NIXL accuracy steps
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add DeepSeek-V3 disaggregated prefill/decode accuracy steps that use NIXL over UCX RDMA on MI350, next to the existing MoRIIO steps. Read uses `NixlConnector`. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8, and 2P2D EP16.

The 2P2D EP16 write step needs https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62055. That change keeps push heartbeats and outgoing WRITE polling on the writer thread, so a blocked NIXL call cannot miss an expert-parallel collective.

## Changes

- `pipeline-disagg.yaml`: six DeepSeek-V3 steps. Read (`NixlConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, 2P2D EP16/DP16. Write (`NixlPushConnector`): 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8/DP8, and 2P2D EP16/DP16.
- `run-slurm-disagg-test.sh`, `run_xPyD_disagg.slurm`: add `KV_CONNECTOR` (default `MoRIIOConnector`) and pass it to the containers. For NIXL, start vllm-router with `--kv-connector nixl` and fixed `--prefill`/`--decode` URLs, because NIXL has no discovery service.
- `vllm_disagg.sh`: when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`, use that name in the NIXL KV transfer config (UCX backend). On 2P2D EP16 prefill, set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. At 0.85 the AITER MoE sort buffer runs out of memory. EP8 stays at 0.85.
- `cluster.sh`: for either NIXL connector, set UCX defaults for the ionic RoCE NICs (RC verbs on `ionic_0`, GPU-direct RDMA) and run accuracy with one concurrent request. The router flag stays `--kv-connector nixl` for both.

MoRIIO steps do not change. All new settings apply only when `KV_CONNECTOR` is `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector`.

Requirement: the image's UCX must support `rc_verbs` on ionic NICs that report `max_srq=0`. The results below used UCX 1.22 with that support. The 2P2D EP16 write result also used the writer-thread ownership from #62055.

## Test plan

UCX environment (the same on every node):

```bash
export UCX_TLS=rc_verbs,ud_verbs,tcp,self,rocm
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=ionic_0:1,lo
export UCX_IB_GID_INDEX=1
export UCX_UD_VERBS_ETH_DGID_CHECK=n
export UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=yes
export UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y
export UCX_PROTO_EMULATION_ENABLE=n
export UCX_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL=inf
export UCX_UD_VERBS_RX_QUEUE_LEN=1024
export UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024
```

KV config (`kv_role` is `kv_producer` on prefill and `kv_consumer` on decode):

```bash
KV='{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX"],"kv_lease_duration":180}}'
```

Write uses the same commands with `"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector"`.

TP8, prefill (port 8100) and decode (port 8200, `kv_consumer`):

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --host $PREFILL_IP --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, prefill:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $PREFILL_IP --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, decode: the same command with `--data-parallel-address $DECODE_IP`, `--all2all-backend mori_low_latency`, no `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`, and `kv_consumer`.

2P2D EP16/DP16 uses the same EP command with `--data-parallel-size 16` on four nodes. Prefill uses `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`. The second prefill node and the second decode node join headless with `--data-parallel-start-rank 8`. The router points only at the two masters. Write uses `NixlPushConnector` and the #62055 writer.

Router (`--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` for TP8, `8` for EP8 and EP16):

```bash
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector nixl \
  --prefill http://$PREFILL_IP:8100 --decode http://$DECODE_IP:8200 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 1800 --port 30000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --intra-node-data-parallel-size 1 --policy round_robin \
  --prefill-policy round_robin --decode-policy round_robin
```

For 2P2D EP16 the router uses `--worker-startup-timeout-secs 7200` and `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 8`.

Accuracy:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```

Script checks: `bash -n` on all changed scripts, YAML parse, NIXL KV config parses as JSON, router arguments checked for 1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8 and 2P2D EP16, `git diff --check`.

## Results

GSM8K (5-shot) exact_match. KV moved GPU memory to GPU memory over `rc_verbs/ionic_0`.

| Config | Connector | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D TP8 | NixlConnector | 0.92 | 0.92 |
| 1P1D EP8/DP8 | NixlConnector | 0.94 | 0.94 |
